lawyer:
For the Appellant: Mr. Shafique Ahmed Senior. Advocate, instructed by Mrs. Sulfa Khatun, Advocate-on-Record 
For the Respondent: A.K.M. Shahidul Huq, Advocate-on-Record.
parties:
Md. Farhat Rahman  ------ Appellant.
Versus
Roomee Tareque Moudud ------ Respondent.
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Ruhul Amin, j:- This is a defendant's appeal, by leave, against the judgment of January 18, 2000 of the High Court Division as to an order of discharge of the Rule for default obtained in Civil Revision No.4256 of 1999 which was filed against the judgment and order .dated November 14, 1999 of the Court of Nari-o-shishu Nirjatan Daman Bishesh Adalat, Dhaka (hereinafter in brief the Adalat) in Family court Appeal .N0.56 of 1997 allowing the appeal upon reversing the judgment and 'order dated July 30, 1997 of the Family Court and the 4th Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka, in Family Court Suit No.8 of 1995 dismissing the same on contest 

2. The suit was filed seeking custody of the minor child by his father. 

3. The plaintiff, father of the minor filed the: suit stating, inter alia, that he married the defendant (the appellant herein) on  14.2.1991  and a- son was born on 27:10.1991, that his wife used to quarrel with him over trivial domestic .matters, that the defendant left the house of the plaintiff in the last week of January,1993 taking the minor child with her and went to her father's house, that the plaintiff divorced the defendant on 22:5.1993 that the Arbitration Council tried to effect a compromise between the plaintiff and the defendant but the same being not fruitful, the divorce took place in terms of compromise to the effect that plaintiff would pay Tk.3,000/- to the defendant for the maintenance of the minor child and that Arbitration Council also made the award that the plaintiff would. be allowed to meet his minor son once in a week, that for the last six months inspite of the award of the Arbitration Council plaintiff was not allowed to meet his son, that defendant being emotionally   unbalanced and indifferent and as such negligent towards the physical and mental welfare of the minor on of the plaintiff and hence the minor should be given to the care and custody of the plaintiff for his welfare.  

4. The suit was contested by the defendant. The case of the defendant amongst others was that her minor son will never get love, care and affection in the congenial and. healthy atmosphere in the house of the plaintiff since the plaintiff is a low paid private service holder and. unable to pay for the daily needs of the minor child and as such plaintiffs claim for the custody of the minor child merits no consideration. 
 
5. The Family Court dismissed the suit upon holding that if the minor is taken away from the custody of the mother, the defendant and given to the custody of the plaintiff the father and his parents the minor would not be able to adjust with them and that he will feel helpless for want of mother and that the minor would not get love and affection from his step mother. The Family Court allowed the plaintiff to meet the minor on three occasions in each two months and on other special clays at the residence of Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiya, the learned Advocate of the defendant. 

6. The father went on appeal and the appellate Court set aside the judgment of the Family Court and the defendant was directed to give the minor to the custody of the father. Thereupon the defendant, herein the appellant, moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained the Rule. It appears that revisional application was filed without furnishing decrees of the trial Court as well as of the appellate Court and in that background while issuing the Rule on 21.11.1999 the High Court Division directed the petitioner "to file the decrees of both the Courts below within 2(two) weeks from date in the section, in default, the Rule shall stand discharged". 

7. The petitioner before the High Court Division applied for the certified copy of the decrees of the trial Court as well as of the appellate Court and obtained the certified copy of the decree of the appellate Court but could not obtain the decree of the Trial Court since no decree in Family Court Suit No.8 of 1995 was drawn. In due course the petitioner (in the civil Rule) filed the certified copy of the decree or the appellate Court in the office on 5.12.1999 and for exempting him from filing the decree of the trial Court he filed a petition on 6.12.1999. 

8. The application so filed was listed for hearing on 4.1.2000 and on the prayer of the petitioner the hearing of the application was adjourned for two weeks and thereafter the application was listed for hearing on 18.1.2000. On the said date the High Court Division rejected the application and discharged the Rule upon observing that petitioner was required to file the decrees of the courts below by 5.12.1999 but the petitioner filed the application on 6.12.1999 with the prayer for exempting him from filing the decree of the trial Court and that as the application has been tiled beyond the period fixed by the Court for filing the decrees of the courts below and that decree of the court below ile. trial Court, having not been filed within the time fixed by the Court the Rule stood discharged since the order of the Court was of the kind which was to take effect automatically in case of default to comply with the order of the Court and that as the order of the Court has not been complied with by 5.12.1999 the application filed on 6.12.1999 for dispensing with the filing of the decree of the trial Court cannot be considered since the Court has become functus officio after 5.12.1999. 

9. Leave was granted to consider the contention that Family court having not drawn up the decree and consequent thereupon as it was not possible to comply with the direction for filing the certified copy of the decree of the trial Court within the time allowed by the Court although with the default clause "the Rule shall stand discharged" and as such the High Court Division was in error in discharging the Rule without passing an order dispensing with the furnishing of the certified copy of the decree of the trial Court.

10. The appellant, who was the defendant in the Family Court, obtained the Rule as against the order of the appellate Court decreeing the suit filed by the Respondent. As it is seen that the revisional application was filed without furnishing the decree of the courts below. The High Court Division while issuing the Rule directed the defendant-petitioner herein 'appellant, to furnish the certified copy of the decrees of the courts below within two weeks from the date of issuance of the Rule i.e. 21.11.1990 and that in case of default "the Rule shall stand discharged".

11. The appellant, as seen from the judgment of the High Court Division, furnished the certified copy of the decree of the appellate Court on 5.12.1999 and tiled an application on 6.12.1999 seeking exemption from filing the certified copy of the decree of the trial Court stating that he filed petition for obtaining the certified copy of the decree of the trial Court but the office had told him that no decree was drawn in Family Suit No.8 of 1995. The statement so made was not disputed by the Respondent. 

12. The learned Advocate-on-record, who appeared in the appeal with the permission of the Court since concise statement was not filed by the Respondent, did not place any material before this Division to show that the statement made in the petition seeking exemption from filing the certified copy of the decree of the trial Court by the petitioner before the High Court Division in his application dated 6.12.1999 was not correct. 

13. The High Court Division instead of disposing of the Rule on merit discharged the same only on the ground the appellant, petitioner before the High Court Division was required to comply with the order of the said Division directing him to furnish certified copy of the decrees of the courts below within the time specified i.e. by 5.12.1999, but he complied with the part of 4 the order of the High Court Division by filing certified copy of the decree of the appellate Court on 5.12.1999 and thereby defaulted in the compliance of the order of the High Court Division passed at the time of issuance of the Rule. The High Court Division discharged the Rule for default on the view that because of the expression used in the order of the High Court Division the same was final one and that on the expiry of the stipulated time the High Court Division had no power to consider the application filed on 6.12.1999 stating the fact in the background whereof the appellant was unable to comply with the order of the High Court Division. 

14. The learned Counsel for the appellant has submitted that there was no an ache or negligence on the part of the appellant to comply with the order of the High Court Division i.e. furnishing the certified copy of the decrees of the courts below but because of the undenied and undisputed fact which was beyond the control of the appellant. he could not comply with the order of the High Court Division in entirety but complied with partially and that in the background of the fact brought on record by the appellant for his failure to comply with the order of the High Court Division within the time specified, the said Division in consideration of the said fact was required to consider the prayer of the appellant and that ought to have exempted him from filing the certified copy of the decree of the trial Court. The learned Counsel for the appellant also submits that the appellant has been penalized for no fault of him since he approached the trial Court for furnishing him the certified copy of the decree but the said Court told him that the decree in a suit like the one wherein the appellant was a defendant decree was not drawn. As we have mentioned earlier, that this statement of fact made by the appellant on oath was not disputed from the side of the Respondent. In the background of the facts brought on record by the appellant we are of the view that High Court Division was not without power to consider the prayer of the petitioner in the civil revision for exempting him from filing the certified copy of the decree of the trial Court. 

15. In our opinion in the background of the statement made by the appellant explaining the reason or ground for his non-furnishing the certified copy of the decree of the trial Court the High Court Division would have been within its jurisdiction to consider the prayer for exempting him from furnishing the certified copy of the decree of trial Court and could have very much exercise its power for the purpose of advancing the cause of justice by allowing the prayer for exempting the appellant from filing the certified copy of the decree of the Trial Court. It is seen from the material on record that the High Court Division discharged the Rule not on merit but for default in the compliance with the order of the High Court Division which was passed at the time of issuance of the Rule on 21.11.1999. 

16. In the background of the facts and circumstances of the case as well as for the sake of advancing the cause of justice this Division should exercise its power of doing complete justice in the matter by sending the civil revision back to the High Court Division for disposal on merit without the decree of the trial Court or in other words with decree of the appellate Court alone which has already been filed by the appellant. 

17. In the light of our discussions made hereinabove and the view expressed by us we are of the view that the civil revision needs be disposed of on merit by the High Court Division. 

18. Accordingly the appeal is allowed. 

19. The order of the High Court Division dated January 18, 2000 in Civil Revision No.42564of 1999 discharging the Rule for default is set aside and the Civil Revision No.4256 of 1999 is sent back to the High Court Division for disposal on merit. 

20. The custody of the child shall remain with his mother till disposal of the Rule. There is no order as to costs. 

	End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave To Appeal No. 431 of 2000.
lawyer:
For the Petitioner: Md. Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record. 
Respondents : Not represented.
parties:
Mrs. Nazma Begum ----- Petitioner
Versus
Mrs. Arzuda Khatun and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Mainur Reza Chowdhury, J: The defendant-petitioner seeks leave to appeal against judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in civil Revision No. 549 of 1999 discharging the Rule and thereby affirming the order dated 12.11.1998 amending the decree passed by the Subordinate Judge, Commercial Court No. 2 Dhaka in Title Suit No. 16 of 1992 

2. The plaintiffs-respondent No.1 Mrs. Arzuda Khatun instituted the above title suit against the defendant-petitioner Mrs. Nazma Begum and others for a declaration of her title and recovery of khas possession of the suit property. The plaintiffs case was that she took lease from of the property from erstwhile Government of East Pakistan by a lease deed no. 6327 dated 05.10.1968 and since then she was possessing the same. During the war of liberation she had to leave her house on the suit land leaving her deeds etc. there in order to save her life and on return after liberation found that the defendant-petitioner had illegally entered into the possession of the same. She failed in her attempts to get back the possession of the said property and therefore constrained to bring the above suit for declaration of her title and recovery of khas possession. 

3. The defendant-petitioner also instituted Title Suit No. 17 of 1992 for specific performance of contract against the defendant-petitioner No. 1 and others. Her contention was that respondent No. 2 who was in possession of the suit property, abandoned the same during liberation movement of Bangladesh whereupon she entered into the property and continued to occupy and enjoy the same openly in her own rights and in 1979 the respondent No.2 a legally constituted attorney of respondent No. 1 Mrs. Arzuda Khatun came back and demanded possession of the suit property from the defendant-petitioner and ultimately entered into a contract to sell the same to her for consideration of Tk. 25,000/- and executed 
deed of agreement on receipt of Tk. 24,000/- as earnest money on behalf of respondent No. 1 and thereafter refused to execute and register sale deed in respect of the property. Both the suits were in respect of the self-same property. 

4. The learned Subordinate Judge tried both the suits analogously on framing the issues including the question of title and possession of the plaintiff respondent in Title Suit No. 16 of 1992 in the suit land. After considering the oral and documentary evidence in support of the respective contentions, the learned Subordinate Judge after discussing the evidence adduced by the parties and attending facts and circumstances of the case came to the conclusion that the alleged power of attorney (Am-Moktarnama) and the deed of agreement in favour of the defendant-petitioner were forged and fabricated and no agreement as alleged was ever entered upon and therefore dismissed the said Title Suit No. 17 of 1992 filed by the defendant-petitioner for specific performance of contract. On the other hand the learned Subordinate Judge after discussing the material evidence on record and considering the fact and circumstances of the case came to the conclusion that the plaintiff-respondent No. 1 in Title Suit No. 16 of 1992 had succeeded in proving her case and decreed the said suit. The learned Subordinate Judge mentioned following in the body of the judgment : " এমতাবস্থায় ৩-৬ নং বিচার্য্ বিষয়গুলো দে: ১৬/৯২ নং মামলার বাদীনি আরজুদা খাতুনের পক্ষে গৃহিত হইল এবং দে: ১৭/৯২ নং মামলার বাদিনী নাজমা বেগমের বিরুদ্ধে গৃহিত হইল। 
 But in the ordering portion he declared "অত্র দে: ১৬/৯২ নং মোকদ্দমাটি দোতরফা সূত্রে ১নং বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে এবং অন্যান্য বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে এক তরফা সুত্রে বিনা খরচায় ডিক্রি প্রদান করা হইল এবং না: জমিতে বাদিনীর স্বত্ত্ব ঘোষিত হইল। পক্ষান্তরে দে: ১৭/৯২ নং মোকদ্দমাটি দোতরফা সুত্রে ১নং বিবাদীর বিরদ্ধে এবং অন্যান্য বিবাদীর বিরদ্ধে এক তরফা সুত্রে বিনা খরচায় ডিসমিস করা হইল। 

5. The learned Subordinate Judge passed the judgment on 27.09.1998 where after the decree .was prepared and signed on 06.10.1998. The decree was drawn in accordance with the ordering portion of the judgment i.e. in the decree plaintiff's title was declared and nothing was said about the prayer for recovery of khas possession. The plaintiff-respondent No.1 Arzuda Khatun on 08.11.1998 filed an application before the learned Subordinate Judge praying for amendment of the judgment and decree incorporating the relief of khas possession in her favour and the learned Subordinate Judge by his order dated 12.11.1998 allowed the prayer for amendment of the judgment and decree and accordingly the judgment and the decree were amended. 

6. Before the High Court Division it was submitted that there was a distinction between clerical or arithmetical mistake in the judgment and decree of the order and judicial mistake crept therein. It was submitted that the mistake corrected by the learned Subordinate Judge did not fall within the admit of a clerical or arithmetical mistake or accidental slip or omission and therefore mistakes corrected by the learned Subordinate Judge was not covered by section 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It was also submitted that the learned Subordinate Judge also committed an illegality in passing the impugned order without serving any notice upon the petitioner. 

7. The High Court Division considered the submission with reference to a decision in the case reported in AIR 1992 (Punjab) 110 that a "clerical error" is one made in transcribing or otherwise, and it must be apparent on the face of the record and therefore capable of corrected. It is in the nature of an inadvertent omission or mistake. The term clerical error was distinguishable from "judicial error" which can be corrected only on review or an appeal as held in the case reported in 39 CWN page 1295. It was held that the court which passed a decree can amended two cases only (I) when there is a clerical or arithmetical mistake or slip and (II) where the court itself finds that the decree does not correctly represent that was decided or intended to be decided, provided the amendment can be made without injustice. 

8. The High Court Division in the instant case found that it was apparent on the face of the record that the learned Subordinate Judge intended to decree in full the Title Suit No. 16 of 1992 and to dismiss in full the Title Suit No. 17 of 1992. It was also apparent on the face of the record from the ordering of portion of the judgment quoted above that it did not manifest the intention of the learned Subordinate Judge and also the decision he took in the body of the judgment. The Court also mentioned that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 16 of 1992 was admittedly out of possession from long before institution of the suit and as such there could be no question of passing the decree of declaration without any consequent relief in her favour. 

9. The High Court Division also correctly took into the submission made by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff respondent that the Court can correct any error or omission covered by section 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure even suo-motu and as such it was not obligatory upon the court to give notice upon the defendant petitioner before amendment of mistake or omission. These views find support in the decision reported in 22 DLR 130. A decree should be consistent with the plaint in the absence of an indication that particular relief has been refused. A matter in issue decided by the court must be included in the decree and if not included it may be corrected on an application of amendment of the decree. Every Court has an inherent power to very or amend its own decree or order so as to carry out its own meaning. In the instant case, the court having found in favour of the plaintiff-respondent as to the title in the suit land and the plaintiff was out of possession the decree would be of no use to the plaintiff unless the ordering portion of the judgment included an order for recovery of khas possession by the plaintiff. The High Court Division therefore discharged the Rule. 

10. No illegality or infirmity in the impugned order could be pointed out by the learned counsel for the petitioner which calls for interference by away of leave petition. 

11. The petition is therefore dismissed. 

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave To Appeal No.694 of 2001.
lawyer:
For the Petitioner: Mr. M. A. Azim Khair, Deputy Attorney General, instructed by Mr. B. Hossain, Advocate-on-Record. 
Respondent: Not represented.
parties:
Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Bagerhat ------ Petitioner
Versus
Sunil Kumar Khan ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Ruhul Amin, J: Delay is condoned. This petition for leave to appeal has been filed against the judgment and order of April 12, 1999 of a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.915 of 1997 making the Rule absolute which was obtained against the order No.48 dated November 12, 1996 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Bagerhat, passed in Miscellaneous Case No.45 of 1995 (registered upon an application filed under Order 9, Rule .13 of the Code of Civil Procedure) setting aside the ex-parte decree passed in Title Suit No.50 of 1993 on February 12, 1995.

2. Facts, in short are that plaintiff-Respondents filed Title Suit No.50 of 1993 seeking declaration of title in respect of the land in suit. In the said suit the plaintiffs impleaded the petitioner and the local tahsildar as the defendants. The suit was decreed ex-parte on February 12, 1995. The petitioner filed an application under Order 9, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure seeking setting aside of the ex-parte decree passed in Title Suit No.50 of 1993 and thereupon Miscellaneous Case No.45 of 1995 was registered. The petitioner sought for setting aside of the ex-parte decree on the ground that summonses were not duly served on the defendants.

3. Plaintiff-Respondents contested the Miscellaneous Case by filing written objection denying the material statements made in the application filed under Order 9, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and stating, inter alia, that the summonses were duly served upon the defendants and the Court being satisfied about the due service of summonses on the defendants decreed the suit ex-parte.

4. The trial Court upon hearing the parties allowed the Miscellaneous Case, in spite of failure on the part of the defendant-petitioners to establish that summonses were not served and on the date the suit was taken up for hearing they were prevented by sufficient cause from appearing before the Court; on the finding that for ends of justice the ex-parte decree needs to be set aside.

5. Thereupon the plaintiff-Respondents would moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction. The High Court Division set aside the impugned order of the lower Court on the findings that there  was no factual basis for the Court of Subordinate  Judge to place reliance on the submission made from the side of the defendant-petitioners in support of the prayer for  setting aside the ex-parte decree, that there. is total absence of finding that summonses were not served upon the defendants or the defendants were prevented by sufficient cause from appearing before the Court when the suit was taken up for hearing, that defendants did not make out any case in support of their contention that they were prevented by sufficient cause from appearing, before the Court when the suit was taken up for hearing. The High Court Division while setting aside the impugned order of the court' below has further observed "In the absence of any factual basis and any material on record, a Court of law cannot be expected to act on the unsubstantiated submissions made by the learned Advocate of an interested party", and that law is now settled that an ex-parte decree can be set aside only on specified grounds i.e. when 'the summons was not duly served and when the defendant was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing" but the court below did neither arrive at the finding that summons was not served, nor held that condition or conditions  in the presence of which an ex-parte decree can he set aside was established by the defendant-petitioners.

6. We have heard the learner Deputy Attorney General and perused the materials on record.

<u>7. In the background of the materials on record the learned Deputy Attorney General felt difficulty to assail the findings arrived at by the High Court Division while setting aside the order of the court below i.e. setting aside the ex-parte decree. In our opinion High Court Division has not committed any error in setting aside the order of the court below. It is seen from the order of the learned Subordinate Judge that tile defendant-petitioners in support of their case for setting aside the ex-parte decree totally failed to establish the summons was not served on the defendants or the defendants were prevented by Sufficient cause from appearing before the Court when the case, was take group for hearing. In that state of the Matter the learned Subordinate Judge was totally in error in setting aside the ex-parte decree and consequently the High Court Division has not committed any error or illegality in setting aside the erroneous order of the court below.</u>

<u>In the background of the discussions made herein above we find no substance in the petition. Accordingly the petition is dismissed.</u>

End.

lawyer:
Mr. M. Moqbul Hossain, Advocate, -- For the petitioner 
Mr. Md. Jamaluddin Ahmed, Advocate -- For the opposite party nos.1-2
parties:
Rashia ----- Petitioner
Versus
Most. Safia Begum and others ----- Opposite parties
full_judgment:
Mr. Syed Md. Ziaul Karim, J:- This Rule calls in question the legality and propriety of judgment and decree dated 29.06.2000 passed by learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Barguna, dismissing Title Appeal no.40 of 1995 and affirming those of dated 25.05.1995 passed by learned Assistant Judge, Amtali, Barguna Sadar, decreeing Title Suit no.147 of 1992 

2. Short facts leading to this Rule are that on 01.12.1992, opposite party nos.1-2 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit no.147 of 1992 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Amtali, Barguna Sadar, impleading petitioner and opposite party nos.3-57 as defendants for setting aside ex-parte judgment and decree dated 28.10.1991 passed by learned Assistant Judge, Amtali Barguna Sadar, in Title Suit no.4 of 1988 instituted by Abdul Khaleq as plaintiff against Hatem Ali and others as defendants for partition in respect of 9.35 acres of land out of 21.17 acres described in Schedule of plaint. 

3. The plaintiffs case put in a nutshell are that they are owners in possession in their land at this stage defendant nos. 1-19 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit no. 04 of 1988 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Amtali, for partition impleading plaintiffs as defendant nos.11 and 14 respectively and others. Summons of suit were not duly served upon them but the same were fraudulently shown to have been served by the relations of plaintiffs of Title Suit no. 04 of 1988. The present plaintiffs i.e. defendant nos. 11 and 14 of Title Suit no.04 of 1988 did not receive any summons by post even they had no knowledge about the suit and ex-parte decree dated 28.10.1991. On 25.08.1992 for the first time they came to know about such ex-parte decree passed in Title Suit no.04 of 1988 Hence the suit. 

4. The defendant no.15 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all materials allegations made in plaint contending interlaid that plaintiffs had full knowledge about Title Suit no.04 of 1988 as they had no title in the suit land so they willfully did not contest the suit. Just only to harass the defendants plaintiff instituted the instant suit. Thus the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

5. On the pleadings defferent issues were settled including issue of maintainability and issue whether plaintiffs are entitled to get a decree as prayed for. 

6. In course of trial plaintiffs examined three witnesses, of them P.W.1, Begum (Plaintiff no.2) who proved their title and possession in suit land and also proved that summons of Title Suit no.04 of 1988 were not duly served upon them. P.W.2 Md. Matiar Rahman, P.W.3 Motahar Hossain were examined to corroborate the evidence of P.W. I . They proved their documents which were exhibited and marked as exhibits 1-9. The defendants examined three witnesses, of 
them D.W.1 Rashia (defendant no.15), D.W.2 M.A. Rahim, Process Surveyor and D.W.3 Hafijuddin Munshi, they proved that notices were properly served. 

7. After hearing learned assistant Judge by judgment and decree dated 25.05.1995 decreed the suit and set aside exported decree passed in Title Suit no.04 of 1988. Against which defendant no.15 as appellant preferred Title Appeal no.40 of 1995 in the Court of District Judge, Barguna, which was ultimately heard by learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Barguna who by judgment and decree dated 29.06.2000 dismissed the appeal and affirmed those of trial Court. 

8. Feeling aggrieved defendant no. 15 as petitioner preferred the instant application and obtained the present Rule. 

9. Mr. M. Moqbul Hossain, learned Advocate appearing for petitioner candidly submits that finding of Courts below regarding non service of summons based on materials on record and Courts below concurrently held that summons were not properly served upon plaintiffs i.e. defendant nos.1 I and 14 of Title Suit no.04 of 1988. He lastly submits that there may be a direction to proceed with the suit. Mr. Jamaluddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for opposite party nos. 1-2 submits that he has no objection if Title Suit no.04 of 1988 be proceeded in accordance with law. 

10. In order to appreciate the submissions advanced by learned Counsels I have gone through revisional application, pleadings, all exhibits, other materials on record and given my anxious consideration to their submissions. 

11. Now the question calls for consideration whether Courts below committed any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing judgments and decrees. 

12. On going to the materials on record it transpires that plaintiffs instituted suit for setting aside exported judgment and decree dated 28.10.1991 passed in Title Suit no.04 of 1988 (exhbt.8). The plaintiffs claim that they were defendant nos.11 and 14 of Title Suit no.04 of 1988 but summons were not duly served upon them. The contesting defendants disowned such facts and claim that plaintiffs intentionally did not receive summons. 

13. It further transpires that Courts below concurrently held that summons were not duly served upon the plaintiffs. The learned Counsel for petitioner candidly submits that there is no misreading or non consideration of evidence on record regarding service of summons by Courts below. Having regard to facts I am of the view that summons upon defendant nos.11 and 14 of Title Suit no.04 of 1988 herein plaintiffs were not properly served. Therefore, I am in full agreement with views of Courts below. 

14. It is well settled that against ex-parte decree four kinds of relieves are available to an aggrieved party under the Code of Civil Procedure, those are: (1) Miscellaneous Case under IX Rule 13; (2) An appeal; (3) A Review under Order LXVII Rule 1; (4) A separate suit for setting aside the ex-parte decree. 

15. It has been decided in the case of Md. Wasiq Khan Vs. Md. Sabiq Khan and others 31 DLR (AD)51 that: when anybody suffers from an exported decree he can maintain a suit for setting aside the same. 

16. It is pertinent to mention that as exported judgment and decree passed in Title Suit no.04 of 1988 was set aside, so in my view, same should be proceeded with trial in accordance with law. In the case of Dharanidhar Aditya and others Hemanga Chandra Jana and others 21 CWN 1087, it has been held: "Decree setting aside ex-parte decree, effect of Court if bound to revive and proceed with trial of suit. Where an ex-parte decree is set aside by a Court of competent jurisdiction the effect is that the decree whereby the suit was terminated stands cancelled and the suit remains on the file of the Court as an undisposed of suit. In these circumstances it is incumbent upon the Court to proceed with the trial of the .suit and if the plaintiff does not wise to proceed with the trial of the suit, the Court must dismiss it but if the plaintiff desires to proceed with it, it must be tried in accordance with law. The fact that the suit terminated in an exported decree and not a consent decree, makes no difference in point of principle." This view receives support in the cases reported in 31. DLR (AD) 51 and 15 BLD-442. 

17. In the present case the suit was terminated in an ex-exported decree. That decree has been set aside by a Court of compete tent jurisdiction. The effect is that the decree whereby the suit was terminated stands cancelled and the suit remains on the file of the Court as an undisposed of suit. In these circumstances, it is incumbent upon the Court to proceed with the trial of the suit. If the plaintiffs do not wise to proceed with the trial of the suit the Court must dismiss it but if the plaintiffs desire to proceed with the suit it must be tried in accordance with law. 

18. In view of the discussions made above and the preponderant judicial views emerging out of the authorities referred to above, I am of the view that the trial of the suit will proceed in accordance with law. 

19. In the result, the Rule is disposed of without any order as to cost. The judgments and decrees of Courts below are hereby affirmed. The Title Suit no.04 of 1988 will stand revive and will be tried in accordance with law. Both parties are at liberty to adduce evidence in support of their respective claim and learned Judge of trial Court is directed to dispose of the suit on merit as early as possible. 

20. Office is directed to send down the records of this case at once with a copy of judgment for information and necessary action. 

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Mohammad Fazlul Karim. J., The defendant No.1 -petitioner seeks leave to 4ipeal against the judgment and decree dated 12.4.2004 passed by the High Court Division Appeal from Original Decree No. 96 of 2002 affirming those dated 26,11.2001 of the Joint District Judge and commercial Court No.1, Dhaka in Title Suit No 197 of 2001 decreeing the suit. 

2. The respondent No. l as the plaintiff filed "title Suit No.208 of 1997 renumbered as Title Stilt No.197 of 2001 against the petitioner bank for a declaration that the plaintiff had no liability to the petitioner bank for any loan amount, the so-called Memorandum of deposit of title deed dated 17.3.1988 was forged, concocted and illegal the plaintiff is entitled to get .back the title deed along with other supporting documents lying with the Bank and a decree of Tk.75,00,000/= as compensation against the petitioner bank. 

3. The plaintiff filed the suit stating, inter alia, that her properties were mortgaged to the petitioner Bank in 1987 in connection with two loan liabilities of Gold Star Lines Ltd and Transbangla Shipping Company of one Shawkat Ali. On 17.11.1988 both the loans were adjusted. Meanwhile a loan in the name of Pan Asia Lines was sought for by her brother-in-law (Bhasur) Mr. A.B. Siddiq but the said loan was not materialized. The plaintiff respondent then sought return of the title deeds by letter dated 17.12.1992 but to no effect. In 1992 the Bank filed Title Suit No.147 of 1992 in Artha Rin Adalat claiming mortgage of the properties of the plaintiff respondent on the basis of execution of Memorandum of Deposit of. Title Deed and the Agreement to create further charge dated 17.31988 and 9.3.1989 respectively. The two documents were forged. 

4. The defendant-petitioner bank filed written statement stating, inter alia, that on 29.2.1988 one A.B. Siddiq Ludu applied for Bai-Muajjal facility to the bank for purchase of two ships and also for adjustment of the loan of tk.99,50,000.00 and offered to mortgage the property of the plaintiff which was given in mortgage against the loans of Shawkat Ali. Defendant bank sanctioned Bai-Muajjal facility and in terms of the facility the plaintiff on 17.3.1988 executed a memorandum of deposit of title deeds and deposited the original lease deed dated 28.10.1968 and original deed of sale dated 22.2.1973 in the Bank. On 17.3.1988 A.B. Siddique Ludu also executed other charge documents. Thereafter, the plaintiff executed the agreement to create further charge on 9.3.1989. The Coast Marine Line Ltd have failed to adjust the loan of Tk1,33,70,592.00 whereupon the Bank instituted Title Suit No.147 of 190.2 renumbered as Title Suit No.113 of 2C00 in the 4th Court of Artha Rio Adalat for foreclosure and sale of mortgage and hypothecated properties including the property of respondent. By amendment of the written statement, the defendant Bank further stated that they already obtained a decree from the Artha Rin Adalat on 24.05.2001 and Artha Rin Adalat found the property of the plaintiff was mortgaged to the defendant Bank. The present suit was therefore hit by the principles of res-judicata. 
5. The trial Court on the pleading framed the following issues for determination:-

1. Was the, in the present form maintainable? 
2. Was the suit had for defect of parties? 
3. Had the plaintiff mortgaged the property covered by schedule deed against the loan of coast Marine Line Ltd? 
4. Was the suit barred by principles of res-judicata? 
5. What relief the plaintiff was entitled to? 

6. The suit was decreed in part without any order as to costs declaring that the loan in respect of M/S. Gold Star lines and Transbangla Shipping Company has been liquidated and the property mortgage on that account being the subject-matter of title deed No.788 dated 8,9,1972 is ordered to be returned to the plaintiff by the defendant No Bank and that the memorandum of deposit of the alleged title deed dated 17.3.1958 is forged, colourable, illegal, fraudulent and in operative. 

7. An appeal therefrom at the instance of the defendant No.1-petitioner was however, dismissed and forming the impugned judgment and decree of the trial Court and the Bank was directed to return the schedule documents within seven days of the receipt of the judgment. 

8. Dr. Kamal Hossain, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner has submitted that the matter in issue in the present suit being directly and substantial in issue in the Artha Rin Suit No. 147 of 1992. The subsequent instant suit being Title Suit No.197 of 2001 being barred by principle of res-judicata, the Courts below erred in law in holding that the decision of the Artha Rin Adalat could not operate as a bar of the present instant suit on the principle of res-judicata. The learned Counsel has further submitted that the property in question having already been mortgaged with the Bank against the liability of Transbangla Shipping Co and Gold Star Lines Ltd and that the same having also been mortgaged in respect of the loan of M/S. Coast Marine Lines Limited and that the petitioner having produced all relevant documents of mortgage including memorandum of deposit of title deeds, deed of agreement to create further charge duly signed by the respondent No.1, the original title documents, the written statement of respondent filed in 1995 in the Bank suit making no claim therein for return of the title deed, the Courts below erred in law in holding that the petitioner bank has failed to prove the case of mortgage or execution of exhibit-E memorandum of deposit of title deed and deed of agreement to create further charge inasmuch as the plaintiff as D.W.2 in the Artha Rin Adalat Suit No.147 of 1992 has admitted that she has mortgage her Gulshan's house with the Al-Baraka Bank as a security of loan against M/s, Gold Star Line and M/s. Transbangla Shipping Co owned by her brother-in-law's son Md. Shawkat Ali. 

9. Mr. Rafique-Ul-Huq, the learned Counsel appearing for the plaintiff-respondent No.1 has, however, submitted that the Artha Rin Adalat Suit No (147 of 1992)/(113 of 2000) being a suit for realization of the loan amount in which the plaintiffs property has been illegally shown to be the collateral security for the loan due to Coast Marine Lines Ltd and that during the pendency of the said suit the plaintiff respondent having filed the instant suit being Title Suit No.  (208 of 1997)/(147 of 2001)  for a declaration, inter alia that the plaintiffs property alleged to have been mortgaged for the loan in respect of Coast Marine Lines Ltd. is forged, fraudulent, not binding upon the plaintiff did not come within the purview of section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure as the issue involved in the instant suit is not directly and substantially in issue in a former suit pending in the Artha Rin Adalat between the parties and no litigating under the same title by a competent civil Court treating subsequent suit is not res-judicata inasmuch as not only the issue and the subject-matter are different but the Court is also not the same and of the same jurisdiction. The learned Counsel has further submitted that though Artha Rin Adalat Suit No. (147 of 1992)/(113 of 2000) was decreed on contest on 24.5.2001 wherein respondent No.1's property was shown to be a collateral security, but upon an application dated 28.8.2001 by the respondent No.1 under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure deleting the suit property thereby the decree was amended on 22.5.2002 deleting the property of respondent No.1 as security for the loan subject-matter of the decree against which order the petitioner bank has filed writ petition No. 3182 of 2002 which is pending. 

10. Admittedly Artha Rin Adalat Suit 147 of 1992 No.  (147 of 1992)/(113 of 2000) was filed for a money decree in 113 of 20(X) respect of the loan amount allowed to Coast Marine Lines Ltd for a  money decree of Tk.1,33,70,592/= with interest and for realisation of the money by sale of mortgage property and the property described to the schedule in the plaint wherein respondent No. l's property was included and it was stating in the plaint that the present plaintiff on 17.3.1988 created an equitable mortgage by depositing of title deed of her property mentioned in the schedule surety. The defendant in the said suit including the plaintiff-respondent No.1 denying the claim of alleged mortgage, it may be mentioned here that; the bank also did not claim that on 17.3.1988 the mortgage executed a memorandum of deposit of title deed on 9.3.1989 executed another agreement for creating further charge on the deed for the loan of Coast Marine Lines Limited. Admittedly no issue on the basis of the said denial of the parties was framed regarding the disputed nature of mortgage as alleged in the said Artha Rin Adalat Suit. D.W.I Mr. Azfar Ahmed an officer of the Bank and tadbirkar has deposed in that suit that the plaintiff respondent No.1 was not a surety and that defendant No.4 did not keep the land in question as security for the loan but the instant case was a suit for the declaration, inter alia, that the plaintiffs property was not subject-matter of security in respect of the loan, the subject-matter of Artha Rin Adalat Suit No.147 of 1992. 

11. Dr. Kamal Hossain has referred to a decision in the case reported in AIR 1965 SC 1153 wherein it has been held that the provision of section II of the Code of Civil Procedure are not exhaustive with respect to the earlier decision operating as res-judicata between the same parties on the same matter in controversy in a subsequent regular suit and on the general principle of res-judicata, any previous decision on a matter in controversy, decided after full contest or affording fair opportunity to the parties to prove their case by a competent Court to decide, it will operate as res-judicata in a subsequent regular suit. It is not necessary that the Court deciding the matter formerly be competent to decide the subsequent suit or that the former proceeding and the subsequent suit shall have the same subject-matter. The nature of the former proceeding is immaterial. 

12. We do not dispute the proposition of law prefounded in the said decision, rather the same has a persuasive force on us but in the facts and circumstances of the case the matter in issue was not at all in controversy in the previous suit and that the same was not litigated upon or any decision arrived at by the Artha Rin Adalat and as such the issue that has been decided on evidence in the instant suit could not operate as res-judicata as no such issue was framed as to whether the property was the subject-matter of mortgage arrived at or decided in the previous Artha Rin Adalat suit and even the same is not litigated upon in the previous suit. 

13. Dr. Kamal Hossain also referred to the decision in the case of Manager, Bangladesh Krishi Bank and others Vs. Al-haj Md. Nurul Islam and another reported in 52 DLR 434. The High Court Division held on the fact in that case that the question whether the plaintiff company suffered any loss or not due to latches non co-operation or activities of the Bank was considered and rejected in the earlier suit and that the suit was decreed against them and those adverse finding of the earlier suit do necessarily from the basic of res-judicata in the subsequent suit. 

14. But in the instant suit as we have found that no such issue was framed regarding the subject-matter of present suit and decision was arrived at and the issue of the present suit was not directly or substantially an issue in the previous suit so as to render the present suit barred by the principle of res-judicata. The High Court Division was not also unmindful as to the question of res-judicata to operate as a bar in the instant suit and the trial Court as well on consideration of the material on record arrived at a finding that the suit is not barred by res-judicata.

15. The High Court Division on merit, on consideration of the evidence on record arrived  at a finding that: 

"In the facts and circumstances of the case, such wild suggestion is not at all accepted. It is on record that after adjustment of the loans of M/s. Gold Star Lines and Trans Bangla Shipping Lines, another project of Pan Asia Lines for purchase of two vessels from London was submitted by Sirajul Alam and others and property of the plaintiff was offered as collateral. As project did not materialize, the plaintiff demanded return of her title deeds by letter dated 17.12.1992 which the bank received by putting the found seal of the bank. The bank did never deny the seal. Nor any step was taken to prove the seal forged. The plaintiff deposited her original deeds in trust with the bank. The bank was required to take utmost care in dealing with such security particularly in making further charge on the deeds. Admittedly, the bank never approached the plaintiff nor obtained any consent oral or written of the plaintiff for making further charge on the document. Such conduct is not becoming with the banking ethics, customs and practice. What disturbed us most, how a bank could have created without any consent of the plaintiff further security on the deed already deposited in the bank in connection with and continuance of another loan. 

In the circumstances, we find no reason to differ with the views of the learned Joint District Judge that the plaintiff did not execute the memorandum of deposit of title deed dated 17.03.1988 exhibit-E or the agreement for further charge dated 09.03.1989 exhibit-L and that she did not further mortgage her property to secure the loan of M/s. Coast Marine Lines Ltd." 

16. The findings on merit arrived at by the High Court Division are concurrent finding of fact arrived at on consideration of the evidence on record. We have perused the same and could not persuade ourselves to disturb the same concurrently arrived at by the Courts below. 

17. For the reasons as aforesaid, we find no substance in the submissions of the learned Counsel for the petitioner to interfere with the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. 

18. This petition is accordingly dismissed. 

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. M. M. Ruhul Amin, J: This appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 20.04.2002 passed by Division Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1578 of 1993 making the Rule absolute and also the judgment and order dated 20.05.2002 passed by the High Court Division rejecting the review application summarily, filed seeking review of the judgment in the civil revision. The revisional application was filed by the plaintiff against the judgment and order dated 24.05.1993 of 6th Court of Addition District Judge, Dhaka, passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No.45 of 1993 reversing the judgment and order dated 20.02.1993 dismissing the Miscellaneous Case No.28 of 1991 registered under Order 9 Rule 13 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The Miscellaneous Case was filed seeking setting aside of the ex parte decree dated 12.12.1984.

2. Short facts are that the respondents' predecessor filed Title Suit No.208 of 1984 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Dhaka for declaration of title in the land described in the schedule of the plaint and for further declaration that the Memo No.560 dated 09.06.1984 issued by the defendant No.6 (Sub Divisional Engineer, P.W.D., Sub-Division No.1 Tejgaon Industrial Area, Dhaka) is illegal, unlawful, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiff.

3. The defendants entered appearance in the said suit and prayed for time to file written statement but ultimately no written statement having been filed the suit was fixed for ex parte hearing on 06.11.1984. On that date the defendants prayed for time to file written statement but no written statement was filed and the suit was fixed on 28.11.1984 for ex parte hearing. The date so fixed for ex parte hearing was shifted to 12.12.1984 by the Court and on that date the suit was heard ex parte and decreed. Thereafter the defendants filed an application under Order 9 Rule 13 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and thereupon the aforementioned Miscellaneous Case was stated. The prayer for restoration of the original suit to its file and number was opposed by the plaintiff. The trial court dismissed the case holding that the petitioners of the miscellaneous case failed to make out a case for setting aside the ex parte decree. Thereupon the defendants took an appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No.45 of 1993 before the District Judge, Dhaka. The appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka and the same was alloyed and the ex parte decree dated a 12/12.1984 was set aside and the original shit was restored to file and number. The plaintiff then moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained Rule. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute upon observing that the appellate court was in error in not holding that the defendants were guilty of latches in conducting their case and thereupon caused failure of justice in allowing the miscellaneous appeal. As against the order dated 20.04.2002 of the High Court Division making the Rule absolute the appellants filed an application under Order 47 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil procedure seeking review of the aforesaid judgment and order and the High Court Division by the order dated 20.05.2002 rejected the review application summarily upon observing that no case for review was made out.

4. Leave was granted to consider the submission that the entire suit plot No.533 was acquired by the Government and the respondent No.1 obtained the ex parte decree by making false statement on the basis of forged document and as such the impugned judgments and orders dated 20.04.2002 and 20.05.2002 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1578 of 1993 are liable to be set aside for ends of justice and further submission that the respondent No.1 previously filed a suit being Title Suit No.222 of 1979 against the present appellants for the same relief and the same was dismissed for default and the respondent No.1 having not filed any Miscellaneous Case or appeal against the said order dated 05.03.1975 the present suit has been filed suppressing the said facts in could ex parte decree was also obtained and as such the impugned judgment and order dated 20.04.2002 and 20.05.2002 passed in Civil Revision No.1578 of 1993 are liable to be set aside.

5. We have heard Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, the learned Attorney General for the appellants and Mr. T. H. Khan, the learned Counsel for respondent Nos. 1-3 and perused the judgment of the High Court Division and other connected papers.

<u>6. It is not disputed that by gazette notification dated 20.02.1950 the total area of C. S. Plot No.533 (suit plot) i.e. 2.30 acres of Mouza-Tejkunipara. P.S. Tejgaon. District-Dhaka along with other lands were acquired by the Government.</u>

7. The plaintiff's case is that although Suit Plot No.533 was requisitioned by the Government in L.A. Case No.3 of 1948-49 but subsequently the suit plot was released from such requisition on 20.02.1950 which fact would be evident from a memorandum vide memo No.5463 dated 18.12.1988 of the Additional Land Acquisition Officer, Dhaka.

8. The learned Attorney General submits that after final publication of gazette notification dated 20.02.1950 the right, title and interest if any, of the original owner in the acquired land including the suit plot had already extinguished and once the property was acquired and gazette notification published, the same vested in the government and cannot be released in the manner as claimed by plaintiff. In support of his argument the learned Attorney General cited the case of Director of Housing & Settlement Vs. Abdul Majid Howlader and others reported in 9 MLR (AD) 73 and submitted that in that case it was held that the settled law is that upon acquisition of particular property the same vests in the Government and that being the position in law the prayer for release made by the Respondents was totally misconceived one since under the law they were not entitled to have the property released. Accordingly suit so filed seeking release of the property was not legally well advised one as well as was not entertainable in law. He further submitted that in the instant case the validity of acquisition of the property in question has not been disputed. He next submitted that the undisputed position is that the property in suit was acquired under the provision of (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 and to that respect gazette notification has been published making the acquisition final and vesting the property in suit in the Government. As per provision of law on the publication of the gazette notification the property acquired vests in the Government and consequent thereupon Government becomes the owner of the property. The person whose property is acquired under the Act and consequent thereupon vests in the Government, is not entitled to claim any interest in the land so acquired. In that view of the matter there was no scope for the plaintiffs, who have no interest of any kind in the land in suit, to seek for a declaration that they are entitled to get the property released.

9. The learned Counsel for respondent Nos.1-3 submitted that the Executive Engineer, P.W.D. Development Division-1, Dhaka vide memo No.615 dated 21.01.1950 recommended for release of the all lands out of alignment and accordingly notice under Rule 10(2) of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Rules, 1948 was issued. The learned Counsel has also drawn our attention to the order sheet of L.A. Case No.3 of 1948-49 dated 20.12.1949 and submitted that the Executive Engineer, P.W.D. by his memo No.10352-58D dated 19.12.1949 sent a revised blue print showing the land to be acquired permanently and temporarily and accordingly by order dated 12.01.1950 after obtaining a report from kanango of the office of the Deputy Commissioner, the Requisition Branch of the Revenue Department of the then Government of East Pakistan was written for action to be taken on the revised plan received from the Executive Engineer, Public Works Department. Order dated 07.03.1950 of the same L.A. Case is as follows:-

"De-requisition notices served. Fresh notice under section 5(7) in form 'D' has been re-submitted to Government with T.O. No.96-L.A. dated 21.01.1950 for publication. Wait till 25.03.1950.

Sd/-Illegible

L. A. C."

10. It is on record that gazette notification regarding permanent acquisition of the land was published on 20.02.1950 as noticed earlier and as such the de-requisition or release of the property as claimed by the e plaintiff could not take place. Therefore, the plaintiff cannot take any advantage of the order sheet of L.A. Case No.3 of 1948-49 or the correspondence made between different Government functionaries in this respect for before these correspondence could reach finality the Gazette notification dated 20.02.1950 regarding acquisition of the suit land was published.

11. It is the case of the plaintiff that 30 decimals of land suit Plot No.533 was under acquisition and the remaining 2 acres of land was outside acquisition as per revised blue print prepared by the Executive Engineer, Development Division No.1, P.W.D. and according to plaintiff's own case steps were taken for de-requisitioning and releasing the remaining 2 acres of land which the plaintiff tried to show from the order sheet of L.A. Case No.3 of 1948/49 as noted earlier.

12. From the plaint of Title Suit No.208 of 1984 of the 1st  Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka brought by Mrs. Shamirunnessa Bibi wife of Hasan Ali against Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and others it appears that the plaintiff sought declaration of her title over the entire 2.30 acres of land of C .S. Plot No.533 of C. S. Khatian No.112 of Mouza Tejkunipara, P.S. Tejgaon, Dhaka although according to plaintiffs own case 30 decimals of land was under acquisition,

13. Without going into the merit of the matter it can be safely said that when it is the admitted case of the plaintiff that 30 decimals of land out of 2.30 acres of land of Suit Plot No.533 is within the acquired land of the Government as per gazette notification dated 20.02.1950, the plaintiff's suit for entire 2.30 acres of Plot No.533 on the face of it was not maintainable. Being faced with the situation the learned Counsel for the respondents could not give a satisfactory reply on this point.

<u>14. The learned Attorney General in this connection submitted that to avoid the embargo of section 14A of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948, the plaintiff brought the suit claiming the entire 2.30 acres of land of Suit Plot No.533. The plaintiff also sought correction of record of right in respect of entire 2.30 acres of land although she claims 100 acres of land only and not the entire 2.30 acres. The learned Attorney General further submitted that although the plaintiff cleverly sought declaration of title over the entire 2.00 acres of land of the suit plot but that will not bring the suit out of the mischief of section 14A of the Act.</u>

15. The learned Attorney General lastly argued that in this court in exercise of the power conferred under Article104 of the Constitution can do complete justice and dispose of the matter finally. In support of his contention the learned Attorney General cited the cases of Gannysons Ltd. Vs. Sonali Bank reported in 37 DLR (AD) 42, AFM Naziruddin Vs. Mrs. Hameeda Banu reported in 45 DLR (AD) 38 and Secretary, Internal Resources Division, Ministry of Finance and Chairman, National Board of Revenue, Dhaka Vs. Nasrin Banu and 5 others reported in 48 DLR (AD) 171.

<u>16. We have already noticed that in this case ex-parte decree was passed on 12.12.1984 in Title Suit No.208 of 1993 and in Miscellaneous Appeal No.45 of 1993 the Ex-parte decree was set aside and the original suit was restored to file and number. The High Court Division making the Rule absolute in the revisional application restored the ex-parte decree to its original position. Therefore, the fact remains that there was no contested hearing of the suit and the defendants could not place their case and other materials before the court for proper adjudication.</u>

17. Complete justice is to be done in an appropriate case. "It is an extraordinary procedure for doing justice for completion of or putting an end to a cause or matter pending before this court. If a substantial justice under law and on undisputed facts can be made so that parties may not be pushed to further litigation, then a recourse to the provision of Article 104 may be justified" (45 D.L.R. (AD)38)

18. Therefore, in the circumstances of the case, we do not consider it a fit case to do complete justice.

<u>19. Since there are some patent incongruities in the plaint of Title Suit No.208 of 1994 brought by the plaintiff Samirunnessa Bibi as noticed earlier the ex parte decree dated 12.12.1984 ex-facie is not sustainable.</u>

20. Accordingly the learned Additional District Judge did not commit any illegality in allowing the Miscellaneous Appeal No.45 of 1993 rather the High Court Division was in error in making the Rule absolute.

21. The appeal is, therefore, allowed without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment of the High Court Division is set aside and those of the appellate court passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No.45 of 1993 are restored.

End.
