Mr. M. M. Ruhul Amin, J.: This appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 21.01.1997 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 488 of 1994 making the Rule absolute. 

2. Short facts are that the writ petitioner filed the writ petition stating, inter alia, that he is a citizen and permanent resident of Bangladesh. After partition of India some members of Ansari family, namely, Bashir Ahmed Ansari, Mokter Ahmed Ansari and Peshkar Ahmed Ansari, the three brothers, migrated to the then Pakistan. Late Bashir Ahmed Ansari, father of Ali Akbar Ansari started business in Karachi and the other two brothers Mokter Ahmed Ansari and Peshkar Ahmed Ansari started their businesses in Dhaka and Chittagong respectively and settled in the then East Pakistah. In 1956 the respondent started his own business in Rajshahi and Chittagong. In 1963 he married a Bengali girl and permanently settled in the then East Pakistan. In 1970 Bashir Ahmed Ansari, the father of the respondent died leaving behind the respondent as his only son and widow Fatema Begum After his death his brothers Mokter Ahmed Ansari and Peshkar Ahmed Ansari took charge of the business and properties of Ansari Family in the then East Pakistan and West Pakistan. Subsequently both of them along with their wives orally gifted all their properties in the then East Pakistan to Ali Akbar Ansari, the respondent who is the only son of their elder brother. The gift was confirmed by a declaration of gift on 15.01.1971. The respondent along with the numbers of his family was in peaceful possession of the disputed properties at 426 and 427, Ansari Mansion, Enayet Bazar, Batali Road, Chittagong long before the liberation of Bangladesh and also from 15.01.1971 when the declaration of gift was made. After liberation of Bangladesh the case properties were declared as abandoned properties vide Memo No. 1574 dated 12.06.1972 issued by the Executive Engineer, Chittagong Buildings Division No.1 Chittagong. The respondent made several representations to the Board of Management of Abandoned Properties which asked him to submit documents relating to his ownership. During the pendency of his applications before the authorities the respondent was evicted from the case properties in the later part of 1979. The case properties were included in the 'K' list in serial Nos. 135 and 136 respectively of the list of abandoned buildings published in the Bangladesh Gazette on the 23rd September, 1986 under Ordinance No.54 of 1985. The respondent then filed Case Nos. 1084 of 1987 and 183 of 1988 in respect of holdings Nos. 426 and 427 respectively before the Court of Settlement which dismissed both the cases and maintained the inclusion of the properties in the list of abandoned buildings. The respondent then filed Writ Petition Nos. 62 and 63 of 1989 before the High Court Division, Chittagong Bench which were renumbered as Writ Petition Nos. 1497 and 1489 of 1991 respectively in the High Court Division in Dhaka. By judgment and order dated 30.07.1992 the High Court Division declared the enlistment of the case properties in the ' 'Ka' list as illegal and without lawful authority. It was further held that the respondent had proved before the Court of Settlement by the said oral gift that the case properties were not abandoned properties. The Government-appellants did not prefer any appeal before the Appellate Division and the Ministry of Works vide Notification No.10/Chatta-150/85/1992 dated 24.05.1993 excluded the case properties from the 'Ka' list. One Abdus Sattar who is a tenant, later on allottee of the case properties tiled Review Petition Nos. 4 and 5 of 1993 against the judgment and order of the High Court Division dated 30.07.1992 before the said Division Bench but the same was rejected by the judgment and order dated 12.01.1994. The Government-appellant also filed Review Petition Nos.4 and 5 of 1994 against the said judgment and order of the High Court Division dated 30.07.1992 and both the review applications were rejected by the same Division Bench of the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 12.07.1994. The Government petitioner in Civil Petition Nos. 650 and 660 of 1994 and one Md. Amin Chowdhury and others the petitioners in Civil Petition No. 694 of 1994 preferred petition for appeal before the Appellate Division against the rejection of the review petitions, but the same were-dismissed. The respondent however in spite of repeated representations to various authorities was not given back the vacant possession of the properties. The respondent then filed the instant Writ Petition No.488 of 1994 for getting back vacant possession of the case properties. 

3. Respondent No.1 in affidavit-in-opposition contended, inter alia, that Mokter Ahmed Ansari and Peshkar Ahmed Ansari, were two brothers who on 22.02.1960 purchased the lands question by two registered deeds from one Babu Kader Nath and thereafter constructed two apartment buildings thereon. On 21.09.1967 Mokter Ahmed Ansari sold his share of apartments in the said buildings and the land to his three nephews, namely, Jobed Aslam, Arshad Parvez and Emran Azad, sons of Peshkar Ahmed Ansari and the transferees were inducted into possession of the sold apartments. The three nephews were possessing the apartments and lands through their tenants. During the war of liberation the owners of the case properties left for Pakistan and as their whereabouts were not known the properties were declared as abandoned properties by operation of P.O No.16 of 1972. The case properties were allotted to the different allottees and some of them were tenants of the said three nephews and Peshkar Ahmed Ansari. The respondent being a cunning man tried to grab the two buildings by impersonating him as Ali
Akbar Ansari son of late Bashir Ahmed Ansari and after creating a forged declaration of gifts using the names of Moktar Ahmed Ansari, Peshkar Ahmed Ansari and their wives. The two buildings were rightly and legally enlisted in the 'Ka' list of the abandoned properties as the owners left the buildings uncared for and their whereabouts were not known. 

4. The High Court Division held that the fact remains that in the earlier writ petitions viz., writ petition Nos. 1497 and 1489 of 1991 the High Court Division declared the properties not to be abandoned properties and asked the Government to release the same from the list of abandoned properties. Therefore the case properties are no longer stand vested in the Government and the Government has also given effect to the order of the High Court Division by excluding the case properties from the 'Ka' list of abandoned properties. It was contended by the Government-appellants that in the light of some observations made by the High Court Division in the judgments delivered in the review petitions the Government has filed O.C. Suit No.109 of 1995 in the 1st court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Chittagong for a declaration that by virtue of the alleged oral gift dated 15.01.1971 in favour of the respondent no title has passed to the respondent and that the alleged oral gift is absolutely false, baseless and concocted. One Abul Hossain, a tenant of the case properties, had also instituted O.C. Suit No. 190 of 1993 in the 1st Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Chittagong to protect the tenant's right and also filed an application for injunction and obtained order of temporary injunction restraining the Government-defendant Nos.1-5 from evicting the tenant and the said O.C. Suit No.190 of 1993 is pending. 

5. The High Court Division opined that since the Government-appellants have divested themselves from all interest in the case properties, they have now no locus standi to file the aforesaid suit in the Civil Court for deciding the question of title. The same is the position of those tenants or lessees who filed similar suit and obtained injunction restraining the defendants from delivering possession to the respondent as their interest in the case properties is derived from that of the Government. The High Court Division held that it is difficult to accept the contention of the Government that the case properties cannot be handed over to the respondent as long as the question of title is not decided. The observations made by the High Court Division in its judgment in the review petitions do not create any right or interest in favour of the Government or of the tenants to file suits before the Civil Court for declaration of title over the case properties. The High Court Division accordingly made the Rule Nisi absolute. 

6. Leave was granted to consider the submission that on 06.03.1997 O.C. Suit No.109 of 1995 filed by the Government-appellants has been decreed ex-parte and under section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure the Civil Courts have jurisdiction to try all suits of civil nature excepting suits the cognizance of which is either expressly or impliedly barred by any law. The High Court Division in exercise of its jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution exceeded its jurisdiction in interfering with the civil suits then pending in the Civil Courts whose decisions and jurisdictions are amendable to interference only by an appellate and revisional court as provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure and the further submission that the ownership of the case properties having not been decided by either the Court of Settlement or the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos. 1497 and 1489 of 1991 and the said two forums being not the forums for determination of title in any case, and, following the judgment of the High Court Division in the two review cases, the Government-appellants having instituted a suit in the Civil Court for determination of title of the case properties, the High Court Division erred in law in holding that the Government-appellants have no locus standi to file a suit in the Civil Court to determine the title of the case properties and further submission that in view of the transfer of the share of Moktar Ahmed Ansari in favour of his three nephews in 1967 and in view of the fact that the said transferees never claimed their share of the case properties, and, further, the alleged gift to the respondent being false, forged and concocted, the case properties have no rightful owner in Bangladesh and have already vested in the People's Republic of Bangladesh under Article 143(1)(c) of the Constitution and therefore the High Court Division committed an error of law in directing the Government-appellants to hand over possession of the case properties to the respondent and also the submission that some of the lessees of the case properties having been inducted into possession before 26.03.1971 the Government-appellants are not in a position to deliver vacant possession of the case properties to the respondent and as such the direction of the High Court Division to deliver vacant possession of the case properties to the respondent is in executable. 

7. We have heard Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, the learned Additional Attorney General for the appellants and Mr. T.H. Khan, the learned Counsel for the respondent and perused the judgment of the High Court Division and other connected papers. 

8. It is not disputed that the case properties, belonged to Moktar Ahmed Ansari and Peshkar Ahmed Ansari, two brothers. The respondent's case is that both of them along with their wives orally gifted all their properties in the then East Pakistan including the case properties to the respondent who is the only son of their elder brother Bashir Ahmed Ansari. The gift was confirmed by a declaration of gift made on 15.01.1971. The further case of the respondent that he was in possession of disputed properties but after liberation of the Country the case properties were declared as abandoned properties and included in the 'Ka' list of the abandoned buildings. He filed the Case No. 1084 of 1987 and 183 of 1988 in the Court of Settlement for exclusion of the case properties from the list of abandoned properties and both the cases were dismissed. He then filed Writ Petition Nos. 62 and 63 of 1989 before the High Court Division (Chittagong Bench) which were subsequently renumbered in Dhaka as Writ Petition Nos.1497 and 1489 of 1991. heard and disposed of by the judgment and order dated 30.07.1992 and the Rules were made absolute. No Civil Petition for leave to appeal was preferred by the present appellants against the judgment and order dated 30.07.1992 passed by the High Court Division in the above mentioned writ petitions. In compliance of the order dated 30.07.1992 of the High Court Division passed in Writ Petition Nos. 62 and 63 of 1989 subsequently renumbered as Writ Petition No. 1497 and 1489 of 1991 the Ministry of Works vide Notification No.10/Chatta-150/85/1992 dated 24.05.1993 excluded the case properties from the 'Ka' list of the abandoned buildings. One Abdus Sattar who is an allottee in respect of a portion of the case properties filed review petition Nos. 4 and 5 of 1993 against the judgment and order dated 30.07.1992 after a long delay and the review applications were rejected by the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 12.01.1994. The present appellants also filed two Review Petition Nos.4 and 5 of 1994 after long delay of 580 days which were also rejected by the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 12.07.1994. Against the decision of the High Court Division dated 12.07.1994 the present appellants filed Civil Petition for leave to appeal Nos.650 and 660 of 1994 and one Md. Amin Chowdhury and others also filed Civil Petition No. 694 of 1994 before this Division. All these leave petitions were dismissed by this Division by judgment and order dated 04.04.1995 but still the possession of the case properties was not handed over to the respondent. Hence the respondent was constrained to file the present Writ Petition No.488 of 1994. 

9. It appears that on 08.08.1995 the appellant filed other Class Suit No.109 of 1995 against the respondent No.1 and others praying for a declaration that by virtue of the alleged oral gift dated 15.01.1971 no title has passed in favour of the respondent and the alleged oral gift is forged. This suit was filed after disposal of the above mentioned Writ Petitions, review petitions, civil petitions for leave to appeal and after excluding the case properties from the list of abandoned buildings by the Government. The suit was decreed ex-parte on 06.03.1997. It is not disputed that the ex-parte decree was however subsequently set aside in Miscellaneous Case No.103 of 1997 and suit was restored to its file and number. 

10. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali submits that the respondent is an imposter in the case properties and a gigantic fraud has been committed by him for grabbing the case property and other properties. He further submits that the Respondent is nobody to the Ansari family and since the original owners, namely, Moktar Ahmed Ansari and Peshker Ahmed Ansari left this country at the time of liberation was in 1971 and after liberation of the country the properties were uncared for and the whereabouts of the owners were not known, the same became abandoned properties by operation of law. He further submits that by Annexure-B dated 24.05.1993 the case properties were excluded from the list of abandoned properties in compliance with the judgment and order of the High Court Division dated 30.07.1992 passed in Writ Petition Nos. 1497 and 1489 of 1991 but the judgment of review petition Nos.4 and 5 of 1994 arising out of Writ Petition Nos.1489 and 1497 of 1991 a Division Bench of the High Court Division observed that contentious matters should always be thrashed out before the Civil Court and accordingly they filed other Class Suit No.109 of 1995 in the Civil Court. It is not disputed that this suit was filed after the disposal of the writ petitions and the ex-parte decree has already been set aside in Miscellaneous Case No.103 of 1997 and the suit was restored to its file and number. Moreover, after release of the properties from list of abandoned buildings by Annexure-B as stated above the learned Additional Attorney General could not satisfy us that the Appellant has locus standi to file a civil suit in respect of the case properties. It is true that under section 9 of the Code of civil Procedure the Civil Courts have jurisdiction to try all suits of civil nature excepting suits the cognizance of which is either expressly or impliedly barred by any law but the plaintiff must show his locus standi to file such a suit. In the instant case, in our view the appellants have miserably failed to prove their locus standi to bring the civil suit. It further appears that in the civil petition for leave to appeal it was submitted by the learned Advocate for the appellants that the High Court Division committed error of law in exercise of its jurisdiction in interfering with the civil suits then pending in civil courts whose decisions and jurisdictions are amendable to interference only by an appellate and revisional Court as provided for in the Code of Civil Procedure. It appears that the submissions of the learned Advocate was wholly incorrect as Other Class Suit No.109 of 1995 was filed by the appellant long after the disposal of the writ petition Nos.1497 and 1489 of 1991. It further appears that the appellants did not plead any case that the respondent is an imposter in the case properties before the High Court Division. Moreover, the High Court Division found that the oral gift which was subsequently confirmed by declaration of oral gift on 15.01.1971 in favour of the respondent by the admitted owner was valid and the appellants did not prefer any petition for leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 30.07.1992 of the High Court Division. So the appellants at this stage can not say that the deed of gift in favour of the respondent in an act of forgery. 

11. Mr. T.H. Khan argued that the other Class Suit No.109 of 1995 was filed by the appellants after disposal of the writ petitions and the review petitions. So, the civil suit is barred by res-judicata in view of the findings made by the High Court Division in the writ petitions that the gift in favour of the respondent by the admitted owners is valid and hence the appellants are debarred from raising this issue again in any subsequent proceeding. In support of his contention the learned Counsel has placed before us the case of Muhammad Chiraghuddin Bhatti Vs. the Province of West Pakistan reported in Supreme Court Monthly Review, 1971, at page 447, the case of Daryao and others Vs. State of U.P. and others reported in A.I.R. 1961 S.C. 1457, the case of Mirza Muhammad Yaqub Vs. the Chief Settlement Commissioner, Lahore and another reported in P.L.D. 1965 S.C. 254, the case of the Union of India Vs. Nanak Singh reported A.I.R. 1968 (S.C.) 1370 and the case of Dr. Syed Motiur Rob being dead his heirs Shamsun Nahar and others Vs. Bangladesh and others reported in 42 D.L.R. (AD) 126. He also referred to section 115 of the Evidence Act and submitted that the appellants are now estopped from raising the plea that the gift in favour of the Respondent is not a valid one or that they have locus standi to bring the civil suit challenging the gift in question in favour of the Respondent in view of the finding made by the High Court Division in the earlier Writ Petition Nos.I497 and 1489 of 1991 and in the judgment of the present writ petition No.488 of 1994. 
12. In reply the learned Additional Attorney General submits that it is the established principle of law that disputed question of fact cannot be decided in writ petition as observed by the High Court Division in the Review Petitions. So, they filed the civil suit and in support of his contention the learned Additional Attorney General cited number of decisions. There is no civil in the proposition of law that disputed question of fact cannot be decided in a writ petition which is a summery procedure for speedy relief. In the review petitions the observation of the High Court Division in this respect is of general nature regarding this settled principle of law. Accordingly we need not discuss the cases cited by the learned Additional Attorney General on this point. 

13. In view of our discussions above, we hold that the provisions of Article 143(I)(c) of the Constitution are not attracted in the present case as the respondent was found to be the rightful owner of the case properties by the High Court Division. 

14. In the above facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the view, that the High 
Court Division on correct assessment of the materials on record came to the correct finding that the case properties are not abandoned properties and accordingly the properties were already released by the Government by Annexure-B and hence the appellants had no locus standi to file the civil suit challenging the validity of the gift made in favour of the Respondent after disposal of the writ petitions. The same is the position of tenants and lessees as their interest in the case properties is derived from the government and the general of observation of the High Court Division in the review petition that disputed question of fact cannot be decided in the writ petition does not create any right and interest in favour of the Government or the tenants to file a suit before the civil court to decide title of the case properties. 

15. Accordingly, we find no cogent reason to interfere with the judgment of the High Court Division. 

16. The appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs. 

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Mamnoon Rahman, J:- Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 13-11-1997 (decree drawn on 19-11.-1997) passed by the Subordinate Judge, Second Court Jhalokathi in Title Appeal No.127 of 1994 reversing those dated 27-6-1994 (decree drawn 4-7-1994) passed by the Senior Assistant Judge Kathalia, Jhalkathi in title Suit No.62 of 1993 should not to be set aside and or pass such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The short facts relevant for the disposal for this Rule are that; The opposite party as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.62 of 1993 in Court Assistant Judge, Kathalia, Jhalokathi impleading the petitioner as defendant for declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No.17 of 1991 is null void, void, collusive and not binding upon the opposite party. The plaintiff further prayed for declaration of the title of the property in question as "vested property" described in the schedule of the plaint. 

3. The case of the plaintiff is that the land in question belong Shatish Chandra Roy and S.S record was prepared and published in his name. Shatish Chandra Roy died on 16.7.65 leaving the present petitioner and Mukundra Behare Roy who equal share. Mokunda left for India with his family after the war of 1965 resulting enlistments of his land as vested property. The defendant being only son of Shatish Chandra Roy filed Title Suit No.17 of 1991 challenging the V.P. proceeding and obtained exparte decree. The plaintiff finding no other alternative filed this suit. 

4. The defendant petitioner contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegation in the plaint and contending inter alia that the suit is not maintainable in its present form. The suit land belong to the father of the petitioner who died on 16.7.1975 leaving the defendant petitioner as the only heirs because the another son Mukunda Behari Roy died in the life time of the predecessor in the interest of the petitioner. The further case of the petitioner defendant is the defendant as plaintiff filed a suit for declaration and the summon was serve property but despite service of summons of that suit the defendants failed to contest resulting exparte decree and as such there is no scope for passing any decree, hence the petitioner defendant prays for dismissal of the suit. 

5. During trial the plaintiffs adduced 4 witnesses while the defendants petitioner adduced 4 witnesses. Both the parties also produced documentary evidence. The Trial Court after hearing the parties and considering the material on record as well as evidence, both oral and documentary dismissed the suit on contest. 

6. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs filed Title Appeal No.175 of 1994 before the District Judge, Jhalkathi. The petitioner defendant being respondent contested the appeal. The said appeal was heard and disposed of by the Subordinate judge; Second Court, Jhalokathi who vide his judgment and decree dated 3.11.1997 and 9.11.1997 allowed the appeal and reversed the judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court. 

7. The petitioner defendant respondent being aggrieved by and dissatisfied by the impugned judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate Court moved this instant revisional application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure before this
Court and obtained the present rule. 

8. Mr. Md. Harun-or-Rashid, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the lower appellate Court committed an error in finding that defendant petitioner obtained exported decree on 14.1:1993 in Title Suit No.17 of 1993 by practicing fraud upon the trial Court which is admittedly beyond the pleadings of plaintiff and such error occasioned failure of Justice. He submits that the Court below misdirected itself in arriving an erroneous finding of fact as well as law and thereby committed an error of law resulting in an error in such order occasioning failure of Justice. He submits that the V.P. proceeding was initiated in the year 1976 and the ultimate V.P. proceeding vide V.P. No.1 of 1981 was initiated in the year 1981 and such initiation is not permissible in the eye of law as because the Ordinance No.1 of 1969 was repealed with effect from 23.3.1974. By referring the decisions reported in 46 DLR (HCD) 136 and 56 DLR(AD)73 the learned Advocate submits that the Apex Court is of the view that after the natural date of the aforesaid Ordinance no further proceeding for vested property can be initiated and as such the appellate Court below failed to assessed the vital question of law. 

9. Mr. Miaan Sheikh Mohd. Abdullah, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposes the rule. He submits that the petitioner by practicing fraud obtained the exparte decree as because admittedly the brother of the petitioner left for India in the year of 1965. He submits that by suppressing the material facts the petitioner obtained the exparte decree and as such the lower appellate Court has rightly allowed the appeal and set aside the Judgment and decree passed by the trial Court which is a misconceived one. The learned Advocate referred two decisions reported in 27 DLR(AD)52 and 33DLR (AD)30 and submits that despite repeal of the parent law the effect can be continued or enforced. 

10.1 have perused the judgments of both the Court below and the L.C. record. Considering the facts and circumstances, evidence on record the Trial Court found that the petitioner obtained the exparte decree in a rightful manner and accordingly the Trial Court dismissed the suit. The Trial Court also observed there is no scope to allow the prayer of declaration that the property in question is a vested one. While adjudicating the appeal the appellate Court came be a conclusion that the petitioner by practicing fraud obtained the exparte decree and also admittedly the brother of the petitioner was left for India which the plaintiff has been able to proved beyond reasonable doubt by adducing both oral and documentary evidence. 

11. In the instant case it appears that the trial Court dismissed the suit but on an appeal the lower appellate Court allowed the appeal and there by set aside the decree obtained by the petitioner in Title Suit No.17 of 1991 as well as passed a decree of declaration of the land in question as vested property. The main question raised in the instant case is that whether any V.P. proceeding can be initiated or a Civil Court can passed a decree for declaration of a vested property after repeal of the Ordinance I of 1969 on 23.3:1974. 

12. Ordinarily this Court cannot adjudicate any factual aspect even in a case of reversal where there is no misreading or miss-appreciation of evidence by the lower Court, but in .the instant case the vital question of law has been reaised by the petitioner and as such I am of the view that this Court exercising the power under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure has got ample jurisdiction to see or examine the impugned order where there is an allegation of misreading of law. 

13. In the instant case admittedly the V.P proceeding was initiated by opening note sheet in the year 1976 admitted by both the parties in the pleadings. The formal case was initiated in the year 1981 being V.P. case No.4 of 1981. The petitioner came to know about the said proceeding and filed the .suit for declaration resulting obtainment of exparte decree. On perusal of the L.C. record it appears that the plaintiffs admitted the receipt of the summons of that suit but due to the fault of the officers the plaintiff cannot contest the suit. In the above circumstances it cannot be said that the plaintiff is not aware of the said suit. Also the plaintiff failed to show any positive case practice of fraud or collusion. 

14. In the instant case 'the entire V.P. proceeding was initiated after 23.3.1974 i.e. the date on which the Ordinance 1 of 1969 was repealed. Whether such proceeding can he initiated after such repeal came before this Court wherein the High Court Division in the case of Laxmi Kanta Roy Vs. Upazilla Nirbahi Officer and another reported in. 46 DLR 136 held; 
"At the very outset it has drawn my attention in this case as to whether the institution of the V.P. cases No.142 of 1980 was maintainable in the eye of law. The Defence of Pakistan ordinace and Rules came in the year 1965 the Defence of Pakistan ordinance and Rules were repealed in the year 1969 but by ordinance No.1 of 1969 promulgated by the then Central Government or Pakistan, some of the provisions of the Defence of Pakistan Rules were kept alive and continued. Thereafter by Act No.XLV of 1974 the Ordinance No.1 of 1969 was repeated on 23.3.74. After the repeat of Ordinance No.1 of 1969 whether any proceeding unde the said ordinance and Rule could be started. Admittedly, the present Vested Property case was started in the year 1980. Unfortunately, this point was neither raised by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff nor the learned Judges had taken notice of the law which was repealed in the year 1974. This point was not specifically agitated and. no issue was framed on it. Mr. Abdul Quayum, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that since it is a question of law it can be agitated in this Court at this provisional stage. In this case Mr. Quayum has referred to the case of Nittay Gopal Roy Barman Vs. Pran Gopal Nandi and others, 32 DLR 11. In the aforesaid Judgment it is categorically held by his Lordship that after repeal of the Ordinance No.1 of 1969 by Act No. XLV of .1971 on 23.3.74 the authority was not completed to start such vested property proceeding in the eye of law in the aforesaid judgment his Lordship held as follows; 
"Mere claim of the Assistant Custodian that the property of the deceased leslator is an enemy property in respect of which an enemy property case was started in 1974 in not sufficient for coming to a conclusion that the property is an enemy property" 
I fully agree with the view of his Lordship expressed in the aforesaid decision. Since the law on Enemy Property itself died with the repeal of Ordinance 1 of 1969 on 23.3.74 by Act XLV of 1974, no further vested property case can be started thereafter on the basis of the law which is already dead. So I find that the starting of the vested property case No.142 of 1980 in the year 1980 is absolutely without jurisdiction and has no legal basis at all" 

15. The same question has been raised before their Lordships of our Appellate Division and their Lordships in the case of Aroti Rani Paul Vs. Sudarshan Komar Paul and another reported in 56 DLR(AD) 73 held; 
"We have perused the judgments of the Court below as well as the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. It appears that both the Courts below having considered the oral and documentary evidence, concurrently held that the transfer by registered deeds of 1975 vide Exhibits-5 and 6 as made by father and uncle living in a joint undivided Hindu family under the Dayabhag School of law, is valid. Since the father and uncle being in Bangladesh in the year 1957, transferred the suit property, by the aforesaid registered deeds of gift, cannot be declared an enemy property in view of the aforesaid decision as referred to above in 46DLR 136 any we accepted the argument of Mr. Bhuiyan that since the law of enemy property itself died with file repeal of Ordinance No.91of 1969 on 23.3.1974 no further Vested Property case can be started thereafter on the basis Of the law which is already dead." 

16. On perusal of the same it appears that their Lordships in a clear language held that after the death of the Ordinance No.1 of 1969 with effect from 23.3.1974 there can be no proceeding relates to vested property. 

17. I have perused the decisions as referred by the learned Advocate for the opposite party. Admittedly as per the said decisions even after repeal of the Emergency Ordinance, 1965 a new Ordinance came namely Ordinance No.1 of 1969 and in the said Ordinance there is a clause that notwithstanding dissolution of the Emergency Ordinance of 1965 some provisions annexed in the said Ordinance of 1965 shall remain enforce under the Ordinance of 1969. But the learned Advocate failed to show us any such clause in the law by which the Ordinance 1 of 1969 was repealed. 

18. In view of the Judgment passed by our Apex Court, I am of the view that any proceeding by way of V.P. case or suit in a Civil Court so far it relates to declaration of any property as vested property is learned after 23.3.1974 i.e after repeal of the Ordinance 1 of 1969. In the instant case in hand admittedly the V.P. proceeding was initiated after the aforesaid date and as such the decree of declaration that the property in question is vested property passed by the lower Appellate Court is not sustainable in the eye of law. Furthermore, the plaintiff also miserably failed to proved that the defendant obtained the exparte decree by practicing fraud and collusively. Rather admittedly the same was passed within the knowledge of the plaintiff of the instant suit. 

19. Considering the facts and circumstances and the provision of law and the decisions as referred to I find substance in this Rule. Accordingly the Rule is made atisc2lute. The impugned judgment and decree passed by the Lower Appellate Court dated 3.11.1997 is hereby set aside. The judgment and decree passed by the trial Court is affirmed. 

20. Send down the L.C. record with a copy of this judgment at once.

End.

Ms. Nazmun Ara Sultana, J:- This Rule was issued calling in question the entire proceeding of Artha Execution Case No.1790 of 2003 of Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Chittagong and also the order No.32 dated 23.3.2004 and order No.41 dated 17.5.2005 passed in that Artha Execution Case. 

2. The facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of this rule, in short, are that the respondent No.3-P Public Bank Limited filed Money suit No.21 of 1983 before the Court of Subordinate Judge, 1'1 Court, Chittagong against this petitioner for recovery of loan money. The said suit was subsequently re-numbered as Money suit No.28 of 1984 and was decreed exparte by the judgment and order dated 14.7.1984. The decree holder bank then put that decree in execution in Money execution Case No.2 of 1984. This petitioner along with others filed a miscellaneous case being Misc. Case No. 62 of 1986 under order 9 rule 13 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside that exparte decree, but the said mist case was ultimately rejected by the order dated 14.12.1987. However the Money Execution Case No.2 of 1984 was subsequently dismissed for default by the order dated 3.10.1992. Thereafter on 8.2.99 the decree-holder bank filed a fresh execution case being Money Execution Case No.1 of 1999. The said money execution case No.1 of 1999 was subsequently transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat No.1, 1970 of 2003. In that Artha Execution Case No.1790 of 2003, on the prayer of the decree holder bank, the impugned order no.32 dated 23.3.2004 was passed issuing warrant of arrest against the petitioner. Thereafter, this petitioner appeared in that execution case and filed an application praying for rejection of the execution case on the ground of limitation and also for recalling the warrant of arrest issued against him. By the other impugned order no.41 dated 17.5.2005 the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat concerned rejected the said prayer of the petitioner. 

3. The petitioner thereafter has come to this court with this writ petition and obtained the rule. 

4. Mr. Shah Md. Munir Sharif, the learned advocate appearing, for the writ petitioner has mainly argued that the execution case in question is hopelessly barred by limitation and as such the entire proceeding as well as the impugned orders are illegal. To elaborate his argument the learned advocate has submitted that admittedly the decree in question was passed on 14.7.1984 and thereafter the 1st execution case was filed on 26.11.1984. This execution case was dismissed for default on 3.10.1992 and thereafter the execution case in question i.e. the 2nd execution case was filed on 8.2.1999. The learned advocate has pointed out that as per Article 182 of the Limitation Act this 2nd execution case had to be filed within 3 years from the date of dismissal of the 1st execution case and as per section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure within 12 years from the date of passing of the decree in order to save the limitation. The learned advocate has contended the since the 2nd execution case in question was filed long after expiry of 12 years from the date of passing of decree and also long after expiry of 3 years from the date of dismissal of the first execution case it is hopelessly barred by limitation. 

5. We have considered the argument of the learned advocate for the petitioner and examined the Writ petition and the papers annexed thereto. Admittedly the present execution case was filed long 8 years after dismissal of the 1st execution case and long 16 years after passing of the decree. The learned advocate appearing for the respondent No.3 decree-holder bank also has frankly conceded this fact that the execution case in question has not been filed within the time prescribed in Article 182 of the Limitation Act and in section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure. So, in this circumstances without any further discussion it may be said that the execution case in question being hopelessly barred by limitation is unlawful and as such the impugned orders passed in this execution case also are of no legal effect. 

6. In the circumstances the rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. It is declared that the proceeding of Artha Execution Case No.1, Chittagong as well as the order No.32 dated 23.3.2004 and the order no.41 dated 17.5.2005 passed in that Artha Execution Case are unlawful and of no legal effect. 

End.

M. Md. Abdul Matin , J:- This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 11.01.2004 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.2727 of 2000 making the Rule absolute preferred against judgment and order dated 21.01.1996 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, 
First Court, Chittagong in Mortgage Suit No.33 of 1991 for removing errors of the final decree not done in accordance with the preliminary decree. 

2. The facts, in short, are that the respondents and the United Commercial Bank Limited preferred the above Writ Petition No.2727 of 2000 under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh before the High Court Division and on hearing on the 21st day of May, 2000 the High Court Division was pleased to issue Rule Nisi calling upon the respondents petitioner to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 21.01.1996 (Annexed as Annexure-A to the Writ Petition No.2727 of 2000) passed by the respondent No.1 shall not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and or such other or further order or orders passed as to the High Court Division may seem fit and proper. The High Court Division was also pleased to stay further proceedings of Mortgage Suit No.33 of 1991 pending before the Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong. 

3. In the meantime the petitioner appeared in the above matter (Writ Petition No.2727 of 2000) by filing power through their respective lawyer and ultimately on 11.01.2004 by judgment and order passed by another Division Bench the Rule issued was made absolute. 

4. The writ petitioner respondent filed Mortgage Suit No.33 of 1991 in the Court of learned 1st Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong against the petitioner and others for realization of Tk.73,63,612.50 which was subsequently made an amount of Tk.67;90,120.06 as per banks subsequent account statement submitted and a preliminary decree was passed on condition for re-accounting and re-calculation of simple interest at the rate of 18% per annum with specific direction that the amount ascertained on such re- calculation and after adjustment of payment made by the petitioner to the respondent during pendency of the said matter the petitioner shall pay rest of the amount (if any) within one year in different installments enjoying waver of interest during the pendency of the Mortgage Suit No.33 of 1991. Thereafter the writ petitioner respondent on practicing fraud upon the court and also suppressing the terms, conditions and observations of the preliminary decree regarding re-calculation of interest and adjustment of the payment made by the petitioner during pendency of the Mortgage suit obtained the final decree dated 23.10.1994 contrary to the provisions provided in the preliminary decree dated 29.11.1992. 

5. After obtaining the above final decree on practicing fraud respondent filed Mortgage Decree Execution Case No.44 of 1994 in the same court for an amount of Tk.1,31,69,877.30 and started the proceeding for auction sale of the mortgage property in spite of the petitioners repayment of a total sum of amount Tk.70. lacs to the respondent duly authenticated (certified) by court against the decreetal amount Tk.67,90,120.66 subject to re-calculation of simple interest @ 18% per annum. The amount ascertained after re-calculation is payable within one year. In addition to above suffering of the petitioner company during pendency of the above Mortgage Suit, Mortgage Decree Execution Case and also the Miscellaneous Appeal before the High Court Division the respondent bank on colourable exercise of administrative power prejudiced the petitioner .company by way of imposing embargo on their normal trade with other schedule bank through Credit Information Bureau (CIB) report of Bangladesh Bank suspending all Bank facilities of the petitioner company although they are not responsible for the abnormal delay apart from substantial payment made by the petitioner company. Copy of the letter of Janata Bank stating the embargo on trading and transaction of normal activity with other banks through Credit Information Bureau of Bangladesh Bank was also annexed with the application made before the High Court Division. 

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the ex-parte final decree and also due to the illegal claim of Tk.1,31,69,377.06 by Mortgage Decree Execution Case No.44 of 1994 the petitioner for ensuring justice by way of legal rectification of errors committed in the final decree and also Mortgage Decree Execution Case due to practice of fraud upon the writ petitioner Bank, the petitioner company preferred a petition under Sections 151/152 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the final decree and also staying the execution proceeding and on hearing both the parties Artha Rin Adalat passed the order (impugned order dated 21.01.1996) setting aside the final decree dated 23.10.1994 and also directed the writ petitioner Bank to submit a current statement on the recalculation of interest @ 18% per annum in the light of preliminary decree by 27.02.1996. 

7. The writ petitioner respondent Bank being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the above order dated 21.01.1996 preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No.30 of 1996 before the High Court Division and also for the order of stay. Ultimately the High Court Division by the judgment dated 12th December, 1999 passed in the above Miscellaneous Appeal No.30 of 1996 dismissed the said Miscellaneous Appeal being not maintainable in law. Thereafter the respondent Bank filed the writ petition and by the impugned judgment the High Court Division made the Rule absolute and set aside the judgment and order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat setting aside the final decree. As against the judgment of the High Court Division the petitioners have filed this petition for leave to appeal. 

8. Heard the learned Counsel and perused the petition and the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other papers on record. 

9. It appears that after a final decree was passed against the petitioners they had specific remedy under the law but instead they filed a petition under Sections 151/152 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the trial court wrongly allowed the same and the High Court Division has rightly set aside that order and rightly held that the petitioners had no remedy under Sections 151/152 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The High Court Division has rightly found that the respondent No.1 acted without jurisdiction in passing the impugned order allowing the prayer for setting aside the final decree under Sections 151/152 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

10. We find that the High Court Division has rightly decided the point in issue and committed no error of law or procedure. Section 151 cannot be invoked when specific provision is there in Code of Civil Procedure or any other law against the decree and Section 152 is only meant for correcting arithmetical errors or clerical mistakes and was wrongly invoked in this case by the trial court which has; been rightly corrected by the High Court Division. 

We find no substance in this petition which is accordingly dismissed. 

End.

Mr. Abdis Salam Mamun, J.: This Rule was issued calling upon the Opposite Parties to show cause as to why the impugned if their No.18 dated 11.4.1992 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Jagannathpur, in the Title Execution Case No.1 of 1991 should not be set aside.

2. Facts leading to the issuance of this Rule are that the Petitioner as Plaintiff instituted the Title Suit No.227 of 1962 in the Court of the Munsif, Sunamgonj on 14.12.1962 against the predecessors of the present Opposite Parties praying for .a decree for declaration of title in the suit land and for recovery for its khas possession. The suit was decreed on 30.5.1963 ex parte. 

The Plaintiff-Petitioner thereafter filed the Title Execution Case No.26 of 1965 on 6.7.1965. 

On 7.9.1965 a Miscellaneous Case, being No.42 of 1965 was filed by one Syed Enamul Hoq under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the suit ex-parte decree on the ground that it was passed against him during his minority and in that Miscellaneous case, the Petitioner obtained an order staying all proceeding of the Title Execution 77.case No.26 of 1965. 

In December, 1966, one Syeda Lutfunnessa and two others instituted the Title Suit No.255 of 1966 against the Petitioner and 17 others praying for a decree for declaration of their rights and title in the jote and that part of the suit land was covered by the decree of the Title Suit. No. 227 of 1962 also praying for confirmation of their possession with a further prayer for declaration of the ex-parte decree dated 30.5.1963 passed in the Title Suit No. 227 of 1962 is void, illegal and not binding upon the Plaintiffs and also for permanent injunction restraining of Defendants from evicting the Plaintiffs from the suit land. 

By order dated 12.4.1967, passed in the Title Suit No. 225 of 1966, the decree-holder of the Title Suit No. 227 of 1962, i-e the Petitioner was restrained from taking over possession of the suit land by virtue of the decree passed in the Title Suit No. 227 of 1962 until further order. 

In November, 1966, the Petitioner of the Miscellaneous Case No.42 of 1965, Syed Enamul Hoq filed an application praying for dismissal of the Miscellaneous Case on the grounds of fraud and misrepresentation. stating that the case was filed in his name showing him minor, but in fact, he is a major and he did not file the Miscellaneous Case and is not willing to proceed with the case and upon the application, the. Miscellaneous Case No.42 of 1965 was' dismissed.

Though in the Title Suit No. 225 of 1966, an order of injunction was passed restraining the Decree-Holder of the Title Suit No. 227 of 1962, from taking over possession until further order, but the executing Court passed an order in the Title Execution Case No. 26 of 1965 (Arising out of Title Suit No. 227 of 1962) On 6.6.1967 as follows: "The case is taken up today. As the Miscellaneous Case No.42 of 1965 had been disposed of in the month of November 1966, so the case is to be proceed with Requisites kept in the record. Decree-Holder to furnish Boat hire by 10.6.1967." And thereafter, the Execution Case was dismissed for default on 20.1.1968. According to the petitioner, the order for dismissal of the Execution case for default was an illegal order, passed without jurisdiction and is void ab initio. 

On the other hand, the Title Suit No. 255 of 1966 was decreed on 29.3.1968 declaring that the Plaintiffs are co-sharers to the extent of 19/(5 )pies of share in the suit land and also declaring their joint possession. 

The Petitioner then preferred an Appeal being the Title Appeal No.143 of 1968 against the said judgment and decree dated 29.3.1968 passed in the Title Suit No.255 of 1966. 

On 21.3.1969 the Title Appeal No. 143 of 1968 was allowed in part by the judgment and decree passed by the Learned Appellate Court, modifying the decree passed by the trial court upon setting aside the decree for joint possession, holding that the appellant i-e. the present petitioner is in exclusive possession of the suit land and holding further that the Respondents-Plaintiffs will be at liberty to enter into possession to the extent of their share in the suit land through a suit for partition. 

The Plaintiffs-Respondents have thereafter, preferred the Second Appeal No.614 of 1969 before the High Court at Dhaka against the said judgment and decree dated 21.3.1969 passed in the Title ...Appeal No. 143 of 1968 and during pendency of the said Second Appeal, further proceeding of the Title Execution Case No. 26 of 1965 was stayed at the instance of the appellants in the Civil Rule No. 920(S) of 1969. 

The Second Appeal No. 614 of 1969 was dismissed on 27.5.1968 on hearing and the decree thereof was drawn up on 12.2.1987. 

The Plaintiffs-Appellants have thereafter preferred the Civil Petition for Special Leave of Appeal No.211 of 1987 before the Appellate Division of the Bangladesh Supreme Court against the judgment and decree dated 27.5.1986 passed in the Second Appeal No. 614 of 1969. 

The Civil Petition for Special Leave to Appeal No.211 of 1 987 was dismissed on 4.6.1990. 

On 23.3.1991 the petitioner filed the Title Execution Case No.1 of 1991 praying for the self-same relief, as it was prayed for, in the Title Execution Case No.26 of 1965. 

On 1.12.1991 the judgment-debtor No. 1(Ka) filed an application in the Title Execution Case No.1 of 1991 under section 151 of the Code of Civil procedure praying for dismissal of the Execution Case on the ground of limitation. 

On 18.1.1992, the judgment-debtor No.1(Ka) filed an application intimating the Court that he will not contest the Execution Case and thus, by order dated 18.1.1992, the Learned Munsif has been pleased to restrain the judgment-debtor No. 1(Ka) from contesting the Execution proceeding. 

On 27.1.1992 the judgment-debtor No. 2(Kha) filed another application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for dismissal of the Execution Case on the ground of limitation. The decree-holder filed an objection to the application and by the impugned order, the Learned Munsif has been pleased to dismiss the Title Execution Case No.1 of 199 1 on the ground of limitation. 

3. The Decree-Holder has thereafter preferred this application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the instant Rule on 19.7.1992 on the grounds that the order dated 20,1.1968 passed in the Title Execution Case No. 26 of 1965 is neither final order nor it was sustainable in law. The Learned Munsif has committed an error in law by not treating the subsequent application for execution, in substance, to be one for revival or continuation of the original application of the Title Execution Case No.26 of 1965 and thus, there was no question of limitation. The Learned Munsif has also erred in law in not computing the period of limitation from 4.6.1990, the date on which, the Civil Petition for Special Leave of Appeal No: 211 of 1987 was dismissed. 

4. Dr. Naim Ahmed, the Learned Advocate, appearing for the Petitioner, after placing the impugned order submits that the Title Execution Case No.26 of 1965 was purported to be dismissed on 20.1.1968 on a date on which an order of injunction was in force over it issued in the Title Suit No.255 of 1966 also restraining the decree-holder from taking over possession of the suit land and as such the said order of dismissal is illegal., inoperative and void ab initio and cannot be treated as a judicial order and consequently, the Title Execution Case Noll of 1991 is merely a petition for revival or continuation of the original execution petition and not for starting an Execution Case afresh. 

Relying upon the cases of Government of Rajsthan and another Vs. Sangram Singh and others, reported in AIR 1962 Raj (FB) 43, Chhatter Singh Vs. Kamal Singh, reported in. AIR 1927 All (FB) 16 and Shah Newaz Ebne Mostaque and others Vs. Shah Alam and others, reported in 55 DLR (AD) 69, the learned Advocate submits that an Execution application must be deemed to be pending so long as no final order disposing of it judicially has been passed thereupon. A subsequent application in such a case for execution will be deemed to be one merely for the continuation or revival of the original proceeding and where the circumstances are such that the decree-holder can ask for a revival of an earlier proceeding, even an application, which is in form one for execution, will be considered to be one for revival or continuation of earlier proceeding and that the decree holder is not required to file an application for proceeding with the pending execution case as it is the duty of the Court to proceed with the same suo motu. Such a pending execution case is not hit by limitation. 

The Learned Advocate further submits that the Learned Munsif in dismissing Execution case has erred in law in holding that the order passed in the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal is not a decree, in .view of the provisions of the Article 182(2) of the Limitation Act, which according to the Learned Advocate, also includes a 'final order'. The Order dated 4.6.1990 is a judgment passed on merit in which the Appellate Division has observed that 'the subsequent Title Suit No.255 of 1966 was filed to •deprive the Plaintiff of the Title Suit No.227 of 1962 and with a view to reap the benefit of the decree obtained against the trespasser', and as such, the Learned Advocate contends, it was a final order within the meaning of Article 182(2) of the Limitation Act. 
The Learned Advocate has further placed his reliance upon the Case of Shamuj Ali and others Vs. Kalarma Bibi and others, reported in 33 DLR (AD) 10.1 where their Lordships held that "It is an intelligible rule that so long as there is any question sub-judice between any of the parties, those affected shall not be compelled to pursue the so often through the thorny path of execution, which. if the final result is against them may lead to no advantage." 

5. Mr. A. S. Md. Abdul Mobin, the learned Advocate appearing for the Opposite Party has, on the other hand, submitted that the final order in the instant case, was one which was passed in the Second Appeal by the High Court Division on 27.5.1986 and the filing of the Civil Petition for Special Leave to Appeal shall not be excluded from computation of limitation, for, in the case of Rupai Vs. Goshain Ram Chanrda Das, reported in AIR 1952 All 391 it was held that "There is a distinction between an application for Leave to Appeal to the Privy Council and the Appeal itself. Hence the date of dismissal of an application for leave to appeal to the Privy Council even it files along with the memorandum of the proposed appeal to the Privy Council cannot be taken into account as making the commencement of the limitation for the execution application." 

In this connection, the Learned Advocate has also relied upon the case of Comilla Banking Co-operation Ltd. Vs. Nanda Kumar Bhattacharjee, reported in PLD 1951 Dacca 130 where it was held that "Appeal-refers to appeal from decree or order sought to be executed and does not include appeal in a collateral proceeding e.g. km] an order refusing to set aside ex-parte decree." 

5. Perused the application, heard the Learned Advocates and considered their submissions. 

The impugned Order is as follows: 

	“আদেশ নং-১৮, তারিখ ১১/৪/১৯৯২ ইং।
		অদ্য নথি আদেশের জন্য নেওয়া হইল। 

	ইহা স্বত্ব জারী ১/৯১ নং মোকদ্দমা তামাদিতে বারিত এই দাবীতে আনীত দরখাস্ত। 
	২(খ) নং দায়ীকের দাখিলী দরখাস্তের সংক্ষিপ্ত বিবরণঃ-

অত্র জারীর মোকদ্দমা আইনত অচল ও বারীত। ডিকীদারের দাখিলী ডিক্রীতে সেটেলমেন্ট জরিপীদাগ খতিয়ানের উল্লেখ না থাকায় তাহা সনাক্ত যোগ্য নয় বিধায় উক্ত ডিক্রী জারীর যোগ্য নয়। ডিক্রীদারের অত্র দরখাস্ত তামাদী আইনের ৩ ধারা ও ১৮২ অনুচ্ছেদ এবং দেঃ কার্যবিধি আইনের ৪৮ ধারা মোতাবেক বারিত বিধায় অত্র মোকদ্দমা খারিজ যোগ্য। ডিক্রিদার দায়ীকে এই বক্তব্যকে অস্বীকার করিয়া দায়িকের তামাদিতে বারিত মর্মে আনিত দরখাস্তের বিরুদ্ধে লিখিত আপত্তি উত্থাপন করেন। ডিক্রীদারের লিখিত আপত্তির মুদ্দা কথা হইল ডিক্রীদার আইনের বর্ণিত সময়ের মধ্যে অত্র মোকদ্দমা আনয়ন করিয়াছেন। ডিক্রীদারের মোকদ্দমা তামাদিতে বারিত নয়। বিধায় দায়িকের লিখিত আপত্তি খারিজযোগ্য। 

এখন আদালতকে এই সিদ্ধান্তে উপনীত হইতে হইবে যে, অত্র স্বত্ব জারীর মোকদ্দমা তামাদিতে বারিত কিনা?

২(খ) নং দায়িকের আনীত দরখাস্ত এবং ইহার বিরুদ্ধে ডিক্রীদারের লিখিত আপত্তি গভীর ভাবে পর্যালোচনা ও  পর্যবেক্ষণ করিলাম। দায়িকের দরখাস্ত এবং ডিক্রীদারের উক্ত দরখাস্তের বিরুদ্ধে উত্থাপিত আপত্তি হইতে ইহা স্বীকৃত যে ডিক্রীদার দায়িকের পিতা জৈন উল্ল্যা গংদের বিরুদ্ধে সুনামগুঞ্জ মুন্সেফী আদালতে দাখিলী ২২৭/৬২ ইংরেজী মোকদ্দমায় গত ৩০/৫/৬৩ ইংরেজী তারিখে এক তরফা রায় ও ডিক্রী হয়। 

ইহা প্রথম পক্ষগণ কর্তৃক স্বীকৃত যে, দায়িক উক্ত ডিক্রীজারীর জন্য বিগত ৬/৭/৭৫ ইং তারিখে ২৬/৬৫ নং ডিক্রীর জারীর মোকদ্দমা দায়ের করেন। ইহা স্বীকৃত যে, স্বত্ব ২২৭/৬২ ইং মোকদ্দমার বিরুদ্ধে দেঃ কাঃ বিধি আইনের ৯ আদেশের ১৩ নিয়মে আনীত বাজে মোকদ্দমা নং-৪২/৬৫ তে উক্ত স্বত্ব মোকদ্দমার ২২৭৬২ মোকদ্দমার কার্য্যক্রম স্থগিত রাখা হয়। ইহাও স্বীকৃত যে, বাজে ৪২/৬৫ মোকদ্দমা ১৯৯৬ সালের নভেম্বর মাসে খারিজ হইয়া যায়। ইহাও পক্ষগণ কর্তৃক স্বীকৃত যে, একই আদালতে স্বত্ব ২২৭/৬২ নং মোকদ্দমা একতরফা রায় ও ডিক্রী অকার্যকরী ও অন্যান্য দাবীতে স্বত্ব ২৫৫/৬৬ একই আদালতে দায়ের করা হয়।

 (7) Date of payment fixed by the decree."

Now the question is arises does the Judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division in the Second Appeal finally dispose of the rights of the parties when a petition for Leave to Appeal was preferred thereafter and pending before the Appellate Division? What would happen if the Leave was granted and Appeal allowed? Thus the principle of law accepted by their Lordships in Shamaj Ali's case is equally applicable in the instant Case. 

The rights and liabilities of the parties to the suit is not finally determined if a petition for Special Leave to Appeal is pending before the Appellate Division.

In the Case of Rupai Vs. Goshain Ram Charandas, AIR 1952 All 391 their Lordships have partially considered the Case. of Nagendranath, supra, and arrived at the decision that : "the date of the final order passed on the application for Leave of appeal cannot be taken into account as \ marking the commencement of the period I limitation for an application for execution". Facts of the instant case are distinguishable from those of the reported case and the principle enunciated in Samuj Ali's Case, supra, is binding in 1 view of the legal position that foreign Ruling is only -persuasive and the instant Ruling is from a Division Bench. 

10. In the instant Case, the litigation started between the parties on 14.12.1962 upon institution of the Title Suit No.227 of 1962 in the 'Court of the Munsif Sunamganj and its exparte decree on 30.5.1963 and reached to its finality on 4.6.1990 upon dismissal of Civil Petition fro Special Leave to Appeal No.211 of 1987.  

11. Under Article 103 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh an appeal lies to the Appellate Division from a Judgment, decree. Order or sentence of 'the High Court Division in the manner enumerated therein. 

Under Section 109 (a) of the Civil Procedure Code, appeals lies to the Supreme Court from any judgment, decree of final order passed on appeal by like High Court. 

12. In the Case of Krishnaswami Vs. Council of C.A. reported in Air 1953 / Madras 79 it was held that The right of appeal under section 109 C.P.C. being subject to the limitation of Article 133 (ours Article 103), must be a civil proceeding in which the order complained of is passed." 

13. The pertinent question in this case, is also: Whether a party can derive any benefit on the basis of an illegal order passed in a proceeding in violation of the provisions of law. 

The order of dismissal passed in the Execution Case No.26 of 1966, was admittedly passed at a time when there was an order of stay in force on the execution proceeding and as such, the order of dismissal was passed in utter violation of law and efface illegal and the Opposite Party is not entitled to reap any benefit out of the said illegal order. 

Since it was not a judicial order, yield no result. 

The subsequent execution petition was filed within the prescribed time from the date of Judgment and order passed in the Leave Petition was in fact a petition for revival of the Execution Case No.26 of 1966 that was pending and stayed, irrespective of its illegal order of dismissal (Government of Rajasthan Vs. Sangram Singh, AIR 1962, FB, Raj, 48). In view of the citations of the Case of Chattar. Singh Vs. Kamal Singh, AIR 1927, ALL (FB) 16 and Shah Newaj Vs. Shah Alam, 55 DLR (AD) 69 it could not be deemed to be a fresh application for execution of the decree. 

14. In the case of Bangladesh Jatiya Samabaya Bank Ltd. Vs. Sangbad Daily Paper and others, reported in 36 DLR (AD) 5 and relied upon by the Learned Assistant Judge, the money Suit in question, was decreed on 23.12.1958 and the Money Execution Case was thereafter filed which was disposed of on 13.1.1961. On 12.6.1969 another Money Execution Case was filed by the decree-holder to execute the money decree dated 23.12.1958, execution petition of which was disposed of on 13.1.1961, taking the ground of 12 years limitation, as has been laid down under Section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure, where the Learned Advocate for the Plaintiff-decree-holder, at the time of hearing, himself conceded that the 2nd Execution petition was barred from either side. 

The instant case is distinguishable both from facts and law. 

15. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. 

The impugned Order No.18 dated 11.4.1992 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Jagannathpur, in the Title Execution Case No.1 of 1.991 is hereby set aside and the Execution Case No.26 of 1966 is restored to its file and number on the basis of the application filed, upon which the Execution case No.1 of 1991 was started. 

The learned Assistant Judge, Jagannathpur is directed to proceed with the Title Execution Case No.26 of 1966 from the stage where it was pending before the order of stay was passed. 

Inform the Court Concerned. 

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.108 of 1993
lawyer:
For the Petitioner: Mr. Mahbubey Alam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. A.K.M. Shahidul Huq, Advocate -on-record.

Versus
