full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Ruhul Amin. J:- This is a petition for restoration of the aforementioned civil petition for leave to appeal which was dismissed on June 21, 1998 for default on the representation of the learned Advocate-on-record for the petitioner that he had no instruction to proceed with the petition for leave to appeal. The petition for leave to appeal was filed against the judgment dated August 3, 1992 in First Miscellaneous Appeal No.75 of 1983 dismissing the same. The First Miscellaneous Appeal was filed against the judgment and decree dated May 22, 1983 of the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) passed in Title Suit No.467 of 1982 making the award Rule of the Court. There is a dispute over the ownership, of the building in plot Nos.115-120 of Motijheel Commercial Area between the petitioner and the Jiban Bima Corporation and over that suits were filed by both the parties. In the afore state of the matter the authority took decision to get the dispute between the petitioner and the Respondent resolved by a sole Arbitrator and following that decision sole Arbitrator was appointed and finally sole Arbitrator made award on August 29, 1993 in favour of the Respondent. Thereupon the petitioner filed objection under sections 30 and 33 of the Arbitration Act, 1940 seeking setting aside of the award and thereupon Title Suit No.423 of 1982 was registered. The sole Arbitrator filed the award in the Court along with an application under section 14(2) of the Arbitration Act, 1940 (hereinafter the Act) to make the award Rule of the Court and thereupon Title Suit No.467 of 1982 of the 3"a Court of Subordinate Judge was registered. The Court decreed the Title Suit No.467 of 1982 ex-pane on May 22, 1983. The Respondent i.e. Jiban Bima Corporation filed Execution Case No.33 of 1983, that while the petitioner came to know about the exparte decree on October 6, 1983, it filed an application under Order 9, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure whereupon Miscellaneous Case No.780 of 1983 was registered, for setting aside of the ex-parse decree dated May 22, 1983. The said Miscellaneous Case was dismissed on September 30, 1984. The petitioner as against the ex-parte decree filed Miscellaneous Appeal No.75 of 1983 and as against the order rejecting the Miscellaneous case (under Order 9, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure) filed Miscellaneous Appeal No.188 of 1984. In Title Suit No.423 of 1982 an application under Order 7, Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed and the same having been rejected the Respondent moved the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No.762 of 1986, that Miscellaneous Appeal No.188 of 1984 was Converted into Civil Revision No.1526 of 1990. The High Court Division dismissed the Miscellaneous Appeal No.75 of 1983 and discharged the Rule in Civil Revision No.1526 of 1990. The petitioner filed petition for leave to appeal only against the judgment passed in First Miscellaneous Appeal No.75 of 1983. As stated hereinbefore the said petition for leave to appeal was dismissed for default since the learned Advocate-on-record represented to the Court that he had no instruction to proceed with the petition for leave to appeal. The petition for restoration of the petition for Leave to Appeal No.108 of 1993 which was dismissed on June 21, 1998 was filed on April II, 2002 stating that the petitioner did not orally or in writing give instruction to the learned Advocate-on-record not to proceed with the petition for leave to appeal and that because of the dismissal of the petition for leave to appeal the petitioner has suffered irreparable loss and injury and as such it is necessary to set aside the order of dismissal and to restore the petition for leave to appeal to its original file and number. 

2. Since the petition filed seeking restoration of the petition for leave to appeal was out of time by 1387 days the petitioner along with the application for restoration filed an application seeking condonation of delay. In the petition seeking condonation of delay it has been stated that before March 16, 2002 they had no knowledge about the dismissal of the petition for leave to appeal. It has been stated that in the Inter Ministerial meeting of the Ministry of Jute and the Ministry of Commerce the. Respondent disclosed about the dismissal of the petition for leave to appeal and thereupon on April 10, 2002 application for the certified copy of the order of dismissal was filed and got the same on that date and filed the petition on the following day. It has been stated that delay in filing the petition for leave to appeal was unintentional and due to the reasons beyond the control of the petitioner. In paragraph 3 of the petition for condonation of delay it has been stated that the petitioner used to inquire of the learned Advocate-on-record regularly about the position of the leave petition and the petitioner was informed by the learned Advocate-on-record that the leave petition awaiting hearing. In the background of the aforesaid statement of the petitioner the accusation against the learned Advocate-on-record that he at no point of time disclosed to the petitioner about the dismissal of the leave petition appears to be not genuine. Since in our view there was no reason for the learned Advocate-on-record while the petitioner inquired of him about the position of the leave petition not to give the state of the leave petition or that not to tell the petitioner about the disposal of the leave petition in the manner as stated hereinbefore. In the afore state of the matter we are of the view explanation offered seeking condonation of delay is not convincing and satisfactory. 

3. Accordingly the application for restoration is rejected being barred. 

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No.631 of 2008
lawyer:
For the Petitioner: Mr. Md. Omar Ali Khan, Advocate, (appeared with the leave of the Court), instructed by Mr. Nurul Islam, Advocate-on-Record. 
Respondents: Not represented.
parties:
Chairman, Mymensingh Pourashava, Mymensingh ----- Petitioner
Versus
Kasimonnessa Bewa and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Abdul Aziz, J:- This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 31.10.2007 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3851 of 2000 making the rule absolute arising out of judgment and order dated 14.06.2000 passed by the learned additional district Judge; 41h Court, Mymensingh in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 24 of 1997 reversing those of dated 30.10.1996 passed by the learned subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge). 1st Court, Mymensingh in Miscellaneous Case No. 123 of 1993 dismissing the same. 

2. Facts of the case, in short, are that, the predecessor of the plaintiff-respondent instituted Title Suit No. 71 of 1983 before the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 1st Court, Mymensingh for partition and declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of the suit land described in the schedule of the plaint against the respondents and after filing the suit summons were duly served upon the defendants and defendant Nos. 55 and ,56 appeared With Vokalathnama and contested the suit by filing written statement and defendant Nos.1-15 and 30 appeared with Vokalathnama and contested the suit by filing an application for separate 'Saham' and thereafter the defendant Nos.30 and 55 (Ka)- 55(Uma)-56 amicably settled the matter out of Court and filed a Solenama for `Sahara' and the learned trial Court accordingly passed a preliminary decree and the said Solenama was treated as a part of final decree by his judgment and decree dated 05.05.1993 and 18-05-1993 respectively.

3. Defendant-petitioner No.54 as petitioner filed an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of the Code of civil Procedure registered Miscellaneous Case No.123 of 1993 on 04.08.1993 against the said judgment and decree passed ex-parte against him before the trial Court stating, inter-alia, that the summons of the suit was not lawfully served upon him and the plaintiff obtained the decree ex-prate against him in collusion with some staff of the Pourashava showing the summon duly served upon him and in collusion with the defendant Nos. 30,55(ka) to 55 (Uma) and 56 filing a solenama before the trial Court. His further case is that one Mir Masan Abdullah shoyeb tenant of the Pourashava came to know about the ex-parte decree and on his information he took the certified copy of the same through his learned Advocate and filed the case.

 4. The plaintiff- respondents opposed the case by filing written objections denying the allegations brought in the application contending, inter-alia, that summons was duly served upon the defendant-petitioner through Process Server, etc.

5. Trial Court dismissed the case on consideration of evidence of the witnesses examined by both the parties and materials on record. Being aggrieved, the defendant-petitioner preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 24 of 1997 before the leaned District Judge, Mymensingh. The learned Additional District Judge, 4th court, Mymensingh on transfer heard and allowed the appeal on contest reversing the judgment and order of the trial court. Plaintiff-respondent Nos. 1-16 moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3851 against the same and° the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division by his judgment and order made the Rule absolute setting aside the judgment and order passed by the appellate Court below. Hence this petition for leave to appeal at the instance of the defendant petitioner No. 54. 

6. Mr. Md. Omar All Khan, the learned Advocate (appeared with the leave of the Court) for the petitioner assailed the impugned judgment and order on the ground that the High Court Division misread. Misconceived and misinterpreted the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record and has committed an error of law resulting in an error in decision occasioning failure of justice and. as such the impugned judgment and order is not tenable in the eye law. He further submits that the plaintiff did not comply the mandatory provision of Section 152 of the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 in filing the suit against the Pourashava without serving notice there under, but the High Court Division failed to consider the same and thereby committed an error of law lie also submits that the high court Division failed to consider that the have appellate Court Correctly found that the summons were not duly served upon the defendant-petitioner in allowing the appeal and has thus committed an error in passing the impugned judgment and order reversing the appellate Court judgment and order.

7. We have heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner and perused the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court division and also those of the Courts below. 

8. An ex-parte decree can be set aside under Rule 13. Order 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure if it is found that the notice upon the defendant was not properly served. But in the instant case, it appears that the summons was duly served in the office of the Pourashava and the peon of the Pourashava received the same and his name and address was noted in the original, summon. Trial court also found that the Process server while deposing as P.W.2 admitted the same. It was also stated in the application tiled under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code by the petitioner that office peon of the Pourashava is appointed only to receive postal documents and summons on behalf of the Pourashava. Evidence shows he received the same on 15.06.1983 and it to the concerned authority.

9. In due consideration of the above, trial Court rejected the Miscellaneous case but the appellate Court below on erroneous view set aside the order of the trial court allowing the appeal which has rightly reversed by the High Court Division on positive finding to the above effect on proper consideration of the evidence. Whether the suit is maintainable or not due to non complying the mandatory provision of section 152 of the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 is a matter relating to maintainability of the suit itself and deserves no consideration in disposing either the application filed under Order. 9 Rule 13 of the code of Civil Procedure or the instant petition.

10. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petition but find no substance. The leave-petition is accordingly dismissed having no merit. 

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No.749-50 of 2008
lawyer:
For the Petitioners: Mr. Arun Kumar Bhathacharjee (In both the Cases), Advocate (appeared with the leave of the Court), instructed by Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas, Advocate-on-Record. 
For the Respondent Nos.1-3: (In both the Cases) Mr. Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record. 
For the Respondent Nos.4-54: Not Represented (In both the Cases)
parties:
Sakat Ali Gazi and others ----- Petitioners (in C.P. No.749/08)
Mozahar Moral and others ----- Petitioners (in C.P. No.750/08)
Versus
Mr. Abdur Razzaque and others ----- Respondents (in both the cases)
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Abdul Aziz, J: The petitioners sought leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 07.02.2008 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.5381 of 2004 and Civil Revision No.5382 of 2004 making both the Rules absolute reversing the judgment and decree dated 11.10.2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Jessore in Title Appeal No. 126 of 2001 and Title Appeal No.95 of 2001 allowing the appeals reversing those of dated 09.08.2001 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Jessore in Title Suit No. 179 of 1993 decreeing the suit in part. 

2. Both the petitions for leave to appeal arose out of the common judgment and order dated 07-02-2008 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.5381 of 2004 and Civil Revision No.5382 of 2004 making the Rules absolute and common questions of law being involved in both petitions, the same are disposed of by this judgment. 

3. The facts, leading to these petitions, in short, are that the respondent Nos.1-3 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.179 of 1993 in the Court of the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Jessore for partition to the suit land alleging, inter-alia, that the suit land belonged to Danu Moral before C.S. operation, who married twice and out the first marriage, he two sons namely, Budhai and Tofel and one daughter Kulsum Bibi and on the death of his first wife, he married Panthi Bibi, who had a son named Panchu by her previous husband. The said Panthi Bibi took Panchu to the house of Danu Moral on her marriage with Danu Moral and Panchu was not a son of Danu Moral and on the death of Danu, the said Panchu did not inherit anything from him and one Hasho Bepari was the father of Panchu. Totel died leaving behind his brother Budhai and sister Kulsum died leaving behind her son Khadem Sarder, Panchu Moral died leaving behind his only son Jongal Moral and during C. S. operation, the land of C. S. Khatian No.254 was recorded in the names of Bank and Khadem Sarder in equal shares and Jongal Moral being elder in age to Khadem and Bank got his name recorded in the C. S. Khatian No.293 to the extent of one anna and in C. S. Khatian No. 112 to the extent of four annas share and Barik Moral died leaving behind Khadem Sarder as his sole heir. Thereafter, the said Khadem Sarder died leaving behind. Hazer Sarder who in turn died leaving sons the plaintiffs as his heirs Jongal Moral filed Title Suit No:314 of 1966 claiming the suit property as successive heir of Danu Moral but the same was dismissed on contest and one Surat All Gazi brought Title Suit No. 107 of 1992 against the plaintiffs and the same was dismissed on 01.03.1993 and Bank Moral did not surrender tenancy right to his landlord and so-called deed of Kubuliyat is void and not acted upon and the deeds dated 26.11.1953, 11.05.1960, 11.10.1961, 09.11.1969, 27.11.1967 and 03.12.1968 were equally void and in effective and there was no partition of the suit land by metes and bounds among the co-sharers and the plaintiffs demanded partition of the suit land as the defendants refused to go for amicable partition and hence the suit.

 4. Two sets of written statements were filed by defendants No.1-5 and other one by defendant Nos. 18 and 20, jointly and defendant Nos. 16 and 17 by accepting their written statement contested the suit. Their case, in brief, inter-alia, is that before the C. S. record, Danu alias Danej Moral was the sole owner of the disputed land in respect of 'Ka' schedule land and before the C. S. record, Danu Moral had two sons and one daughter and a wife and Panchu was the son of Panthi Bibi and Danu Moral and not the step son of Danu and Panchu acquired the property according to his share. Before C. S. operation Panchu died leaving behind his son Jongal, Budhai died leaving behind a son Bank and in this way Jongal acquired 12 gondas, Bank acquired 12 gondas and Khadem acquired 16 gondas share. During the period of S. A. operation, the responsibility, of recording was shifted upon Khadem, who did not record the names of Jongal although Jongal was the owner of the eight annas share and Jongal used to possess the share by erecting houses and established some portion as burial ground, he transferred VD. some land and delivered possession to defendants. Defendant No.18 established a Rice Mill in the plot and Khadem and Barik were possessing the respective share and Jongal sold a portion of the land to Sabirannessa by a registered deed dated 26.11.1953 and delivered possession in her favour and also some land to the defendant Nos.16 and 17 and to one Noor Islam and delivered possession in their favour, who surrendered the land in favour of the landlords. Thereafter, the said Jongal Moral took settlement and plaintiffs have mentioned in the suit land that Panchu Moral was not the son of Danu Moral and this was done with a view to grab the land and. the plaintiffs have no right, title and interest in the suit land and thus the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

5. The learned Senior Assistant Judge upon hearing the parties decreed the suit in part on 09.08.2001. Against which, the defendant Nos.16-18 and 20 filed Title Appeal No.126 of 2001 and the defendant Nos.1-5 preferred Title Appeal No.95 of 2001 before the learned District Judge, Jessore, which were transferred to the Court of the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Jessore for hearing, who upon hearing the parties allowed both the appeals on 11.10.2004. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the same, the plaintiffs filed Civil Revision No.5381 of 2004 against the judgment and decree of Title Appeal No.126 of 2001 and Civil Revision No.5382 of 2004 against the judgment and decree of Title Appeal No.95 of 2001 before the High Court Division and the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division made both the Rules absolute and the judgment and decree dated 11.10. 2004 and 18.10.2004 respectively passed in Title Appeal No.95 of 2001 and Title Appeal No.126 of 2001 by the Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Jessore have been set aside and the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.179 of 1993 by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Jessore are restored. Hence, these leave petitions have been filed by the defendant-petitioners. 

6. Mr. Arun Kumar Bhattacharjee, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners in both petitions, submits that the moot question of the case is whether Panchu Moral is the son of Danu Moral as alleged by the defendants or son of Hache Bepari as alleged by the plaintiff and from the oral evidence of the P.Ws. and D.Ws. and from documentary evidences it is evident that Panchu Moral inherited the share 'in the Ka, Kha and Ga schedule land from Danu Moral but the High Court Division committed error in holding that in Title Suit No.413 of 1986 Jongal Moral failed to prove his relationship with Danu Moral. 

7. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners. His only contention is whether Panchu Moral is the son of Danu Moral as alleged by the defendants or son of Hache Bepari as alleged by the plaintiffs. This question has been dissolved on the evidence on P.W.2, who is aged about 90 years and saw both Danu Moral and Panchu Moral and deposed that Panchu Moral is not son of Dana Moral. In' consideration of the evidence on record, the learned Single of the High Court Division correctly held that in Title Suit No.413 of 1966 Jongal Moral failed to prove his relationship with Danu Moral, who is admittedly the son of Panchu Moral and as such neither Panchu Moral nor his son Jongal Moral is entitled to inherit the properties left by Danu Moral described in the schedule of the plaint. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division having passed the impugned judgment on due consideration of the evidence and materials on record we find no reason to disturb the same. 

8. We are also of the opinion that the said Jongal Moral being unsuccessful in Title Suit No.413 of 1966 the defendant-petitioners are precluded by Rule 2 Order 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure from claiming the share of Jongal Moral. 

9. Therefore, we find no substance in these leave-petitions and accordingly both the petitions are hereby dismissed. 

End.

lawyer:
For the Appellant Mr. A.S. Mohammad Ali, Additional Attorney General, instructed by Mr. B. Hossain, Advocate -on-Record.
For Respondent No.1: Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record.
Respondent No. 2 : Not represented.
parties:
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh ----- Appellant
Versus
Md. Yakub Mia and another ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Tafazzul Islam, J:- This appeal by leave arises out of the judgment and order dated 23.11.1999 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 2060 of 1993 making the Rule absolute. 

2. The respondent No.1 filed the above writ petition calling in question the judgment and order dated 10.11.93 passed by the 1st Court of Settlement, Dhaka in Settlement Case No.10 of 1988 by which the enlisting of House No. 11/5, Block-F Joint Quarter, Mohammadpur, Dhaka in the "Ka" list of the abandoned building, was upheld. In the writ petition it was stated, inter alia, that the above building was allotted to Md. Shafi by a registered lease deed dated 19.4.62; while in peaceful possession of the building Md. Shah, on 08.01.1970 entered into an agreement with the respondant No.1 for sale of the building at a total consideration of Tk.9,750/- out of which the respondent No.1, paid to Md. Shafi a sum of Tk.7,000/- as earnest money and on the same very day Md. Shafi handed over possession of the said building to him; Md. Shafi did not comply with his part of the contract though the respondent No.1 complied with his part of the contract and so he filed Title Suit No. 138 of 1976 against. Md. Shafi seeking specific performance of the contract in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) Dhaka and he after obtaining decree on 26.6.78 put the said decree in execution by filing a Title Execution Case No. 37 of 1978 and got the sale deed executed and registered in his favour; the Government then filed Miscellaneous Case No. 248 of 1986 under Order 9, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the aforesaid ex-parte decree which was allowed on condition that the Government will pay Tk.30,000/and in case of default the said miscellaneous case shall stand dismissed; the Government having failed to comply with the said condition the miscellaneous case stood dismissed for default; the respondent No.1 had been in possession of the disputed building since the date of agreement dated 8.1.70 and being in possession he got his name mutated and has been paying municipal taxes and other bills but even then above building was listed as an abandoned property by the Gazette Notification published on 23.9.86; the Court of Settlement by judgment and order 10.11.93 dismissed the above case. The respondent No. t of the writ petition, who is the appellant herein, contested the said writ petition without filing any affidavit-in-opposition. The High Court Division after hearing made the Rule absolute. 

3. Leave was granted to consider the submissions that the High Court. Division not being the court of appeal erred in law in interfering with the findings of fact arrived at by the Court of Settlement and that during the relevant period the whereabouts of the original owner of the above building not being known and the said original owner also having failed to look after and possess 
the building, the Court of Settlement rightly found that the above building duly vested in the government and the High Court Division erred in law in shifting the onus on the Government to show that the suit property is an abandoned property even though the enlisting of the above building in the Gazette Notification published on 23.09.1986 itself is proof of its abandoned character. 

4. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that the High Court Division not being the court of appeal, can not interfere with the findings of fact arrived by the Court of Settlement which is the final authority to decide the character of the property; the decree for specific performance of contract and the deed of sale pursuant to the said decree being hit by the provisions of P.O. 16 of 1972 the High Court Division erred in law in making the rule absolute; the whereabouts of the original owner not being known during the relevant period and the original owner having failed to look after and possess the above building personally at the relevant time the Court of Settlement rightly held that the above building duly vested to the government; the High Court Division erred in law in shifting the onus on the Government to prove that the property was an abandoned property specially when the enlisting and publication of the said building in the Gazette Notification published on 23.09.1986 conclusive proof of its abandoned character. 

5. The learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.1 on the other handed submits that the Government, the appellant herein, did never serve any notice either upon the respondent No.1 or upon the original owner of the building for surrendering their possession declaring the building as abandoned properly and there was also no material before the Court of Settlement to show that the possession of the building has been taken over by the appellant at any time in compliance of section 5(1) of the Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 or P.O. No. 16 of 1972 and further the respondent No.1 along with his vendor, was also in physical possession of the building and was never dispossessed from the building and stilt is in possession of the same on mutating his name in the Government Khatian and has been paying municipal taxes, gas bills and so the decision of the High Court Division does not call for any interference 

6. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute holding as follows: "On perusal of the Judgment of the Court of Settlement we find that while disposing the petition of the writ petitioner it compared the signature of the Vendor appearing in the original lease deed with the signature of agreement of sale as if deciding the Title of the parties. The Court of Settlement without considering the basic aspect of that is to see as to whether the property is an abandoned property under the provision of P.0.16 of 1972 and whether the soil property under the provision of Ordinance No. 54 of 1985. It appears that the respondent Government appearing before the Court of Settlement could not produce any materials to show that the original allottee being a non-local did anything prejudicial to the war of liberation of Bangladesh. There is also no material before the court of Settlement that the possession of the property was taken by the Government under Section 5(1) of the Ordinance No.54 of 1985. The court of Settlement is not a Civil Court to decide title". 

7. However, as it appears the Court of Settlement found that the respondent No.1 did not possess the vital documents of title i.e. the original allotment letter dated 16.9.1961, registered lease agreement dated 19.4.1963 and letter of delivery of possession dated 26.6.62. Before the Court of Settlement the learned lawyer for the respondent No.1 tried to meet the said position by contending that at the time of execution of the agreement for sale the original owner supplied to the respondent No.1 merely the photostat copies of the aforesaid documents but the Court of Settlement did not accept the above contention as at the relevant time i.e. in the year 1970, there was no photostat machine in the country and moreover on perusal of the said photostat copies the Court of Settlement found that those were made from the office Copies and Duplicate Registered Lease Agreement preserved in the office-file of the Deputy Commissioner of Housing and Settlement Department and the photostat copies filed by the respondent No.1 contained the words "0/C" and "Duplicate" and further the note dated 27.09.83 at para-4 of the page-2 of the file of the above building supports this and the respondent No.1 also submitted the Photostat copy of the 1st page of the same file. Moreover on perusal of the aforesaid office file the Court of Settlement found that Md. Shafi signed each and every document in English including the registered lease deed whereas he executed the alleged bainanama in Urdu which made the Court of Settlement to hold that the alleged bainanama is a forged and anti-dated and the respondent No.1, thus obtained the exparte decree on the basis of the same and further there is no evidence that Md. Shafin was present in Bangladesh after the,25th March, 1971 and moreover till the date of judgment i.e. 10.11.1993, there was also no trace of him. 

8. It further appears that the scope of certiorari applying which the High Court Division made the Rule absolute is very limited and moreover the High Court Division did not advert to the finding of the Court of Settlement regarding absence of original documents and the absence of Md. Shafi in the Bangladesh after 25th March 1971. So the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division cannot be sustained. 

9. Accordingly the appeal is allowed and the judgment and order dated 23.11.1999 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 2060 of 1993 is set aside. There is no order as to costs. 

End.

Mr. Siddiqur Rahman Miah, J.: This revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of the plaintiff respondent is directed against the judgment and decree dated 28.09.2003 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 7th Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No. 102 of 2003 allowing the same and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 18.02.2003 passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 1 Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 106 of 2001 decreeing the suit. 

2. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted suit being Title Suit No. 40 of 2000 in the court of Subordinate Judge now Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka praying for cancellation of deed of sale bearing No. 2826 dated 12.08.1996 and subsequently it was transferred to the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 1 Dhaka and re-numbered as Title Suit No. 106 of 2001.
3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that .52 decimals of ditch and nal land out of 3.24 acres of land of plot No. 582 of CS khatian No. 356 corresponding to SA khatian No. 472 of mouza Ramchandrapur of police Station, Tajgaon, now . Mohammadpur of District Dhaka belonged to one Abdul Majid who sold out the same to the plaintiff and Mohammad Hanif by sale deed No. 16717 on 08.06.1977 in equal share and the plaintiff possessed and enjoyed suit land measuring. 26 decimals of ditch and nal land on amicable partition; that the suit land as being unable to cultivatable, the plaintiff developed it and hanged a sign board of his name in the suit land; that the plaintiff being physical ill, went to his village home at Bandarampur of Daudkandi and started living there with the members of his family, and sometimes went to the suit land to look it. 

4. It is further stated that the plaintiff suddenly went to the suit land and found a sign board in the names defendants Nos. 1 to 3 Md. Yusuf Shikder, Mst. Momtaz Begum and Akhter Hossain Sikder along with their address in the suit land on 18.1.2000: that then the plaintiff went to the residences of defendants No. 1 to 3 and found defendant No. 2 Mst. Momtaz Begum who claimed that they purchased the suit land from the plaintiff but defendant No.2 failed to recognize the plaintiff; and that thereafter the plaintiff paid necessary money to a deed writer to get a certified copy of the sale deed, if any, was executed and registered in the names of defendants Nos. 1 to 3 on 18.01. 2000 and he found sale deed No. 2826 dated 12.08.1996 on search and obtained a certified copy of the said sale deed on 20.01.2000 and got it on 02.02.2000. It is further stated that on scrum"' of the said deed of sale, the plaintiff found it a false deed as he did not execute and register it and the attesting witnesses were not known to him and he did not receive consideration money from the defendants and even the plaintiff did not appear before the sub-registrar office; that the defendants Nos. 1 to 3 created a false deed of sale bearing No.2826 on 12.08.1996 by using his false signatures and then he requested defendants Nos. 1 to 3 to cancel the said deed but they did not lend cars ' to the request of the plaintiff. Thereafter the plaintiff threw away the sign-board of the defendants from the suit land and he placed a sign board of his name in the suit land. It is further stated that deed of sale no. 2826 dated 12.08.1996 case a cloud in the title of the plaintiff in the suit land and as-such the plaintiff was constrained to institute Title Suit No.40 of 2000 which was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No.106 of 2001 for cancellation of sale deed on 17.02.2000. It is noted that thereafter the defendants Nos. 1 to 3 taking advantage of the abnormal political situation prevailing in the country, dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land and constructed thatched huts thereon and as such the plaintiff amended the plaint of the suit by inserting the prayer for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in the suit property.

5. The opposite parties Nos. 1 to 3 as defendants contested the suit by submitting a joint written statement denying all the material allegations stating. inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and no 'cause of action was arisen at all; that the suit is barred by the law of limitation; that the suit is bad for defect of parties and it is barred by section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It is stated that 3.24 acres of land of plot No. 582 of CS khatian No. 356 was originally belonged to Krishna Chandra Mondal, son of late Barku Mondal who died leaving only one son Ramani Mondal and thereafter Ramani Mondal died leaving his son Upendra Chandra Mondal who inherited the entire land and SA Khatian was prepared in his name. It is also stated that Upendra Chandra Mondal died leaving one son Kamal Kanta Mondal who being, owner in possession of the entire land, sold it to one Shamsuddin, son of late Musa Matbar by sale deed No. 3156 dated 04.04.1970; that Shamsuddin sold out. 52 decimals of land through sale deed no. 13524 dated 09.05.1977 and .52 decimal of the land through sale deed No. 13609 dated 09.05.1977 to one Abdul Majid again Shamsuddin sold .26 decimals of land to Abdul Hamid who sold it to Abdul Majid by sale deed No. 37354 dated 24.12.1977. It is further stated that Abdul Majid owning and possessing the suit land including other land sold. 26 decimals of land on 15.05. 1980 to one Kazi Mostafizur Rahman who sold it to Wahidul Islam by sale deed no. 2068 dated 29.07.1989; that Wahidul Islam sold .52 decimals of land by sale deed No.: 1169 dated 30.04.1990 to one Salimullah son of Haji Chinu Mia who sold it to defendant No. 1. It is further stated that Shamsuddin while owning and possessing the suit plot sold out .52 decimals of land through sale deed No. 13535 dated 09.05.1977 to Jahanara Khatun who executed a registered Power of Attorney to one Khandaker Nazrul Islam to sell the said land and thereafter he sold .39 decimals of land to defendant No. 1 through sale deed no. 889 dated 21.03.1995, and that Abdul Majid sold .52 decimals of land through sale deeds No. 4032 dated 08.10.1980 and deed No.33547 dated 08.10.1980 to defendant No.2. It is further stated that Shamsuddin executed a registered deed of sale in favour of Mozammel Hossain who executed a power of attorney to one Azizullah Miah and thereafter Azizullah Miah sold .13 decimals of land to Md. Shafiuddin and .13 decimals of land to Md. Ali Hossain and said Md. shafiuddin and Md. Ali Hossain sold .26 decimals of land to defendant No. 2 on 14.08.1996. It is further stated that Shamsuddin executed a Power of Attorney in favour of Abdul Majid for 1.40 acres of land and thereafter Abdul Majid sold 1.17 decimals of land to Ful Maher Begum who sold the same to defendant No. 2 and that thus defendant No. 1 owned .91 decimals of land and defendant No. 2 owned 1.95 acres of land and it was acquired by LA case No.24 of 1988-89 for flood control Road and Abdul Majid drew compensation for the same. It is further stated that defendants Nos. 1 to 3 developed land and constructed houses in the suit plot. They mutating their names have possessing the same paying rent to the government. 

6. The learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. l Dhaka framed as many as 5(five) issues as to whether the suit is maintainable in its present form and manner, whether the suit is barred by the law of limitation, whether sale deed No. 2826 dated 12.08.1996 is forged, inoperative and illegal whether the plaintiff has right, title and interest in the suit property and whether the plaintiff was dispossessed from the said property and whether the plaintiff is entitled to get relief as prayed for. 

7. At the time of trial. the plaintiff examined as many as 5 (five) witnesses as PWs including the Attorney of the plaintiff namely AR Alamgir as PW-1 while defendants Nos. 1 to 3 examined as many as two witnesses as DWs including defendant No. 1 Yusuf Sikder as DW-1.

8. The plaintiff produced the documents to prove his case in court. But defendants Nos. 1 to 3 did not produce any document of title to prove his defence in court. 

9. The learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka after considering the facts and circumstances and material evidence on records decreed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 18.02.2003. 

10. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 
18.02.2003, the defendant preferred appeal which was allowed reversing the judgment and decree of the trial court. 

11. It is against the aforesaid judgment and decree, the petitioner moved this court and obtained the present Rule. 

12. Mr. Alim Hossain, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the learned Additional District Judge, Dhaka allowed the appeal and thereby reversed the judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 106 of 2001 of the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, First Court, Dhaka most illegally without considering the facts and circumstances and evidence on record of the parties; that the opposite parties Nos. 1 to 3 did not produce any deed of title in court to substantiate their claims in the suit land and they did not adduce any witness to prove the claim of their title and possession in the suit land; that deed of disclaimer bearing No. 2937 dated 20.07.2000 was not produced in court by the opposite parties and it was not marked as a exhibited document and hence the findings regarding the said deed by the appellate court are not based on evidence. He further submits that the petitioner purchased the ditch and nal suit land by sale deed no. 16717 on 08.06.1977 and due to change of ownership of the north and south side of the suit land during these 25 years and construction of flood control road in 1988-89, the owners of the land of three sides were changed but his possession remained as usual and that on the other hand the opposite parties failed to prove their possession in the suit land by evidence and as such the impugned judgment and decree dated 28.09.2003 are liable to be set aside. 

13. Mr. Md. Ahsanullah the learned Advocate for the defendants opposite parties submits that there is enmity between the petitioner and the opposite parties; that the petitioner in order to humiliate the opposite parties in the society collusively created the deeds nos. 2826 dated 12.08.1996 and filed Criminal case on false grounds in order to harras them. 

14. He also submits that defendants could not prove the deeds of purchase of the suit land due to the fault of their learned Advocate, although the deeds were submitted which are lying with the record. 

15. It is further submitted that the petitioner has admitted that, the petitioner purchased the ditch and nal land by sale deed no 16717 dated 08.06.1977 and due to change of ownership of the north and south sides of the suit land during these 25 years and preparation of flood control road in 1988-89, the owners of the land of three sides were changed. 

16. Mr. Md. Ahsanullah the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the petitioner purchased suit land by kabala no. 16717 dated 08.06.1977 and the boundary of the kabala was shown as kitabuddin Madbor in the north and west, vendor Abdul Majid is to the south and Abdul Roaf is to the east; that in the boundary of suit deed no. 2826 dated 12.06.1996 Kitabuddin Maqtbor was shown in the north side; that in the deed of disclaimed No. 2937 dated 23.07.2000; kitabuddir Madbor was shown in north and west side and that all these land are outside the flood control Road. 

17. It is further stated that in the schedule land, Abdul Hakim is shown to the north, Abdul Razzak is to the south, Abdur Roaf is to the east and flood control Road is to the west; that boundary of these three deeds mentioned above are not identical with the suit land. 

18. Mr. Ahsanullah further submits that as the suit land is not identical with the purchased land of the petitioner that is why the defendants opposite parties filed an application for appointing a survey knowing advocate Commissioner in order to relay the petitioner's purchased land with suit land but the learned trial court rejected the prayer. He further submits that suit land is not identical with the purchased land of the petitioner and moreover the interested persons were not made parties in the suit, so the plaintiff petitioner cannot get a decree for declaration and khas possession. He further submits that ends of justice will be met if suit is sent back on remand with direction to make the interested persons parties, to take their deeds into evidence and to relay the suit land with the purchased land. 

19. The moot question that calls for our determination in this revisional application is whether the learned Additional district Judge, 7th court, Dhaka committed any error of law resulting in an error in his decision in allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree of the trial court. 

20. In plain reading of the plaint, it appears to us that plaintiff petitioner firstly filed suit for declaring the kabala no. 2826 dated 12.08.1996 forged, ' void, inoperative fraudulent and illegal and later on the amended the plaint for declaration title and for khas possession along with earlier relief as he was dispossessed from the suit land. 

21. The main contention of the defendants opposite parties is that the suit land and the purchased land of the petitioner and the land of alleged deed no. 2826 dated 12.08.1996 are not identical; that the defendant's purchased the suit land including other land by kabala No 1169 dated 30.04.1990, kabala No. 889 dated 21.03.1995, kabala No. 4032 dated 08.10.1980 kabala No. 33547 dated 08.10.1980, kabala dated 14.08.1996 etc is identical to the suit land and all the interested persons were not made parties. The defence further contention is that their lawyer in the trial court was very inefficient who failed to prove their deeds. He simply submitted these kabalas without former prove for taking the same into evidence, that the learned advocate failed to prove the mutation Khatian and rent receipts and thus he failed to bring the same into evidence. Their prayer is that justice will be best met if this court send case back on remand for bring those document into evidence. 

22. It appears from record that one Mostafa Khondaker and Md. Halim purchased .52 decimals of land by kabala No. 16717 dated 08.06.1977. By amending the plaint, the plaintiff claim that his nick name is Mostafa Khondaker but there is no evidence on this vital aspect of plaintiffs case without which it is very difficult to take any decision as regard the title of the plaintiff. It is admitted that the partner of the plaintiff Abdul Halim has not been made party. He is a very vital and important person in this case whose presence is utmost necessary. 

23. On perusal of the record, it appears that the defendants filed an application for appointing a survey knowing Advocate commissioner to relay the suit land with the purchased land of the plaintiffs suit land with land of disputed kabala and suit land with the land of contesting defendants. Without the identification of suit land with the land in dispute, it is impossible to arrive at a proper decision in this suit. But the learned trial court without applying his judicial mind rejected the prayer. 

24. If the court wants to declare the disputed kabala illegal and void, it is to be decided as to whether the suit land is identical with land of disputed kabalas. In order to declare the title of the plaintiff and to give him khas possession, it is to be decided first as to whether the salt land and the purchased land of plaintiff is identical or not. 

25. It is not possible to decide all these matters in this court and it is required to sent the case back on remand for taking the above mentioned matters into consideration. 

26. Now the point that calls for our determination is whether isit a fit case for sending back on remand. 

Now let us see law regarding sending the case on remand. 

The law on remand is envisaged in order 41 Rule 23 of the Code of Civil Procedure which runs as follows: 

"Where the court from whose decree an appeal is preferred has disposed of the suit upon a preliminary point and the decree is reversed in appeal, the appellate court may, if it thinks fit, by order remand the case, and may further direct what issue or issues shall be tried in the case so remanded, and shall send 'a copy of its judgment and order to the court from whose decree the appeal is preferred, with directions to readmit the suit under its original number in the register of civil suits, and proceed to determine the suit, and the evidence (if any) recorded during the original trial shall subject to all just exceptions be evidence during the trial after remand." 

27. Where the trial court has decided the suit on a preliminary point without recording findings on other issues like identification of land, defect of parties etc. and if the appellate court reverses the decree so passed, the case may be sent back to the trial court to decide other issues and to a determine the suit. Before the court can exercise the power of remand under rule 23 it is necessary to show that the lower court has disposed of the suit on a preliminary point avoiding other issues. 

28. No remand can be ordered by the appellate court under this rule unless the decision of the lower court on the preliminary point is reversed in appeal where such is not the case, the appellate court cannot order remand simply because the judgment of the lower court is not satisfactory or that the lower court had misconceived or misread the evidence or had ignored the important evidence or had acted contrary to law or that the materials on which the conclusion is reached are scanty and the appellate court must decide the appeal in accordance with law. Rule 23 of Order 41 empowers the appellate court to remand a case even when the lower court has disposed of the case otherwise than on a preliminary point and remand is considered necessary by the appellate court in the interest of justice. In the instant case without ascertaining the point of identification of suit land or addition of the interested persons in the suit and without asserting whether the purchaser Mustafa Khondaker's nick name is Md. Motiullah Khondaker, the decision cannot be taken. So it is a fit case for sending the case back on remand to the trial court for ascertaining all these points for interest of justice. An order of remand can be passed if it is necessary to do so in the interest of justice. The power of remand must be regulated by the provision of rule 23 of order 41 and that inherent powers under section 151 of the Code cannot be exercised by the appellate court to order remand. The power of remand was thus, strictly a limited power and yet in practice, the case like this arose wherein remand was necessitated for some reasons. 

29. In the instant case it appears that trial court failed to determine in the issues on point of identification, of the suit land and to ascertain defect of parties and failed to take the deeds of the contesting defendants into evidence which are essential for arriving at a proper decision. 

30. The trial court has liberty to give chance to the parties concerned to amend the plaint and written statements- as per law, to give chance to adduce evidence on relevant point or to frame any new issues, appoint survey knowing Advocate commissioner to ascertain the suit land with other land etc. The trial court has liberty to decide all points holding the trial afresh giving the parties chance to adduce evidence. 

31. The learned appellate court also failed to understand these vital points though he categorically stated in his judgment that the suit land is not identical with other land and that he ought to have gone deep in the matter for sending the case back on remand for clarifying all these points but he has failed to do so. 

32. It is not consonance with equity and justice that an old case could not be remanded lightly, but the circumstances of this case strongly demand the solution of the above mentioned points by the learned trial court and without ascertaining those matters, it is not possible to arrive at a proper conclusion. 

33. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case and law relating to this matter, we are of the view that it is fit case for sending the suit back on remand to the trial court. 

34. In the result, the Rule is disposed of in the light of the discussion made above both the judgment and decree dated 28.09.2003 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 7th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 102 of 2003 and also the judgment and decree dated 08.02.2003 passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka in Title Suit NO. 106 of 2001 are set aside and the suit is sent back on remand for fresh trial giving the parties chance to adduce evidence and to prove documents in the light of the observation made above and the trial court is directed to hear and dispose of the case preferably within 6(six) months from the date of receipt of this record. 

35. Let a copy of this judgment be sent to the learned appellate court for information. 

36. Send down the L.C.R at once to the trial court. 

End.

Mr. Shahidul Islam J:- This Rule is directed against the judgment and decree dated 19.7.2003 passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Kurigram in other Appeal No. 21 of 2000 dismissing the appeal and affirming those dated 9.02.2000 passed by the Assistant Judge, Sadar. Kurigram in other Suit No 59 of 1993 decreeing the suit finally

2. By this Rule the plaintiff opposite party was called upon to show cause as to why the judgment and decree complained of in the Rule should not he set-aside and or pass such other or further order or orders be passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

3. Facts necessary for disposal of the Rule are that the predecessor of the petitioners No. 1-8 and the sole opposite party are 2(two) brothers. The petitioner No. 9 is the mother of the opposite party. The opposite party as plaintiff instituted other class suit No. 59 of 1993 in the court of Assistant Judge. Sadar, Kurigram seeking for a preliminary decree for partition to 1.001/4th acre stating interalia that the land under partition belonged to Dhaniullah, the father of the plaintiff. Said Dhaniullah transferred 2.25 acres of land in favour of his 2(two) sons the plaintiff and the defendant NO. 1. Thereafter he had only 20 acre of land and during his possession he (Dhaniullah) died leaving behind the plaintiff and the defendant No. 1 as his sons and a widow the defendant No. 2. Thereafter the plaintiff sold .21 acre of land from Plot No. 1090 in favour of the defendant No. 1. The plaintiff demanded partition by mots and bounds and the same was refused and as such the suit.

4. The defendant No. I and 2 contested the suit by filling a written statement contending interalia that Dhaniullah transferred 2.25 acres of land from the schedule 1-4 land to the plaint by a heba deed dated 16/7/92 in favour of the plaintiff and defendant No. 1. The plaintiff sold .21 dcc. of kind from Plot No. 1090 in favour of the defendant No.1 The defendants specifically pleaded their exchesive possession in .53 acre from Plot No. 443, 444 and 449 under schedule No. 1 jote. 241/2 acre out of .49 acre in schedule 2 jote .42 acre in schedule 3 jote and .11 acre in schedule 4 jote. The defendant prayed for a separate saham to 1301/2 acre of land as mentioned above and paid court fee. 

5. The suit was decreed in preliminary for on admission by the parties, by the judgment and decree dated 26.9.94 by the Assistant Judge, Kurigram. 

After passing of the preliminary decree the defendant made a prayer for final decree. A commissioner was appointed for effecting final allotment of saham who after making partition submitted report. The said report was accepted and the preliminary decree was made final by the judgment and decree dated 21.8.1996. 

6. Against the said final decree the plaintiff preferred other Appeal NO. 86 of 1996 and the said appeal was allowed by the judgment and decree dated 28.4.97. The matter was sent back on remand for a fresh final partition decree. 

7. Thereafter Mr. Md. Akhtaruzzaman, the learned advocate commissioner was appointed for effecting final partition who submitted report on 15.7.98. 
8. The defendants submitted written objection against the said report but ultimately the said report was accepted and the final decree was passed by the judgment and decree dated 9.2.2000. 

9. Being aggrieved by the said decree the defendant preferred other Appeal NO. 21 of 2000 and the said appeal was dismissed by the Joint District Judge by the impugned judgment and decree dated 19.7.2003. 

10. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree the defendants have moved this court and have obtained the instant Rule. 

11. Mr. Md. Khalilur Rahman, the learned advocate on appearing, before this court at the very outset drawn the attention of this court to the preliminary decree and pointed out that the preliminary decree was passed on admission made by the plaintiff and the defendants. He submitted that the defendants made a prayer for saham claiming their specific possession in .53 acre of land of Plot No. 843, 844 and 849 and also claimed possession in .20 acre of land adjacent to their homestead from Plot No. 850 and 855. He submitted that the plaintiff did not raise any objection against such a prayer for separate saham. He submitted that the trial court also considered that prayer and has specifically mengoned in the judgment dated 26.9.94 that “বিবাদী যেহেতু পৃথক ঠাহামের প্রার্থনা পূর্বক ১০০/- টাকার কোর্ট ফীস দাখিল করিয়াছেন। সেই হেতু বিবাদীগন ও তাহাদের দাবীকৃত ভূমি বাবদ (যেহেতু বাদীর আপত্তি নাই) পৃথক ছাহাম পাইতে পারেন” He submitted that in spite of that admission the learned advocate commissioner has allotted only .44 acre of land from Plot No. 443, 444 and 449 in the saham of defendants. He submitted that the advocate commissioner had no jurisdiction to go beyond the direction given in the preliminary decree. He further submitted that the defendants have prayed for saham claiming specific possession in the land of Plot No. 443, 444 and 449 and also in .20 acre of land of Plot No. 850 and 855 and the plaintiff has accepted that claim. He submitted that the learned advocate commissioner on violating the direction given in the preliminary decree has allotted the specifically possessed land of the defendant in the saham of the plaintiff. He submitted that both the courts below overlooked the said illegal distribution of saham made by the commissioner and passed the final decree. He submitted that the appellate court committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice in failing to consider that the admitted specific possession of the defendant and the specific direction of the trial court has been disturbed by the advocate commissioner in making final allotment of saham. 

12. Mr. Abul Kashem, the learned advocate for the opposite party on the other hand submitted that the courts below on considering the evidence on record and also on considering the convenience of both the parties have accepted the final decree. He submitted that the judgment and decree impugned in the Rule being a judgment of affirmance, there is no scope to interfere with the same. 

13. I have considered the submission made by the learned advocates of both the parties. I have perused the preliminary decree, the field book prepared by the advocate commissioner showing final allotment of saham and written objection filed against the final allotment of saham. I have also gone through the admission made by the PW1 in his evidence who did not raise any objection against the defendants prayer for saham to .53 acre of land of Plot No. 443. 444 and 449 which is their homestead and did not dispute for allotting .20 acre of land from Plot No. 850 and 855 from adjacent to the homestead of the defendant constructed upon the land on Plot NO. 443, .444 and 449. The plaintiff himself in his cross-examination also admitted that he has got no objection if the defendant is given saham to his exclusively possessed land from those plots. It appears from the saham chita that the defendant has not been alloted .53 acre of land from Plot No. 443, 444 and 449 and has not been allotted .20 acre of land from Plot No. 850 and 855. It appears from the saham chittar that .09 acre of land from Plot No. 449 has been allotted to the plaintiff which he is not entitled to get as per the preliminary decree. So it appears that the final decree impugned in the Rule has been passed violating admission made by the plaintiff himself in his evidence and also has been passed violating the specific direction given by the trial court in the preliminary decree. Both the courts below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice in accepting the final decree. There is merit in this Rule. 

14. In the result, this Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The judgment and decree dated 19.7.2003 passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Kurigram in other Appeal No. 21 of 2000 dismissing the appeal and affirming those dated 9.2.2000 passed by the Assistant Judge, Sadar, kurigram in other Suit No. 59 of 1993 are set-aside. The suit is sent back on remand to the court of Assistant Judge, Kurigram directing him to issue a fresh writ to the advocate commissioner for effecting final partition as per the direction given in the preliminary decree and also as per the admission made by the plaintiff. The Assistant Judge. Kurigram is further-directed to mention specifically in the writ to allot .53 acre of land (homestead) to the defendant from Plot NO. 443, 444 and 449. The Assistant Judge is directed to complete the final decree proceeding within a period of 6 (six) months from the date of receipt of the record. The office is directed to. Send down the Record at once.

End.

Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties nos.1-15 to show cause as to why the order No.76 dated 05.9.2001 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Chita! Mari, Bagerhat in Execution Case No.1 of 1996 directing for delivery of possession in accreted land in excess of the decree passed by the trial court should not be set aside. 

2. The decree Execution caseNo.1 of 1996 arises out of Civil Petition for leave to appeal no.505 of 1993 and their Lordships of Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh dismissed the appeal on 16.6.1994 thereby affirmed the judgment and decree of the Hon'ble High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh on an Appeal from Appellate Decree No.929 of 1994, allowed the appeal by judgment and decree dated 12.8.1993 and thereby setting aside judgment and decree dated 30.11.1962 passed by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, Additional Court of Zilla Khulna passed in Title Appeal No.246 of 1960 reversing the judgment and decree dated 24.8;1960 in Title Suit No.143 of 1952, passed by the learned Munsiff, 2nd Court Bagerhat and the instant Decree Execution Case No.1 of 1995.

The opposite party No.I32 as opposite party No.1 of Decree Execution Case No.1 of 1996 filed a separate written objection stating inter alia that total land upto the river measuring an area of 125 Bighas of land and near about 30/35 persons residing thereon by constructing their house acquired by the settlement from the Government dated 12.3.1987 and 18.3.1987. 

5. The learned Trial Court has fixed for execution of the decree through execution case on 31.10.2001 and against issued process relating to delivery of possession but the order was not complied with and a date was fixed on 12.11.2001 for delivery of possession and subsequently another date was fixed on 26.11.2001 but till today order was not complied with and the next date was fixed for delivery of possession on 2.1.2002. 

6. The learned Assistant Judge on 5.9.2001 passed the impugned order directing delivery of possession in accreted land in excess of the decree passed by the trial court against which the petitioner moved this application and obtained the present Rule. 

7. Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas with Mr. Sadananda Rana the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the judgment debtor petitioners submit that the original title being No.143 of 1952 was filed for declaration and recovery of possession measuring an area of 55 Bighas of land and it was decreed but the decree holder opposite party nos:l-15 claimed excess land in the decreetal boundary after accretion upto the river totaling to land measuring 125 Bighas of land which is not the part of the decree and the court has gone beyond the original quantum of decreetal land in execution case which caused miscarriage of justice and further submits that he has no objection if an advocate Commissioner is appointed to locate the said 55 decimals of land as per decree of the trial court and it handed over to the Decree holder within Specified date. 

8. Mr. Gobinda Chandra Thakur the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the decree holder opposite parties submits that it is a suit of 1949 and the decree holder obtained decree in 1960 and that has been affirmed by the Appellate Division in Civil Petition for leave to Appeal Nos.741 with 960 of 2000. The Execution case started in 1996 being Execution Case No.1 of 1996 which could not be executed still and with malafide intention of delaying the execution proceeding only, the Judgment debtor petitioner again moved this application and obtained the present rule. He further submits after the judgment of the Appellate Division no such frivolous application should be entertained and it cannot be re-opened or the matter cannot he adjudicated again and again which amounts to contempt of the Court. Mr. Gobinda Thakur has also filed an application drawing proceeding under section 476 of the Court of Criminal Procedure Court against the judgment debtor petitioner. 

9. Be that as it may the judgment and decree holder opposite parties are entitled to have the decree execution as obtained in title suit No.143 of 1952 and an execution proceeding seems to be obstructed on the ground that the excess land is going to be handed over. It seems that before filing of this present application the judgment debtor has also preferred similar application before this court which went up to Appellate Division and that was rejected. Therefore under this circumstances the application alleging that excess land is going to be delivered is just a decree to make delay in executing and delivering the possession of the decreetal land. Therefore the executing court must not make further delay in delivery of possession in respect of decreetal land by appointing an Advocate Commissioner after demarcating the boundary in respect of 55 Bighas of land as per schedule within one month from the date of receipt of this order. Accordingly this rule is discharged without any order as to costs. 

10. Send down the L.C.R. immediately. 

11. The Decree holder may file the application for drawing proceeding under section 476 Cr. P.C. against the judgment debtor petitioner in the appropriate Bench. 

End.

lawyer:

full_judgment:
Mr. Shahidul Islam J: By this Rule the Opposite Parties Nos. 1-4 were called upon to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 21.9.2000 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Paikgacha, Khulna in Title Suit No. 156 of 1997 dismissing the suit brought under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders pass as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. Facts necessary for disposal of the Rule are that admittedly the suit land belonged to the defendants Nos. 1-3 who entered into a contract for sale of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff Akam alias Akram Goldar. The plaintiffs case is that he paid the entire consideration money but the kabala deed was not executed and registered but he was handed over possession in the suit land. The suit land was a ditch and that was filled in by earth and thereafter the plaintiff had erected a golpata house upon the said land and started a furniture mart in the said premises in the name and style "Shagar Furniture". While he was in possession by running a furniture business, he was dispossessed at. 08:00 pm on 9.7.1997 and as such he filed the suit on 20.11.1997. It is his further case that the defendant refused to hand over possession in the suit land on 30.9.1997. 

3. The defendants Nos. 1-2 by filing a written statement contested the suit by denying material statements made in the plaint and the defendants Nos. 5-6 being represented by the Court Guardian did not file any written statement. It is their case that the defendants inherited the suit property. There was a shop upon the suit land. The suit land was never sold in favour of the plaintiff and possession of the same was not handed over in their favour as stated in the plaint. Thereafter the defendants made an amendment of the written statement and by that amendment they incorporated a story to the effected that they filled in the suit land by earth and had erected two golpata huts upon the said land, those huts were leased out with the plaintiff and plaintiff had started a furniture business. Thereafter the rent was enhanced and the plaintiff became unable to pay rent. The total arrear of rent arose upto Tk. 10,200.00 out of which the plaintiff paid Tk.3.000.00. The matter was placed before the distinguished members of the Awami League and there held A salish on 19.9.1997. The plaintiff himself willfully handed over vacant possession in favour of the defendants. With these averments they prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

4. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Paikgacha, Khulna framed 4(four) issues in the suit. 

5. The plaintiff examined 5 PWs on the other hand the defendant examined 4 DWs. The plaintiff himself in his examination-in-chief substantiated his plaint's case. The PW1 specifically added that "19/9/1997 ইং তারিখ রোজ শুক্রবার আমি বেলা দুই ঘটিকার সময় বাড়ী চলিয়া যাই। আমি রাত্র আটটা-সাড়ে আট ঘটিকার সময় জানলাম আমার সমস্ত মালামাল লুটপাট করিয়া উক্ত ঘরে বিবাদীরা জোর পূর্বক ঢুকিয়া পড়িয়াছে। মালামাল বিবাদীরা ল��টপাট করিয়া নেয়। নগদ আড়াই হাজার এবং এক লাখ সাড়ে নয় হাজার টাকার ফার্নিচার ছিল। আমার দখল ফেরত চাহিয়াছি। কিন্তু বিবাদীদের ৩০/৯/১৯৯৭ ইং তারিখ আমাকে দখল প্রদান করিতে বিবাদীরা অস্বীকার করিয়াছে। আমি প্রার্থনা মোতাবেক খাস দখল ও খরচার ডিক্রী চাই।”   

6. These evidences had neither been denied nor any suggestion had been given to the PW1 that he was not dispossessed as alleged in the plaint. Rather in his cross-examination he admitted that “১৯/৯/১৯৯৭ ইং তারিখের রাত্রেই বেদখলের কথা জানতে পারিয়াছি।” 
7. PW.2 Abdul Majid Gazi claiming him to be the maker of the thatched Golpatahut added “নালিশীরঘর আমি তৈরি করিয়াছিলাম। বাদীর নিকট হইতে টাকা নিয়া ঘর তৈরী করিয়াছিল। ছয় হাজার টাকা চুক্তিতে নালীশী জমি বাদীর বরাবরে বিবাদীগণ বিক্রী করে এবং আমার সামনে উক্ত ঝয় হাজার টাকা আদান প্রদান হইয়াছে। ১৯/৯/৯৭ ইং তারিখে বাদীকে নালিশী ঘর হইতে জোর পূর্বক বেদখল করা হইয়াছে। জোরপূর্বক বেদখলের পূর্ব পর্যন্ত বাদী নালিশী জমিতে এবং নালিশী জস্থি ঘরে বানিজ্য পরিচালনা করিয়া আসিতে থাকে।” These evidences were neither denied nor the defendant's case was thrown before' the PW2 by putting suggestion: PW3 Mohammad Janab All Morol, PW4 Sarwar Mallik, PW5 Abdtis Sttar Sana all claiming them to be contiguous land holder supported the plaintiff's case and had substantiated the date of dispossession dated 19.9.1997. Their evidences were not discarded in cross-examination. On the other hand the defendant had admitted that they have taken possession amicably on 19.9.1997 in the suit land, On the basis of a Salish. The plaintiff did not admit the fact of handing over possession in favour of the defendants amicably. DW2 in his cross-examination admitted that possession was taken by the defendants on 19.9.1997. PW4 Sarwar Mallik being one of the maker of the but in his examination-in-chief admitted that the possession was taken over from the plaintiff on 19.9.1997 although he stated that said taking over of possession was made amicably. This witness in his examination-in-chief stated that an inventory list of the furniture was prepared before taking over possession but in cross-examination he admitted that the plaintiff was not present at the time of preparing that inventory list. This evidence supported the plaintiffs case. It is absurd to believe that the plaintiff  would hand over possession of his but along with furnitures in favour of the defendant but would remain absent at the.time of making inventory list. So reliance cannot be made upon the evidences of PW.4 and also DWs. From the evidences of both the parties it is crystal clear like sunshine of broad daylight that the plaintiff while was running his furniture business in the suit hut was dispossessed by the defendant on 19.9.1997. The suit having been filed within 2(two) months of the date of dispossession, the same was maintainable under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act. 

8. The learned Assistant Judge was not justified in dismissing the plaintiffs suit. Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act provides relief for recovery of possession within 6 months from the date of dispossession, which runs as follows: 

"9. Suit by Persons Dispossessed of Immoveable Property: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immoveable property otherwise than in due cause of law; he or any person claiming through him may, by suit recover possession thereof, notwithstanding any other title that may be set up in such suit. Nothing in this section shall bar any person from suing to establish his title to such property and to recover possession thereof No suit under this section shall be brought against the Government. No appeal shall lie from any order or decree passed in any suit instituted under this section, nor shall any review of any such order or decree be allowed,"'

9. On perusal of the evidences on record and from the discussions made above I have no other option but to hold that the plaintiff successfully proved his case beyond doubt and was entitled to get relief as prayed for. The learned Assistant Judge has committed an error' of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice. I find merit in the Rule. 

10. In the result, the Rule is made absolute however, without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 21.9.2000 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Paikgacha, Khulna in Title Suit No. 156 of 1997 is hereby set aside. The suit is decreed, however without any order as to costs. The defendants are directed to hand over vacant possession within 1(one) month from the date of the decree failing which the plaintiff would be at liberty to get possession through process of the Court. 

The office is directed to send down the lower Court's record at once.

End.
