Mr. Mir Hashmat Ali, J:- This Rule was issued calling upon Respondents to show Cause is to way the impugned notice dated 1.4.1999 as contained in Annexure 'C' should not be declared to have been Passed without any lawful authority and of me Legal effect 

2. Respondent No.2 Bank granted loan of Taka.2,50,000/- under cash Credit against hypothecation of stocks on 8.12.1984 In favour of M/S Reemi Flour Mill. The predecessor of the petitioner was the owner of the said mill who died on 30.1.1985 Leaving behind the petitioner as wife and minor sons and daughters the interest the Respondent no.2 filed Money suit No 17 of 1988 for realisation of Taka 2,21,104/- petitioner contested the suit. After hearing the parties the trial court decreed the suit in part of Taka 1.51,1041= and directed to any day 15 installments within 71/2 years in every 6 month after by the judgment and decree dated 30.7.1987 and 18.8.1987 respectively. 

3. Against the said judgment and decree dated 30.7.1987 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in money suit no. 17 of 1986 the Respondent no .2 Bank filed first appeal No. 19 of 1987 before the Right court Division Comilla Bench. 

4. The said First Appeal was dismissed for default vide order dated 24.5.1990 noted on 7.7.1990. The Respondent No.2 Bank filed an application on 22.4.1993 for restriction of the said first appeal and Civil Rule No 52(F) /93 was issued for restoration of the said First Appeal. After hearing the learned Advocates for the parties the said rule was discharged on 28.8.1997. 

5. Respondent No .2 Bank instituted Money Execution case No.2 of 1999 on 1.4.1999 . The petitioner speared and filed an application to the effect that the execution proceeding is barred by limitation. 

6. The executing Court after hearing the learned Advocates of the parties was pleased to reject the said application by it judgment and order dated 22.7.1999in money execution caseNo.2 of 1999. 

7. Being aggrieved the petitioner filed the present write petitioner and obtained the rule. 

8. Mr. Harunur Rashid, learned advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that respondent No. 2 Bank having been diesel dissatisfied with the decreed dated 15-08-87 filed the First appeal against the said decree which was dismissed for default on 07-07-1990, and no execution case was filled during this period and the Bank filed the execution case No. 2 of 1999. after the disposal of the civil rule on 28-08-1977 beyond the period of limitation of 3 years the execution process ding is without jurisdiction. The petitioner filed application for rejecting the execution proceeding but the executing court without considering the real question in controversy rejected the said application on misconception of law. In support of his contention he cited the case of Md. Abdur Rahim and others Vs, Sree sree Gridgari jee reported in 27 SLR 72. 

9. None appears to oppose the rule. 

10. It appears that respondent bank obtained decree in Money suit No 17 of 1986 dated 30. 7.1987 and 15.8. 1987 passed by learned Subordinate Judge, Chandapur Against the said decree Respondent Bank filed F. A. No.19 (Comilla) of 1987 which was dismissed for default noted on 7.7.1990 respondent bank filed application for restoration of the appeal and Civil Rule No 52(F) of 1993 was started and the said Rule was discharged on 28.8.1997 Respondent bank Filed Money Execution case no .2 of .1999 before the Trial court on 1.4. 1999 for execution of the decree dated 15.8.1987. 

11. Article 182 of the limitation Act provide a period of limitation for 3 years the date of decree for putting the decree in to execution. The petitioner objected to the said proceeding by filling an application dated 23-06-1999. 

12. The question is whether the execution case was filed within the period of limitation? It is to be noted that the Respondent No.2 Bank filed the execution case No.2 of 1999 on 01-04-1999 for execution of the decree dated 15-08-1987. 

13. The limitation Act prescribes that an supplication for execution is to beamed without 3 years from the date mentioned in third column of the Article 182 of the limitation Act. An application for execution has therefore, to satisfy first Article 182 of the Limitation Act. 

14. The Execution court held that against the original decree, there was first Appeal and the said First Appeal was dismissed. 

For default consequently there was a rule for restoration of the said first appeal. The rule has been discharged on 28-08-1997 and as such the elimination will run from the date 28-08-1997 and thus the execution case has been filed within the period of limitation. 
15. Let us see whether the formal decree passed in F.A.N.19 of 1987 dismissed for default is also a decree within the meaning of decree under the Civil Procedure Code. The meaning of Decree was contemplated under section 2 (2) of the Code of Civil procedure runs thus:

2(2) Decree me and the formal expression an adjudication which se far as regards the court expressing it conclusively determines the rights of the parties with regard to all or any of the matter in controversy in the suit and may be either preliminary of final. It shall be deemed to include the rejection of a plaint and the determination of any question within section 144 but shall not include-

(a) Any adjudication from which an appeal lies as an appeal from on order or, 

(b) any order of dismissal far default. 

16. It the case of Md. Abdur Rahim Vs. sree sree Grishari Jes reported in 27 DLR-72 it has been held that "Section 48 of the Civil procedure code provides the maximum period of 12 years during which a decree retains its life of execute ability whereas A "title 182 of the Limitation on Act provides a period of 3 years from the date of decree for putting the decree in execution (Or within 3 years from the date of last order its barred and beams non executable. It was further held that it now well settled that a degree means an appellate decree if an appeal is taken. In this case there was an appeal to the High court but it was dismissed for default for non-compliance of the order and a formal decree was drawn, could it be said a degree in terms of section 2 (2) of the Civil procedure code? in the plain language of the code it is not: it says that any order of dismissal for default shall not be counted a decree" 

17. In this case the respondent No. 2 Bank attained the decree on 15-08-1987 made by the trial court, Against the said decree the decree holder Bank filed First Appeal No. 19 of 1987 which was dismissed for default by order dated 24-05-1990 noted on 7-7-1990 and as such the decree passed by the trial court dated 15-08-1987 remains as decree under section 2(2) of the civil procedure code under article 182 of the limitation Act the period of limitation runs for 3 years from the date of decree dated 15-08-1987 passed by the Artha Rin adalat. The decree holder Bank put the decree dated 15-08-1987 in execution on 1-04-1999 beyond the period of limitation. Since the execution case has been filed beyond the period of limitation, the decree is not executable as the execution, case was initialed as per the prevision of the code of civil procedure the executing court (Artha Adalat) had no jurisdiction to execute the-decree. The decree that was put to execution became barred by limitation before section 6 (Ka) of the a Artha Rin Adalat Ain 1990 cone into Operation in 1997 and as such the impugned notice date 1.04.1999 annexure C issued by the Adalat in the execution case no 2 of 1999 and the proceeding there under are without jurisdictions and declared to have been made without lawful authority, and are of no legal effect. 

18. In the result the rule is made absolute without any order as the casts. 

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Mohammad Fazhil Karim, J:- This petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 27.04.2004 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.5047 of 1998, discharging the Rule upholding the orderNo.34 dated 15.10.1990 passed by the Additional Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur Sadar, in Title Suit No.7 of 1998 allowing the petition for local investigation filed by the defendant respondent No.1 

2. The petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.7 of 1998 impleading the respondent No. 1 as principal defendant and respondent Nos.2-4 as proforma defendants praying for decree for permanent injunction in respect of the suit land alleging, inter alia, that they are owners in possession of C.S. Plot No.1 67 which has been correctly recorded in the names of the plaintiffs and that the plaintiffs are in exclusive possession of the said plot. It is further stated that the land measuring 633 square feet has been leased out by the plaintiff No.1 in favour of the plaintiff Nos.2-10 as per Rules of the Zilla Perished and the plaintiffs Nos.2-10 are in exclusive possession by carrying on business upon constructing tin shed shops on the suit land but the defendants were threatening the plaintiffs with dispossession and hence the suit. 

3. The defendant No.1 as the respondent No.1 has been contesting the suit by filing a written statement denying the allegations and contending amongst others that the suit land is vague and uncertain. 

4. Mr. Muhammad Samsul Hoque, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner submits that the prayer for local investigation is seemingly innocent as observed in the impugned order but most dangerous as in effect it is designed to grab the Government land as it is founded on a claim, made by the defendants-respondents in the written statement and written objection and referred to in their application for local investigation filed in Title Suit No.7 of 1998, which is barred by the Emergency Requisition of Property Act, 1948 and also barred by Res-judicata as the claim was settled against the predecessor of the respondents in Title Suit No.45 of 1996 and Title Appeal No.131 of 1997 and further the claim is sub-judice in view of pendency of Title Appeal No.173 of 2003 and Demarcation Case No.59 of 2003 elaborately stated in paragraph No.4 of the instant civil petition for leave to appeal to show how the respondents have made to grab the Government land; that the respondents have practiced fraud in their evil design to grab the Government land requisition vide Dacca Gazette dated 15.10.1953 and 21.07.1955 in the background stated in paragraph No.4 of the present civil petition- for leave to appeal which could not be made clear before the High Court Division as the learned Advocate for the petitioners having missed the cause list was not present at the time of disposal of the Civil Revision No.5047 of 1998 while he was instructed by the petitioners to file a, supplementary affidavit to furnish necessary' particulars and thus material points having not been considered by the High Court Division there has occasioned failure of justice; that the defendant-respondents in the written statement filed in Title Suit No.7 of 1998 and written objection against the plaintiffs' petition for injunction claimed that Haji Abdul Jalil Khan got possession of the land appertaining to C.S. Plot No.166 on 1 28.05.1953 while the requisition of the said land by the Government was published in the Dacca Gazette on . 15.10.1953 and 21.07.19.55 the claim of the defendant-respondents is legally barred by the Emergency Requisition of Property Act, 1948 and had this material fact been not suppressed by the defendant-respondents the .trial Court would not have entertained the application for local investigation at the instance of the persons having -no locus standi in the matter. 

5. The learned Advocate further submits that in the Title Suit No.45 of 1996 filed by the father of the defendant-respondent No.1 the trial Court categorically observed that he has no title to the land appertaining to C.S. Plot No. 166 which is the Government requisitioned land and the fraudulent decree obtained by him in Title Suit No.4 of 1996 was set aside and Tide Suit No.45 of 1996 filed by him was dismissed on contest wherefrom appeal being Title Appeal i No.131 of 1997 was also dismissed and he did not further proceed and as such, the same claim by his successors in any separate proceeding is simply barred by Res-judicata and the prayer for local investigation solely based on such a claim which is not maintainable was liable to be thrown out in limini; that in the present suit for simple permanent injunction filed by the plaintiff-petitioners while their possession over the suit land has been admitted and also proven by documents. 

6. The learned further submits that as per admitted documents the defendant-respondents have no title, no possession over any portion of the suit land i.e. C.S. Plot No. 167 or 166. So, they have no locus standi to file an application for local investigation and further no useful purpose would be served by local investigation as in the circumstances in a suit for simple permanent injunction; no remedy is available to the defendants while as per admitted documents, the plaintiffs are in possession and locally influential defendants having threatened the plaintiffs with forcible dispossession; the order for local investigation at the instance of the defendants may create some scope for them in these days of unrest and uncontrolled law and order situation to fish in the troubled water and even blood shed is not unlikely; that the claim of the respondents to the effect that no portion of the suit land was ever been requisitioned by the Government on the face of the Dacca Gazette published on 15.10.1953 and 21.07.1955 showing requisition by the Government whether at all maintainable is required to be settled once for all to stop multiplicity of proceedings being handed by the different bodies of the Government at the cost of public money and also causing unnecessary harassment to the petitioners. Lastly, the learned Advocate submits that only the respondent No.1 contested the suit claiming that his father executed two Heba-bil-Ewaz transferring (12+11)=23 decimals of land in his favour but the day when those two deeds were executed, Haji Abdul Jalil Khan had no right to the suit land in view of the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.45 of 1996 and Title Appeal No. 131 of 1999 and therefore nothing was passed to the respondent No. 1 by those deeds and he fraudulently suppressed these material facts. 

7. It appears that the plaintiff filed the suit praying for a decree for permanent injunction in respect of the suit land asserting his exclusive possession in the suit land but the defendant contested the suit filing written statement stating the suit land as vague and uncertain. Under the circumstances the plaintiff filed a prayer for local inspection of the suit land for ascertaining the question of structure standing thereon. The defendant as well filed an application under order 26 of rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for holding local investigation of the suit land in order to ascertain the suit plot and its boundary through an Advocate Commissioner. By order dated 15.10.1998 the learned Assistant Judge allowed both the prayers but the plaintiff being aggrieved by the order allowing local investigation on application of the defendant moved the High Court Division and the High Court Division discharged the Rule holding, inter-alia, that the defendant raised the prayer of identity of the suit land and sought for a local investigation to ascertain the same in order to resolve the issue involved in the suit. In view of the above, we do not find any substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners. 

8. Accordingly, this application is dismissed.

End.

full_judgment:
A.B.M. Khairul Haque, J : This revisional application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, arises in respect of the order dated 03.09.2002 and order dated 28.09.2002, passed in Title Execution Case No. 18 of 1980, by the Joint District Judge, Second Court, Comilla.

2. It is stated in the petition that the opposite parties filed a title suit being Title suit No. 73 of 1976 which was decreed on contest on 30.09.1980. In due course, the decree-holder-opposite-party filed an execution case being the Execution Case No. 18 of 1980. On appeal being the First Appeal no 20 of 1981, it was decreed in part on 07.07.1996. Thereafter, the judgment debtor petitioner filed an appeal before the Appellate Division being the Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No 689 of 1996 which was ultimately rejected on 16.03.1997 and a review petition being the Civil Review Petition no. 14 of 1997 was filed which was dismissed for default in pursuance to an order dated 16.11.2000. In the meantime, the decree holder opposite party filed another execution case on 08.06.2002 being the Title Execution Case no 3 of 2002 but on their prayer for withdrawal made on 08.08.2002 the said execution case was rejected on 03.09.2002 (Annexure-B). The decree-holder opposite parties also by their application dated 08.08.2002, prayed for vacating the earlier order of stay in Title Execution Case no 18 of 1980 passed on 19.12.1980 and by another application prayed for amendment of the petition of the execution case and also prayed for deputing a Magistrate with a police force along with an Advocate Commissioner. The learned Judge after hearing by his order dated 03.09.2002, allowed the amendment and re-started the Title Execution Case on 18 of 1980. On 15.09.2002 the judgment debtor petitioner filed an application praying for rejecting the Execution Case no 18 of 1980 as barred by limitation (Annexure-C). On hearing, the learned Joint District Judge, Comilla, by his order dated 28.09.2002 rejected the said petition as not maintainable and directed issuance of writ of delivery of possession in favour of the decree-holder-opposite-parties.

3. Mr. Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, Senior Advocate appears with Mr. Horandra Nath Nondy, Advocate, on behalf of the petitioners. He submits that according to the provisions of Article 182 of the Limitation Act, An execution case has to be filed within three years from the date of the decree or to take some steps in aid of the execution of the said decree within the next three year but the Execution Case No 18 of 1980 although was filed within the period of limitation but when the decree was modified in the First Appeal No 20 of 1981 by the judgment dated 07.07.1996 and the decree drawn on 03.11.1996, the decree holder opposite party ought to have taken steps in the execution case in aid of execution of the decree as modified, within three years from the said date or at least within the period of three years from the date of dismissal of the Civil petition for leave to Appeal no 689 of 1997 as such, although a review petition. being the Review petition no 14 of 1997 was filed which was dismissed for default on 06.11.2000 but the steps in aid of the execution case in Execution Case No 18 of 1980, being taken as late as on 08.08.2002, much beyond the period of limitation of 3 (three) years, the petition of the petitioners dated 15.09.2002 praying for dismissal of the execution case on the ground of limitation, was illegally rejected by the learned Joint District Judge by his order dated 28.09.2002 and is liable to be set aside.

4. On the other hand, Mr. Shafique Ahmed, Senior Advocate, appears with Mr. Md. Anwar Hossian, Advocate, on behalf of the decree holder opposite parties. He submits that they had no laches to file the execution case immediately after obtaining the decree in Title Suit on. 73 of 1976 being the Title Execution Case no. 18 of 1980 as early as on 26.11.1980 but the petitioner judgment debtors filed the First Appeal no 20 of 1981 and being unsuccessful took a further appeal before the Appellate Division being the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal no 689 of 1996 which was dismissed and thereafter filed a review petition being the Review Petition no 14 of 1997 which was also dismissed for default because of laches on his part on 06.11.2000 and thereafter within the period of limitation from that date necessary application was filed on 08.08.2002 to proceed with the execution case, as such, the learned Judge by his order dated 28.09.2002 rightly rejected the petition of the judgment-debtors to dismiss the Execution Case no 18 of 1980. The learned Advocate further submits referring to the decision in the case of Mymensingh Co-Operative Town Bank Ltd. Vs. Rajendra 12 DLR(1960)730, that an execution case will be within time if it is filed within 3 (three) years of the order passed in revision or review, as such, the application filed on 08.08.2002 in the Title Execution Case No. 18 of 1980 within the period of limitation of 3 (Three) years from the date of dismissed of the Review Application no 14 of 1997 for an default on 06.11.2000 and the learned Subordinate Judge rightly rejected the petition of the judgment debtors on 28.09.2002.

5. 1 have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides. The decision reported in 12DLR(1960) 730 is based on the provisions of Bengal Co-operative Societies Act, 1940 where the execution case was filed on 2nd December, 1955, within the period of 3(three) years from the date of disposal of the revision on 3rd of December, 1932. But this decision has got no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the present case.

6. In the instant case, the suit was decreed on 30.091980 and the execution case was filed no 26.11.1980 (Annexure-A) but its proceedings was stayed on 19.12.1980, as directed by the High Court Division in Civil Rule No 1557(F) of 1980 in an appeal which was subsequently numbered as the First Appeal no 20 of 1981. The decree of the Trial Court was, however, modified by the High Court Division in its judgment and decree passed on 07.07.1996 (Decree drawn up on 03.11.1966), as such, in the normal course, the steps in aid, as envisaged in Art 182(5) of the limitation Act, for amendment of the petition of the execution case, ought to have been filed within 3(three) years from the date of the decree passed in appeal on 03.11.1996 but the operation of the said decree was also stayed by the Appellate Division in the Civil petition for leave to Appeal no 689 of 1996 which was however, dismissed on 16.03.1997 Although thereafter a review petition was filed before the Appellate division but no order of stay was given in the said review petition which was ultimately dismissed for default for non-compliance of the order of the Appellate division passed on 06.11.2000 after six weeks from the said date.

<u>7. Since there was no order of stay either of the execution case or of the operation of the appellate decree, the period of limitation of 3 (three) years started to run from 16.03.1997 when the Civil petition for leave to Appeal No. 689 of 1996 was dismissed and the step in aid of the execution case as envisaged under Art. 182(5) of the limitation Act, became time-barred on the expiry of 15.03.2000. Since no step was taken to amend the petition of the execution case in commensurate with the decree as amended in appeal, within the period of limitation, the execution case itself is liable to be dismissed.</u>

8. No doubt this is harsh on the part of the decree-holder-opposite-parties but it cannot be helped since law helps only a diligent and not an indolent.

9. Under such circumstances, the orders dated 03.09.2000 and dated 28.09.2002 allowing to proceed with the Title Execution Case no 18 of 1980, are set aside.

10. In the result, the rule is made absolute.

11. Send down the records forthwith.

End.

full_judgment:
Kashefa Hussain, J : Rule was issued at the instance of the petitioner against order no.155 dated 13.01.2013 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 02 of 2011 arising out of Title Suit No. 07 of 1996 allowing the application of the defendant under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and condoning the delay of 307 days in filing the application.

2. The facts relevant for disposal of the Rule in short are that the petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 277 of 1995 which was transferred and subsequently re-numbered as Title Suit No. 07 of 1996. The suit was filed after complying with due procedure and upon hearing ultimately decreed vide judgment and decree dated 30.03.2010. Thereafter, on 08.02.2011 the defendants filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 02 of 2011 under order 9 rule 13 of Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the judgment and decree dated 30.03.2010 paying the prescribed mandatory deposit etc. Primarily the defendant alleged that the judgment and decree dated 30.03.2010 was an ex-parte order and ought to be set-aside. The PW-1 and DW-1 deposed in the Miscellaneous Case which was allowed by order dated 13.01.2013 along with condonation of delay of 307 days and thus setting aside the judgment and decree dated 30.03.2010 passed by the Trial Court being aggrieved by the order passed in Miscellaneous Case no. 02 of 2011 allowing the application under order 9 rule 13 of Code of Civil Procedure the plaintiff as petitioner preferred this instant Revisional Application and is hence before us.

3. Mr. Md. Harun-Ar-Rashid Learned Advocate appeared for the petitioner while Mr. Moinuddin Learned Advocate appeared for the opposite party.

4. Learned Advocate Mr. Md. Harun-Ar-Rashid on behalf of the petitioner submits that the Miscellaneous Case can be allowed but basically on 2 grounds that is for non service of summons and another ground being that order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not applicable in the instant case. Since the defendant executed Vokalatnama, written statement and also cross-examined the plaintiff. He further drew our attention to the operative portion of the judgment and decree dated 30.03.2010 and primarily tries to focus upon the word “দোতরফা সুত্রে শুনানী অন্তে ডিক্রি হইল” in his argument he stresses on the point that it is 'clear' that the judgment dated 30.03.2010 was not an ex-parte order since the ordering portion itself reads “দোতরফা সুত্রে শুনানী অন্তে ডিক্রি হইল” stating that the judgment was executed upon presence of both the plaintiff's and defendant's sides. He also submits that according to Article 164 of the limitation Act the miscellaneous case has to be filed within 30 days of knowledge of the decree when in case of non service of summons.

5. On the other hand learned Advocates Mr. Moinuddin on behalf of the defendant opposite party submits that judgment and order dated 30.03.2010 is actually an ex-parte order and defendants were not present on that particular day before the court and had no knowledge that judgment was going to be passed on that day. He persuades that the use of the term “দোতরফা সুত্রে” is only an inadvertent error on the part of the Trial Court and which is evident from the order passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 02 of 2011 dated 13.01.2013 allowing the application along with condonation of delay of 307 days and also submits that the original Title Suit was filed in the year 1995 and the suit was dragged on for long 15 years mainly due to various delaying tactics resorted to by the plaintiff. He stresses upon the fact that it is evident from the records that the suit was dismissed several times and that it would be eventually restored repeatedly on various pleas of the plaintiff's. He further persuades that lastly when it was taken up for hearing due to some unavoidable circumstances on the part of the learned Advocate for the defendant which was inadvertent and totally unintentional, the defendant otherwise diligent regarding the case however could not be present in court on that day. He alleges that the defendant had no knowledge of the judgment being passed on 30.03.2010 and which they ultimately learnt later, and finally on 24.01.2011 after receiving knowledge of the judgment filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 02 of 2011 on 08.02.2011, In this context he assails that lie filed the case within 30 days of knowledge of the decree in accordance with the statutory rules.

6. We have heard the Learned Advocates from both sides, perused the materials on record including the miscellaneous application and order passed by the Trial Court allowing the application, wherefrom, it transpires and as is evident from the records that the defendant received summons etc. and in filing the Miscellaneous Case is barred by Article 164 of the Limitation Act, and it also appears from the records that the plaintiff-petitioner had actually prayed for adjournment several times from last 15 years on different pleas and it is also evident from the record that the suit was dismissed for default thrice, firstly on 07.02.19999, secondly on 10.05.2001 and lastly on 24.07.2005 and it was restored each time on the prayer of the plaintiff.

7. However, upon perusal of the records, we have marked the lack of diligence and delaying tactic shown by the petitioner pending the suit, whereas on the other hand no such conspicuous lack of diligence appears on the part of the defendant, while it is also evident upon examination that the petitioner had on different pretexts created by themselves dragged the suit up to 15 years. It also transpires that even after hearing and examining PW-1 the defendant for some reasons could not appear on the day of the judgment and which they have submitted and stated that they had no knowledge of the same which is unintentional and inadvertent. It is true that the plaintiff's suit was discharged and restored thrice and adjourned several times and also restored several times but on the other hand the defendant as is ex-facie evident from the records only once failed to be diligent which was due to inadvertence of the learned advocate for the defendant-petitioner-opposite party. Thus relying upon equitable principles, we are of the considered view that if the plaintiff-opposite party-petitioner could be given so many chances even after failing thrice, it is only fair that the defendant opposite parties having failed only once ought to be given a similar chance. Pursuance to the submissions of the learned Advocates we are of the considered view that for some inadvertent fault of the learned advocate for defendant and that is only once, the party should not suffer, and, therefore, we feel that the Trial Court correctly allowed the application in Miscellaneous Case No. 02 of 2011 dated 08.02.2011. The learned Advocate for the petitioner argued that Article 164 of the Limitation Act provides that in the event of prayer for setting aside a decree passed ex-parte, time shall start from the date of the decree or where the summons was not duly served when the applicant has knowledge of the decree. The learned advocate for the petitioner tried to persuade us that in this case summons was served, it is evident that summons was served and all other due process were complied with, and, therefore, the defendant cannot rely on having received  knowledge of the judgment and decree.

8. Now the instant civil revision arises out of a Miscellaneous Case for setting aside the judgment and decree under order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, and, therefore, we feel that for our purpose order 9 rule 13 of Cpc. is applicable in the instant case.

9. Order 9 rule 13 reads as under; "In any case in which a decree is passed ex-parte against defendant, he may apply to the Court by which the decree was passed for an order to set it aside; and if he satisfies the court that the summons was not duly served, or that he was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing, the Court shall make an order setting aside the decree as against him upon such terms as to costs, payment in to Court or otherwise as it thinks fit, and shall appoint a day for proceeding with the suit. Provided that where the decree is of such a nature that it cannot be set-aside as against such defendant only it may be set-aside as against all or any of the other defendants also."

<u>10. After perusal of order 9 rule 13, that order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure quite expressly states the criteria and condition and situations under which an application for setting aside an ex-parte order may be allowed. We have examined that order 9 rule 13 provides for a disjunctive clause, wherein it provides for situations or circumstances where a defendant may be prevented by any "sufficient cause" for appearing before the court. In the case before us, it is evident from the order dated 08.02.2011 of the trial court, that the court upon examining the facts and upon exercising its own discretion allowed the application under order 9 rule 13 which discretion the court is lawfully empowered to exercise. Our considered view is that under the facts and circumstances, it is only fair that the application under order 9 rule 13 ought to be allowed and the Trial Court correctly allowed the same and has elaborated upon the reasons for allowing the same in his Order in the Miscellaneous Case filed by the defendant against the ex-parte Judgment and Decree passed by the Trial Court. The last contention of the petitioner is that the Judgment and Decree is not actually an ex-parte order and further persuades that it also "apparent" from the ordering portion of the judgment dated 30.03.2010 wherein it is stated that the Judgment is passed “দোতরফা সুত্রে” Against this contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner our considered finding is that using the word “দোতরফা সুত্রে”was actually an inadvertently error on part of the Trial Court and which is obvious from the fact that the Trial Court allowed the application under order 9 rule 13 of Cpc. and in his order explained the facts and grounds of allowing the application quite elaborately, and which is also apparent from the Judgment where the Trial Court made an observation that after cross examination of PW-1, the defendant did not come, therefore, it is evident and obvious that the order “দোতরফা সুত্রে”used in the ordering portion of the judgment was only an inadvertent error on the part of the Trial Court.</u>

11. Taking all the facts and circumstances into consideration, we arrive at our considered finding that the Trial Court vide its Order no.155 dated 13.01.2013 in Miscellaneous Case No.02 of 11 arising out of Title Suit No. 07 of 1996 correctly allowed the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Cpc. , and, therefore, we do not find any merits in this rule.

12. In the result, the Rule is hereby discharged without any Order as to costs and the judgment and order dated 08.02.2011 passed by the Trial Court is hereby affirmed. 13. Communicate at once.

End.

full_judgment:
The Rule was issued on an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 10-4-2006 passed, by the Joint District Judge, Section Court, Narail in title Appeal No. 44 of 2000 reversing those dated 3-4-2000 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Narail in Title Suit No.6 of 1992 should not be set aside and/or any other order passed as this Court may deem fit and proper.

2. By the Same Rule issuing order dated 30-7-2006, operation of the impugned judgment and decree was stayed.

3. The necessary facts for disposal of the Rule are that the 'Ka Schedule' land appertained to SA khatian No. 232 and some other SA khatians under mouza-Damurtala and 'Kha Schedule' land appertained to SA khatian No. 242 and some other SA khatians under mouza-Raghunathpur, Thana and District Narail and 'Ga Schedule' movable property belonged to Zitu Beg, husband of the plaintiff Hazera Begum. Zitu Beg had no issue and he sold some of his land to one Md Shahidul Islam. As he became older and older and ill, he appointed the plaintiff as his attorney by registered deed of irrevocable power of attorney dated 17-9-1990 for his property and delivered possession thereof. The plaintiff took possession of the suit land and during her possession, on 26-1-1991 corresponding to 12 Magh 1398 BS Zitu Beg died. Thereafter, on 7 Poush 1398 BS, the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 claimed title over the suit land as heirs of Zitu Beg denying the title of the plaintiff thereto. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are not heirs of Zitu Beg. Koresh Beg was the father of Zitu Beg and Koresh Beg had brothers and sisters. As the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 denied the title of the plaintiffs to the suit land, her title thereto had been clouded and as such, she filed the suit for declaration of her title to the suit land.

4. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable in the present form. Their positive case was that the suit land belonged to Zitu Beg who owned the same by purchase and inheritance. He gifted 13 decimals of land from non-suit plot No. 139 to his brother's son defendant No. 1 petitioner Golam Beg alias Golam Rahman Beg by registered deed dated 8-3-1988 and orally gifted the rest 13 decimals of land of the said plot to defendant No. 1 on 10-10-1988 and delivered possession thereof in his favour. Thereafter, Zitu Beg filed Title Suit No. 171 of 1999 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Narail against defendant No. 1 challenging the aforesaid gift but subsequently, the suit was compromised on the basis of a solenamaand Zitu Beg left his right over the suit land in favour of the defendant No.1. Zitu Beg then died leaving wife the plaintiff and brother's sons defendant Nos. 1 and 2. The defendants and the plaintiff have been possessing the suit land as per amicable partition. The plaintiff has been possessing the house of Zitu Beg.

5. The learned Assistant Judge, on the pleadings, framed issues and both the parties adduced evidence. He believed the plaintiff's case and dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 30-4-2000. Against this decree, the plaintiff preferred. Title Appeal No. 44 of 2000 in the Court of District Judge, Narail which was ultimately heard and disposed of by the Joint District Judge, Second Court, Narail who allowed the appeal and decreed the plaintiff's suit by his impugned judgment and decree dated 10-4-2006.

6. Being aggrieved by this decree dated 10-4-2006, the defendant No. 1 preferred this Revision and obtained the Rule.

7. None appears on behalf of either of the parties when the revision is taken up for hearing. It is now well settled by our Appellate Division that a revision can be disposed of on merit in absence of any party or both the parties. If any authority is needed, I can cite the case of Safaruddin vs Fazlul Haq, 49 DLR (AD) 151.

8. I have perused the revision petition and the LCR. It appears that in the Ka and Kha Schedules of the plaint, CS plot numbers have been mentioned without mentioning the CS khatian numbers. Instead, SA khatian numbers have been mentioned. It appears that the plaintiffs did not file any of the SA khatians. It further appears that the plaintiff filed CS khatian No. 584 and other CS khatians, Exhibit 2 series. Exhibit 2 CS khatian No. 101 shows that the land of this khatian belonged to Abdul Wazed Beg and others. It appears from Exhibit 2(ka) CS khatian No. 422 that the land of this. khatian belonged to Naimuddin Beg and others. Exhibit 2 (kha) CS khatian No. 170 shows that the land of this khatian belonged to Wazed Beg. Koresh Beg and others It is evident from Exhibit 2(g) CS khatian No. 584 that the land of this khatian belonged to Surja kanta Ghosh. The plaintiff did not mention the CS khatians in the plaint though CS plots have been mentioned in the schedules. It appears that the defendant also did not file any SA khatian but they filed CS khatian No. 222, Exhibit Ga which shows that the land of this khatian belonged to Ismail Beg and Abdul Beg.

9. It may be mentioned that no statements about CS as well as SA record have been made in the body of the plaint. The genealogy of the CS recorded tenants has not been mentioned in the plaint. Though both the parties have claimed that Zitu Beg was the owner of the suit land, but in fact neither party stated in the pleading the mode of acquisition of title of Zitu Beg right from CS record. It ought to have been stated in the respective pleading of the parties since they have filed CS khatians and it has been mentioned in the written statement that Zitu Beg owned the suit land by purchase and inheritance. It is not understood as to how the learned Advocate for the plaintiff drafted the plaint without narrating the mode of acquisition of title of Zitu Beg in the suit land. It is also not understood as to how the Courts below passed their judgments without perusal of the SA khatians and discussing about CS khatians and mode of acquisition of title of Zitu Beg in the suit land, particularly when Koresh Beg, father of Zitu Beg is the CS recorded tenant vide Exhibit 2(Kha) and thus, I find that both the Courts below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in their judgments and decrees. In fact, they ought to have instructed the plaintiff to amend the plaint by narrating the mode of acquisition of title of Zitu Beg in the suit land in view of the CS khatians as filed by her. Therefore, the impugned judgment and decree and those of the trial Court have no foundation and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree cannot stand.

<u>10. It is well settled that CS record has got a presumptive value though rebuttal in nature. That is why in a title suit relating to land like the instant one, the plaintiff claims title by narrating facts showing chain of title right from the CS record. If the title is derived from a common ancestor of the parties, still the stand of the ancestor should be described in the pleading. If the common ancestor is admittedly SA recorded tenant or a tenant of some other record-of-right, the same must also be narrated in the pleading because the Court, in determining title, is to peruse such record-of-right. The facts constituting chain of title of the plaintiff/defendant must be narrated in the pleading deducing the same from CS record, particularly when the common ancestor is an heir of a CS recorded tenant. The learned Advocates for the plaintiff as well as the defendant must not forget this in drafting the respective pleading though they are Advocates of a mofassal area because the long-standing practice throughout the country is that in a title suit relating to land, the derivation of title of the plaintiff/defendant is narrated in the pleading from the stage of CS record as it forms the basis of title.</u>

11. In view of the aforesaid discussion, for proper adjudication, the plaint should be amended by stating the mode of acquisition of title of Zitu Beg right from the CS record. The plaintiff as a client cannot suffer for the latches done by her engaged learned Advocate in drafting the defective plaint as indicated above. Therefore, this is a fit case for remand to the trial Court. As I have taken the decision of sending the suit back on remand to the trial Court for amending the plaint, I refrain myself from discussing the suit on merit. The Rule is fit to be made absolute.

12. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The stay order granted earlier is hereby vacated. The judgment and decree of the Courts below are hereby set aside and the suit is sent back on remand to the trial Court. The trial Court is directed to ask the plaintiff to amend the plaint by stating the mode of acquisition of title of Zitu Beg right from the CS record in the light of the observations made above and then proceed with the suit in accordance with law. It shall obviously give the defendant an opportunity to file additional written statement if the plaint is amended.

Send down the LCR along with copies of this judgment to the Courts below immediately.

End.

Fazle Hossain Mohammad Habibur Rahman, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 AKM Murshed to show cause why the judgment and order dated 18.1.86 passed by Mr. Md. Ibrahim Ali, District Judge, Narayanganj in Title Appeal No. 184/84 arising out of Title Suit No. 56/84 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, Narayanganj should not be set aside or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. The case of the plaintiff-petitioner Meher Ali is that he instituted Title Suit No. 56/84 in the court of Subordinate Judge, Narayanganj against the defendant opposite parties A.K. Murshed, Full Chand Mia, Rahatan, Milan Mia, Razzak and Aklima praying for a decree of declaration of plaintiffs title in .16 acre of plot No.131 (Shabek Pukurpar-at present bhiti) and .21 acre of .plot No. 132.(Shahck pukurpar-at present bhiti) of mouza Hajiganj, P.S. Narayanganj, District Narayanganj and also for a declaration that defendant No. 1 A.K. Murshed is a tenant in the premises in the suit land. Plaintiff and defendant Nos. 2-6 are sub-lessees inducted by defendant No. l. The suit land originally belonged to the Zamindari Estate of Ram Ratan Sharma which was seized, owned and possessed by Suresh Chandra Poddar, Joy Durga Daysa, Govinda Chandra Poddar, Mem Chandra Chowdhury, Nawab Ali Chowdhury and others in odd shares and their names with their shares were correctly recorded in the maliki claim of C.S. Khatian. Nawab Ahsanullah Bahadur represented by Manager, Court of Wards Estates, Dhaka owner of pattani taluk was immediate tenant under the said Zamindars with respect to the suit land. The said Manager, Court of Wards Estate, Dhaka leased out the suit land along with other lands as raiyats in favour of Shorojini Bala Dutta who seized, owned and possessed the suit lands along with other lands as permanent raiyat under the said Court of Wards Estate of Dhaka. Shorojini Bala Dutta constructed tinhuts in the suit land and let out the premises to defendant No.1 as monthly tenant. She executed a Will dated 4.12.82 in favour of her daughter-in-law Anjali Rani Dutta. After the death of Shorojini Bala Dutta her daughter-in-law Anjali Rani Dutta obtained probate of the said Will in Probate Misc. Case No. 103/63 in the 4th Court of Munsif, Narayanganj on 20.5.64 and thus became owner of the suit lands and the premises therein along with other lands of the said Will. Anjali Rani Dutta sold out the suit lands and the premises therein along with other lands to the plaintiff by registered sale deed dated 26.6.89. Defendant No.1 opposite party A.K. Murshed entering into occupation of the premises of the suit land as an ordinary ejectable monthly tenant under Shorojini Bala Dutta, paid monthly rents to her. The defendant No. 1 continued his occupation in the suit lands as usual during the ownership of Anjali Rani Dutta who delivered possession of the suit and the premises to the plaintiff along with the ordinary ejectable occupation of the said monthly tenant defendant No. 1 opposite party A.K. Murshed and thus defendant No. 1 A.K. Murshed became tenant under the plaintiff. As defendant No. 1 became defaulter and as he sublet a portion of the premises in the suit land illegally without permission of his land lady to defendant No. 2 Ful Chand Mia and Rustam Ali Mia (predecessor of defendant Nos. 3-6), the plaintiff terminated his tenancy by quit notice dated 16.1.70 with the expiry of the month of February, 1970 directing him to hand over vacant possession of the premises in the suit land with the expiry of tilt month of February, 1970. As defendant No.1 A K. Murshed did not comply with the said quit notice, the plaintiff instituted SCC Suit No. 5/70 in the SCC Court of 4th Munsif, Narayanganj for ejectment of defendant Nos. 1-2 and Rustom Ali Mia, that the said SCC Suit was decreed ex parte on 19.5.72 with cost. Defendant No. 1 A.K. Murshed filed Misc. Case No. 77/72 under Order 9, rule 13 C.P.C. for setting aside the said ex parte decree which was allowed on contest on 30.12.72. Thereafter it was found that the said Misc. Case No. 77/72 was filed without depositing the cost or submitting any security as per provision of section 17(1) of SCC Act Hence the plaintiff challenged the validity of the order dated 13.12.72 in the said Misc. Case No. 77/72 in Title Suit No. 182/75 (probably it is a mistake for 1974) as it appears from the judgment of the Appellate Division in the case of Murshed Ahmed Vs. Meher Ali 35 DLR (AD) 178 in the Second Court of Munsif, Narayanganj which was de-creed on contest by judgment dated 31.1.77. Defendant No.1 preferred Title Appeal No. 39/77 in the court of District Judge, Dhaka against the said decree in Title Suit No. 182/75 (1974) which was dismissed on contest by judgment dated 28.12.78. Defendant No. 1 preferred Second Appeal No. 177/78 before this court and a learned Single Judge of this court dismissed the said Second appeal on contest by judgment dated 5.4.82 Thereafter defendant No. 1. filed civil appeal No. 136/82 before the Appellate Division and the same was allowed on contest by judgment dated 27.1.83 which is reported in 35 DLR (AD) 178. The said SCC Suit No. 5/70, the further proceedings of which remained stayed during the said interim period was made ready for trial after vacating the stay order in SCC Court of the 4th Court of Munsif, Narayanganj. Major Monwar Hossain, son of defendant No. 1 A.K. Murshed, being an army personnel managed to have said SCC Suit No. 5/70 transferred to Summary Martial Law Court No. 25 at Narayanganj on 25.7.83 by Major General N.A. Chisty illegally by gazette Notification No. 142 dated 25 July 1983 (published in the Bangladesh Gazette on 26th July, 1983). Defendant No. 1 A.K. Murshed in the Summary Military Court claimed adverse possession in the suit land without observing the legal requirements of first surrendering the possession of the property to the owner and then regaining the same through court on establishing adverse possession. Defendant No. 1 thus has got no legal right to set up the plea of adverse possession in the suit land. The defendants since 19.4.84 have recently started making open denial of the plaintiffs title in the suit lands. In view of this the cause of action of the present suit has arisen. As the SCC Suit No. 5/70 has not yet been finally disposed of by judgment, the plaintiff has no other alternative but to take shelter of the civil court for appropriate relief. The plain-tiff prayed for leave of the court for consequential relief after getting back the SCC Suit No. 5/70 from the review court of the Zonal Martial Law Court Administrator. The cause of action of the present suit arose on and from 19.4.84 when the defendants openly denied the title of the plaintiff in the suit land and disclosed that they will henceforth deal with the suit lands as owners of the same.

3. On 9.5.84 the plaintiff-petitioner Meher Ali filed a petition for amendment of the plaint under rule 17 of Order 6 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the ground that the plaint of the suit was drafted hurriedly. Among various minor amendments it was prayed that in paragraph 16 of the present plaint in the 7th line the word 'lands' will be deleted and thereafter the following shall be inserted, "defendant No. 1 became defaulter in payment of rent and as such Shorojini Bala instituted a case in the court of the House Rent Controller, Narayanganj for permission to sue for ejectment of defendant No.1 on the ground of default". In the said case defendant No. 1 was directed to pay the rent with effect from 1.3.50 etc. and the prayer for permission to sue for ejectment of defendant No. 1 was ultimately rejected. The appeal against the said order dismissed on contest asking defendant No. 1 to pay all arrears rents up to May, 1953 or in default of such payment the landlord appellant is permitted to sue the tenant for ejectment on the ground of default, that the Summary Military Court No. 25 in spite of application has not sup-plied the plaintiff with the report regarding the fate of the SCC suit No. 5/70, that defendant No.1 with the help of the Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Narayanganj with police force and many unknown people damaged the dochala tin hut, dochala cowshed, and dochala kitchen and two other dochala tin-huts from the suit premises and looted away C.I. sheets etc. and constructed 3 pucca boundary walls in the suit plots. That defendant No. 1 on 21.4.84 has filed a copy of the Gazette Notification No. 142, Dhaka dated 25.7.83 showing the illegal transfer of SCC Suit No. 5/70 from the Second Court of Munsif, Narayanganj to the Summary Martial Law Court No. 25 Dhaka and also filed copy of the illegal order of the Summary Martial Law Court No. 25 to the effect that he (defendant No. 1 A.K. Murshed) is not tenant under the plaintiff, that SCC Suit No. 5/70 is dismissed and that the plaintiff and others be evicted from the suit land and that the suit land is distributed to defendant No. 1 A.K. Murshed, one Mir Sayed Ali and the Government of Bangladesh (who are to be added as defendants 7 and 8 respectively in the plaint), that the Summary Martial Law Court No. 25 at Narayanganj was constituted for trial of certain offences and not for adjudication of civil suits involving right to property, that the Summary Martial Law Court had no jurisdiction to try the SCC Suit, that by virtue of order of the summary Military Court in disposing SCC suit illegally the plaintiff cannot be evicted or plaintiffs right, title and interest in the suit property cannot be affected. Nor can the suit property be distributed among defendant Nos. 1, 7 and 8, that the order of the Summary Military Court is void ab initio, without jurisdiction, malafide, baseless and has no legal effect or force and does not bind the plaintiff as the Summary Military Court exercises its power illegally and without jurisdiction and malafide with colourable use of power and without lawful authority and that in paragraph 21(b) it should be added that the prayer for a decree for eviction of the defendants from the suit premises through court demolishing the boundary walls if made during the pendency of the suit.

4. Defendant No. 1 A.K. Murshed filed an application under Order 7, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure stating that the suit is barred by the Martial Law Regulation No. 1/82, that the plaint is liable to be rejected, that all issues regarding C.S. plot No. 131 and 132 of of mouza Hajiganj P.S. Fatullah, District Narayanganj have been finally adjudicated upon and decided by Summary Martial Law Court No. 25 at Narayanganj, that the decree passed on 19.3.84 in Martial Law case No. 25/83 and 17/83 was duly confirmed by Zonal Martial Law Administrator, Zone-A, that the judgment and decree was passed by the Martial Law Court on 19.3.84 in presence of all the parties including the plaintiff after hearing the parties, that the said decree is binding on the plaintiff, that the said decree passed in the judgment by the Summary Martial Law Court was cxecuted on 19.4.84 and 20.4.84 through the Deputy Commissioner, that the plaintiff was evicted from the suit land in which he was in wrongful possession, that title of Mir Sayed Ali to .120 acre of land has been established, that .07 acre of land has been found to be Government khas land, that the suit is barred by the principle of res judicata, that the plaint is liable to be rejected for want of cause of action and that the attested photo copy of the judgment and decree of the photostat of the Summary Martial Law Court is attached to the application under Order 7 rule 11 C.P.C.

5. The learned Subordinate Judge, Narayanganj on 29.11.84 allowed the prayer of the plaintiff to amend the plaint but rejected the plaint under Order 7, rule 11 C.P.C. on the ground that the subject matter of the suit has already been decided by the Summary Martial Law Court No. 25 and confirmed by the Zonal Martial Law Administrator on 15.4.84 and that as Regulation No. 3(6) of Martial Law Regulation No. 1 of 1982 provides that no order, judgment, sentence or proceedings of a Martial Law Court shall be called in question in any manner whatsoever, by or before any Court including the Supreme Court, the court of the Subordinate Judge cannot question the legality or illegality of the judgment and decree passed by the Martial Law Court.

6. Against the said judgment of the Subordinate Judge, Narayanganj the plaintiff Meher Ali preferred Title Appeal No. 184/84 in the Court of the District Judge, Narayanganj before whom it was argued at the time of admission hearing on behalf of the appellant that by clause 2(3) of Martial Law Regulation No. I of 1982 the Chief Martial Law Administrator or an Officer authorised by him was empowered to transfer a case from a Martial Law Court or from a criminal court or from a civil court to a Martial Law Court, that the said Regulation No. 2 (3) of Martial Law Regulation No. 1/82 was published in the Gazette on 24th March, 1982, but by Martial Law Regulation No. III of 1982 the said Regulation No. 2(3) was substituted on 19th April, 1982 as follows:–

"The Chief Martial Law Administrator or Officer authorised by him in this behalf may transfer a case from one Martial Law Court to another Martial Law Court or from a criminal court to or a Special Tribunal or a Court of Special Judge to a Martial Law Court."

That the said subsequent amendment made on 19th April, 1982 was given retrospective effect from 24th March, 1982. The District Judge, Narayanganj however, summarily dismissed the appeal on 18.1.86 on the ground that in view of the provision of Regulation 3(6) of Martial Law Regulation No. 1 of 1982 the order of the Martial Court cannot be questioned by him.

7. Thereafter the plaintiff-petitioner Meher Ali obtained this rule against the said judgments of the Courts below.

8. The instant suit (being Title Suite No. 56/ 84) was filed by the plaintiff-petitioner in the court of the Subordinate Judge, Narayanganj on 10.4.84. Thereafter an application for amendment of the plaint was filed by the plaintiff-petitioner and the same was allowed by the learned Subordinate Judge on 30th April, 1984. Defendant No.1 opposite party A.K. Murshed Ali filed an application under Order 7, rule 11 C.P.C. stating that as all issues regarding C.S. plot Nos. 131 and 132 of Mouza Hajiganj, P.S. Fatullah have been finally decided and adjudicated upon by the Summary Martial Law Court No. 25, Narayanganj by the judgment and decree dated 19.3.84 in Martial Law Case Nos. 15/83 and 17/83 which was confirmed by the Zonal Martial Law Administrator on 15.4.84, the present suit is barred by res judicata, that the plaint is liable to be rejected for want of cause of action and that the plaint should be rejected as no Court including the Supreme Court has jurisdiction to call in question the judgments, orders and proceedings of any Martial Law Court in view of the provision of Regulation 3(6) of Martial Law Regulation No. I of 1982 (published in the Bangladesh Gazette, Extra-Ordinary, dated March, 24,1982) which reads as follows:—

"Regulation 3(6) of MLR No. I of 1982 No Order, judgment, sentence or proceedings of a Martial Law Court shall be called in question in any manner whatsoever in, by or before any Court, including the Supreme Court."

It has further been argued on behalf of the defendant opposite party before this court that by Act No. I of 1986 the Constitution (7th Amendment) Act, 1986 was enacted amending the Constitution inserting the following new paragraph 19(2) of the 4th Schedule to the Constitution:-"

All Orders made, Acts and things done, and actions and proceedings taken, or purported to have been done or taken, by the President or the Chief Martial Law Administrator or by any other person or authority during the said period in exercise or purported to exercise of the power derived from the said proclamation or from any other Proclamation, Chief Martial Law Administrator or, Martial Law Regulation, Martial Law Order, Martial Law Instruction, Ordinance or any other Law or in execution of order in compliance with any order made or sentence passed by any court, Tribunal or Authority during the said period, in exercise or purported exercise of the powers derived from the said Proclamation or from any other Proclamation, Proclamation Order, Chief Martial Law Administrator's Order, Martial Law Regulation, Martial Law Order, Martial Law Instruction, Ordinance or any other law or in execution of or in compliance with any Order made or sentence passed by any Court, Tribunal or Authority in exercise or purported exercise of such powers, shall be deemed to have been validly made, done or taken and shall not be called in question before any Court, Tribunal or Authority on any ground whatsoever."

9. The learned Subordinate Judge as trial Court rejected the plaint on 18.1.86 simply on the ground that the suit is barred by law, i.e. to say that the suit is barred by the provision of Regulation No. 3(6) of Martial Law Regulation No. 1 of 1982. The District Judge, Narayanganj as Appellate Court dismissed the appeal preferred by the plaintiff affirming the judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge.

10. On behalf of the defendant opposite party A.K. Murshed the judgment of the Summary Military Court No. 25, Narayanganj dated 19.3.84 photo copy of the said alleged judgment (without any authentication) was filed in the trial Court and the same reads as follows:—

"From the above findings it was proved that A.K. Murshed Ahmed was not the tenant of Meher Ali. Therefore, the Court is of the opinion that the adjudication of A.K. Murshed Ahmed as monthly ejectable tenant of Meherabi does not arise. Hence the Court unanimously decides to dismiss the S.C.C. suit No. 5/1970, T.S. No. 233/1980 and Misc. Case No. 19/81. The Court also decides to allow the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 216/81 and Orders for vacating the order of injunction passed in Title Suit No. 233/80.

2. Considering all these facts, the court unanimously decides that Meher Ali, Ful Chand, Rustam, Dil Mohammad and Ali Hossain be evicted from the disputed land (i.e. plot No.131 and 132) and the court also decides and orders that the distribution of the disputed land (i.e. plot Nos. 131 and 132 be recorded afresh in the following manner:-

a. A.K. Murshed Ahmed--- 0.26 decimals.

b. Mir Sayed Ali 0.10 decimals by possessional right and

c. rest of the disputed land i.e. .07 decimals should be recorded as Government khas lands."

It is allegedly signed by Major Md. Emran Hossain, Captain Mirza Md. Arshaful Haque and N/ Sub. Akbar Hossain. This is also allegedly con-firmed by K.M. Abdul Wahed, Major General, Zonal Martial Law Administrator on 15.4.84.

11. In Martial Law Regulation 2(3) of Martial Law Regulation No. I of 1982 published in the Bangladesh Gazette on March 24, 1982 it was provided by Lt. Gen. Hossain Mohammad Ershad, the Chief Martial Law Administrator and Commander-in-Chief as follows:—

"Regulation 2(3) of M.L.R. 1 of 1982.----The Chief Martial Law Administrator or an Officer authorised by him in this behalf may transfer a case from one Martial Law Court to another Martial Law Court or from a civil or criminal court or Special Tribunal to a Martial Law Court or from a Special Martial Law Tribunal to a Special Martial Law Court."

On April 19, 1982 the Chief Martial Law Administrator and Commander-in-Chief amended the above quoted Regulation 2(3) of M.L.R. No. I by Martial Law Regulation No. III of 1982 with retrospective effect from 24.3.82 substituting sub-Regulation 3 of the said Regulation 2 of MLR No. I as follows:—

"The Chief Martial Law Administrator or an Officer authorised by him in this behalf may transfer a case from one Martial Law Court to another Martial Law Court or from a criminal Court or a Special Tribunal or a court of Special Judge to a Martial Law Court."

<u>12. Thus it is clear that the Chief Martial Law Administrator who was the sole law making Authority during the continuance of Martial Law at that time was the sole law making authority and although by Martial Law Regulation No. I of 1982 promulgated on March 24, 1982 by Regulation 2(3) of M.L.R. No. I the Chief Martial Law Administrator or an Officer authorised by him in this behalf was empowered to transfer a case from a civil court to Martial Law Court; but the Chief Martial Law Administrator and the Commander-in-Chief by Martial Law Regulation No. III of 1982 amended the same with retrospective effect from 24.3.82 omitting the power to transfer a case from a civil court to a Martial Law Court it may be that even after such amendment the Chief Martial Law Administrator as the sole law making Authority perhaps could have himself transferred the S.C.C. Suit No. 5/70 of the 4th Court of Munsif, Narayanganj, Misc. Appeal No. 216/81 of the Court of District Judge, Dhaka (along with the records of Title Suit No. 233/80 of the Second Court of Munsif, Narayanganj and Misc. Case No. 19/81 arising out of Title Suit No. 233/80 Md. Meher Ali Vs. A.K. Murshed & others) to a Martial Law Court because the Chief Martial Law Administrator and the Commander-in-Chief making the proclamation of Martial Law on March 24, 1982 in paragraph C provided,</u>

"I may make, from time to time, Martial Law Regulations, Orders and Instructions among others;

(1) providing for setting up of Special Military Courts...... ;

(2) Prescribing penalties for an offence .... ;

(3) Empowering any Court or Tribunal to try and punish any offence.... ;

(4) Barring the jurisdiction of any Court or Tribunal from trying any offence as specified in such Martial Law Regulations or Orders; and

(5) on any other subject or in respect of any other matter including any subject or matter specified in or regulated by or provided in any other law.", as though that would be highly, discriminatory and openly questionable, partial, malafide and colourable exercise of power.

No other Subordinate Authority including any Military Officer of any rank had the power to act beyond the Proclamation of Martial Law, Martial Law Regulation, Orders and Instructions made by the Chief Martial Law Administrator and Commander-in-Chief. But in the present case in spite of the amendment by way of omission of power to transfer a case from a Civil Court to a Martial Law Court by Martial Law Regulation No. III dated April 19, 1982 with retrospective effect from March 24, 1982, Major General N.A. Chisty by Notification No. 142 dated 25th July, 1983 (published in the Bangladesh Gazette on July 26, 1983) passed the following order.—

"In exercise of the powers conferred by Regulation 2(3) of Martial Law Regulation, 1982 (Martial Law Regulation 1/82), I, Major General N.A. Chisty an Officer authorised by the Chief Martial Law Administrator in this behalf, do hereby transfer the cases mentioned in column I of the Schedule below pending in the courts shown in column 2 thereof to the Martial Law Court as specified in column 3 to the schedule;

SCHEDULE

I	II	III

Case

Courts where the cases are pending

Martial Law Courts to which the cases are transferred

5. 4th Munsif Court, Narayanganj S.C.C. 5 of 1970, Md. Meher Ali Vs. A.K. Murshed Ahmed. 	2nd Munsif Court, Narayanganj, Dhaka.

Summary Martial Law Court No. 25, Dhaka.

6. District Judge Court Dhaka, Misc. Appeal No. 216 of 1981. A.K. Murshed Ahmed Vs. Md. Meher Ali and oth-ers (along with the records of 2nd Munsif Court, Narayanganj, T.S. No. 233/1980 and Misc. Case No.19/1981 arising out of T.S. 233/ 1980 Md. Meher Ali Vs. A.K. Murshed Ahmed and others.) 	District and Sessions Judge, Dhaka.

Ditto

It is obvious that the said Notification No. 142 dated July 25, 1983 by Major General N.A. Chisty in exercise of power conferred by Regulation 2(3) of Martial Law Regulation No. I of 1982 was without jurisdiction, coram nonjudice, nullity and void ab initio because Martial Law Regulation 2(3) of Martial Law Regulation No. 1 of 1982 as it stood amended on the date of the said Notification No. 142 dated July 25, 1983, did not empower any subordinate Officer of the Chief Martial Law Administrator including Major General N.A. Chisty to transfer any civil case to any Military Court. That being the legal position, the judgment and order passed by the Summary Martial Law Court No. 25, Narayanganj on 19.3.84 and confirmed by Major General K.M. Abdul Wahed, Zonal Martial Law Administrator on 15.4.84 are without jurisdiction, coram non judice, without any lawful authority, nullity and void ab initio.

<u>13. In support of the above view a reference may be made to the case of Nasiruddin Vs. Government of Bangladesh and others, 32 DLR (AD) 216 wherein it was held in paragraph 10 as follows:—</u>

<u>"It is to be observed that when an authority is vested with jurisdiction to do a certain act and in the exercise of that jurisdiction he does it wrongfully or irregularly the action can be said to be done within the purported exercise of his jurisdiction. But an act which is manifestly without jurisdiction, such as the property which not being an abandoned property within the meaning of P.O. 16/72 is declared to be so, or in case of judicial or quasi-judicial act which is coram non judice, the use of the expression purported exercise in the validating clause of 5th Amendment of the Constitution cannot give such act the protection from challenge, it being ultra vires. It is true that malafide act is also notprotected, but then malafide act is to be pleaded with particulars constituting such malafide and established by cogent materials before the Court."</u>

<u>14. In this connection, the decision in the case of Khondker Ehteshamuddin Ahmed @ Iqbal vs. Bangladesh and others reported in 1981 BLD(AD) 107 =33 DLR(AD) 154 may be referred to wherein it was clearly held in paragraph 34 as follows:—</u>

<u>"Of course when a Martial Law Court or Tribunal has acted without jurisdiction or such court or Tribunal is not properly constituted, i.e. to say, is coram non judice, or has acted malafide, the power of the Superior Courts under Article 102 of the Constitution in an appropriate case may be exercised (the power exercised under Article 102 of the Constitution by the Superior Court is only an efficaious remedy which can always be exercised by the ordinary civil court.)."</u>

<u>15. Thus, as already stated, the Notification No. 142 dated July 25, 1983 made by Major-General N.A. Chisty was coram non judice, a nullity and void ab initio because of the amendment of M.L.R. No. I of 1982 by M.L.R. No. III of 1982 with retrospective effect from 24.3.82 omitting the power to transfer a case from a civil court to a Martial Law Court and consequently the aforesaid judgment and order passed by the Summary Military Court No. 25, Narayanganj on 19.3.84 and confirmed by Major General K.M. Abdul Wahed, Zonal Martial Law Administrator on 15.4.84 are without jurisdiction, Co-ram non judice without lawful authority, a nullity and void ab initio.</u>

16. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The judgment and order passed on 29.11.84 by Mr. Md. Anwarul Haque, Subordinate Judge, Narayanganj rejecting the plaint in T.S. No. 56 of 1984 under Order 7 rule 11(d) C.P.C. and the judgment and order passed on 18.1.86 by Mr. Md. Ibrahim Ali, District Judge, Narayanganj in Title Appeal No. 184 of 1984 dismissing the appeal summarily and upholding the aforesaid judgment and order passed by this Subordinate Judge on 29.11.84 in T.S. No. 56 of 1984 (Narayanganj) are set aside. The learned Subordinate Judge, Narayanganj is directed to dispose of T.S. No. 56 of 1984 in accordance with law as expeditiously as possible.

End.
